News.title: Cambridge Dictionary reveals word 2026 of the year amid rising AI fears
News.content:
Next

Cambridge Dictionary has officially named “Human” as its Word of the Year – as fears grow over rising AI use.

The word beat tough competition this year, winning over terms including “analogue”.

Defined as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have – as opposed to gods, animals or machines – “Human” has been given the top spot in the competition this year.



Colin McIntosh, chief editor of Cambridge Dictionary, said that the term was chosen over fears “about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking” to AI.



Other terms, including “human-made”, have also made their way into everyday conversation, as McIntosh said it has become increasingly difficult to distinguish human work from AI.

Commenting on the dictionary’s choice, Bill Gates said: “AI is making us think harder about what it means to be human.

“The measure of AI’s success should be how much it improves human lives,” he added.



Other terms in the running for Word of the Year included “agent” – which refers to an AI system that can operate without human control – as well as “wholesome” and “analogue”.

Popular social media terms have also made their way into the dictionary, such as “aura farming” and “looksmaxxing”.

The dictionary is also considering including “FOBO”, meaning fear of becoming obsolete, as concerns rise about AI replacing jobs.

This comes as “mogging” took the crown as Collins’ Word of the Year last month, having beaten the likes of “bixie”, a hairstyle shorter than a bob but longer than a pixie cut, and “fricy”, when a food is both fruity and spicy.



The “fast growing slang” term refers to outperforming or outshining something or someone.

News.title: Senior officer on nuclear armed submarine that spent record seven months underwater missed dad’s death and funeral
News.content:
Next

A SENIOR officer on the Royal Navy submarine that spent a record seven months at sea missed their father’s death and funeral as a result.

The personal tragedy underlined the extraordinary sacrifice submariners make.



It follows broken Government promises to maintain and replace Britain’s nuclear subs.

HMS Vengeance — a Vanguard-class sub designed for up to 80 days at sea — set sail in April and returned on Sunday after 217 days.



The 140 crew members are more cut off than astronauts with no way of contacting home.

The father died aged 72 in the summer but the officer was only informed hours before the sub sailed into the Clyde.



It is Navy policy to withhold bad news in case it prevents sailors from conducting their mission.

A source said: “This shows the sacrifice these deterrent crews make, especially with these longer patrols.



“Tragedy doesn’t respect rank.”

Sailors are allowed a text a week from home — read by the captain to weed out bad news. The captain’s messages are read by a comrade.

Anyone facing bad news is summoned to the captain’s cabin on the penultimate day of patrol.

Sailors are unable to send messages home for fear of revealing the sub’s location.

And there is almost no way of getting off early – unless a sailor’s life is in danger – for fear of breaking the continuous at-sea deterrent.



There is always one nuclear-armed submarine patrolling beneath the waves to fire in the event of a nuclear war.

News.title: Putin orders secret lovechild, 23, to change her name and claim his dead crony is her actual father
News.content:
VLAD'S DECEIT Putin orders secret lovechild, 23, to change her name and claim his dead crony is her actual father







Next

VLADIMIR Putin ordered his secret lovechild to change her name to make it appear she was the daughter of his dead crony.

Bombshell leaked records reveal Luiza Rozova, 23, officially adopted the name of one of the Kremlin tyrant’s closest allies just weeks after her parentage was exposed.



The glamorous 23-year-old, who now lives in Paris, was previously registered as Elizaveta Vladimirovna Rozova – with her middle name pointing to a father called Vladimir.

But she is now officially known as Elizaveta Olegovna Rudnova, suggesting her dad was instead Oleg Rudnov, a trusted Putin confidant who died in 2015.



The secret switch was made in December 2020, just a month after journalists exposed her alleged links to the Russian dictator.

And newly leaked Russian civil registry records have now confirmed the change was officially registered, rather than being just a cover identity.

Investigative journalist Andrey Zakharov, who helped expose Luiza’s alleged parentage, claims she was instructed to adopt the new name to hide her ties to Putin.

He said: “She did this – or, more precisely, was told to do it – exactly one month after our investigation for Proekt [news outlet] was published [in November 2020].

“Media executive Oleg Rudnov, whose name was given to Luiza, was a longtime associate of Putin and one of his trusted confidants.

“For instance, he bought Putin’s ancestral family home in the Tver Region on his behalf.



“Rudnov was also among those who showered Svetlana Krivonogikh – Luiza’s mother and Putin’s mistress – with expensive gifts.

“Specifically, he gave her an apartment near the Hermitage [world famous art museum housed in the Winter Palace of the Romanov Tsars in St Petersburg].”

Zakharov believes the name change was designed “as an official narrative to discredit our investigation”.



He alleged Putin had effectively “registered his illegitimate daughter under the name and patronymic of a dead friend” to obscure their relationship.

The explosive discovery emerged after Zakharov examined a fresh leak from Russia’s civil registry database.

Documents reportedly show Luiza received her new identity papers in late December 2020.

Although reports emerged in 2024 that she possessed a passport under the Rudnova name, investigators had previously been unable to prove her original identity had been officially changed.

Both identities carry the same date of birth – March 3, 2003.



Luiza is widely believed to be the daughter of Putin and his alleged former mistress Svetlana Krivonogikh, 49.

The former cleaner reportedly went from scrubbing floors to amassing a staggering £75million fortune after becoming involved with the Russian strongman.

Her business interests include a stake in Bank Rossiya, which has close links to Putin’s inner circle.

She has also been linked to a St Petersburg nightclub known for its raunchy performances.



Investigators believe Svetlana met Putin during the 1990s before giving birth to Luiza while he was still married to Lyudmila Putina.

Rudnov, whose surname Luiza adopted, also played a key role in property deals involving women linked to Putin.

In 2006, he reportedly bought a luxury St Petersburg apartment that was later transferred to Svetlana.

Five years later, he registered a penthouse in Sochi that investigators believe was intended for Putin’s alleged partner, former Olympic gymnast Alina Kabaeva.



The tycoon died in Germany in 2015, five years before Luiza’s name was officially changed.

Luiza once flaunted her lavish lifestyle on Instagram, posing in designer clothes and working as a DJ in Russia.

But she abruptly vanished from social media in October 2021 before later resurfacing in Paris.

Zakharov previously said: “Something happened in October 2021 because she deleted her Instagram account and she is no [longer] public.”



“It looks like somebody told her: ‘Stop it’.”

She now reportedly works at two Paris art galleries associated with anti-war exhibitions.

Her presence has sparked controversy among Russian dissidents and Ukrainian artists who fled Putin’s brutal regime.

In shocking footage filmed on a Paris street, she was confronted by a Ukrainian journalist who accused Putin of killing his brother.



Dmytro Sviatnenko told her: “Three weeks ago, your father killed my brother.”

Luiza refused to discuss the allegations and objected to being filmed.

She has never publicly confirmed Putin is her father.

The Kremlin has also refused to acknowledge the alleged relationship.

When Proekt first exposed the claims in 2020, Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov insisted he had “never heard anything” about Svetlana.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Officially, the Russian president acknowledges only two daughters, Maria Vorontsova and Katerina Tikhonova, from his former marriage to Lyudmila.

But the latest leaked records have raised fresh questions about how far the Kremlin tyrant may have gone to conceal his alleged secret daughter.

News.title: Brussels could gain sweeping powers over Britain’s taxes if UK rejoins EU, bombshell report warns
News.content:
Next

REJOINING the EU will put billions of pounds of taxpayers’ cash under the control of rules made in Brussels, a report reveals.

Some 84 per cent of UK tax revenue would be constrained by EU legislation, according to Stay Out, a cross-party group set up to stop a Brexit betrayal.



Ministers would not be allowed to cut taxes on petrol and diesel beyond a certain rate, and duty-free shopping for travellers from Britain to the EU would be scrapped.

While Brussels would not have direct access to the cash, it would have a huge say over what the Government could do with it.



Stay Out chairman Oliver Lewis said Brits would also be forced to pay more for their energy bills as well as sending over £750million a week in total to the EU.

He said: “Rejoining the EU would hand Brussels a say over 84 per cent of the taxes families pay, with 27 foreign countries holding a veto over any change a British Chancellor wanted to make.

“Before Andy Burnham goes any further, he owes the public a straight answer about who would really be setting their taxes, and whether he is prepared to put VAT back on electricity bills to rejoin.”

Britain has used its Brexit freedoms to scrap VAT on household electricity bills and women’s sanitary products.

‘SAVINGS’ DOUBT By Tom Scotson ANDY Burnham last night faced scepticism after he claimed his EU deal will cut costs for supermarket shoppers. The PM justified unpicking Brexit because “if we can get the right deal, it can cut the costs of a weekly shop”. But Brexit-linked red tape on food is thought to have a negligible cost impact on customers. He also said his constituents in Makerfield would back a deal if it could slash food costs. But Reform’s Richard Tice said: “He’s wasting his time on this pointless project instead of fixing Britain’s actual problems.”

Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith said: “Our plan to cut taxes and simplify the UK’s over-complicated tax code would be nearly impossible with the EU setting minimum rates for VAT and fuel duty and the Luxembourg court able to overturn decisions made in Westminster.”

Stay Out said a quarter of revenue, £271billion, would be set directly by EU law.



This includes VAT and the duties on fuel, alcohol and tobacco.

The warning comes as Mr Burnham prepares for a UK-EU summit on Friday.

News.title: Incredible moment Putin’s beloved £3bn bridge to Crimea collapses after being blitzed over and over by Ukraine
News.content:
Next

THIS is the dramatic moment Putin’s beloved £3billion Crimea Bridge is blown up after relentless blitzes from Ukraine.

Incredible footage shows the moment the bridge explodes and topples over after a missile and drone onslaught.



An enormous fireball can be seen lighting up the night sky before a second blast collapses one of the bridge’s giant 745ft-wide arches.

The 11-mile crossing collapsed into the water after Ukraine pummelled it over and over again with a huge aerial assault.



It marks a humiliating blow for Putin who opened the bridge in 2018 – four years after his invasion of the peninsula.

The targeted strike formed part of an overnight operation that saw Ukraine unleash a record number of drones across Russia.

It blasted the vital Kerch bridge, which links Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky called the operation unprecedented on Tuesday.

He said the collapse came after a weekslong effort by Ukrainian forces to gradually wear down Russian air defences in the area.

They then bombarded the bridge with a powerful barrage of missiles and drones.



The collapse of the bridge has blocked the route for shipping between the Black Sea and Azov.

It is essential for moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to occupied Crimea and for supporting troops on the front line.

Zelensky said: “Palianytsia drones performed exceptionally well, striking the road section of the bridge, while Neptune missiles, Ruta drones, and FP-5 drones struck the railway section.



“Using Flamingo, our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds.”

The Ukrainian president added: “We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation – and every proposal has been met with loud rejection.

“Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region.

“We are restoring our infrastructure. But we are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began.”

The road bridge was completely cut off, but train traffic has since resumed across the parallel rail bridge.



The Kremlin claimed the bridge will be restored to be better than it was before.

Ukrainian war commentator Denys Kazanskyi said: “Under wartime conditions, it is practically impossible to repair the Crimean bridge.

“Floating cranes are needed, but in the current situation, they would not be able to operate and would be destroyed by drones, as shipping in that area is virtually paralysed.”

Russian pro-war sources were left outraged at the failure of air defences for the bridge – with 100 strikes on the crossing in 24 hours.

Kazanskyi said: “It was believed that the bridge was reliably protected. In reality, nothing worked.”



If the Crimean Bridge is fully disabled it will be a huge embarrassment for Putin as he flies to China for a meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

The crossing was seen as a key symbol of Putin’s illegal invasion of the territory in 2014 when he annexed Crimea.

Ukraine has attacked Crimea Bridge three times since the start of the war, with major strikes hitting in October 2022, July 2023 and June 2025.

As well as blasting the bridge, Kyiv launched thousands of drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles at Russia in a relentless 24-hour operation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to Russian figures, the overnight salvo saw the largest number of drones unleashed by Ukraine since the start of the war.



Defence secretary Wes Streeting said in Brussels that the bridge strike was another example of Ukrainian ingenuity and the country’s absolute determination to defend itself against Russian aggression.

News.title: Irishman facing 10-year prison sentence after alleged attack on $60m US military aircraft that left plane ‘destroyed’
News.content:
PLANE RAP Irishman facing 10-year prison sentence after alleged attack on $60m US military aircraft that left plane ‘destroyed’







Next

AN Irish national has been charged in New York by the United States Department of Justice with breaking into and destroying a $60million US military aircraft parked on the taxiway at Shannon Airport.

Daithi O’Corrain, also known as David Curran, is alleged to have targeted the C-130 Hercules plane after breaching the site’s security perimeter on the morning of April 11 2026.



Shannon Airport is a major transatlantic hub for US military troops and equipment.

The US Air National Guard plane is said to have been en route to another country on a US military assignment.



On reaching the aircraft, O’Corrain is claimed to have gained entry by breaking the lock on the rear crew door before barricading himself inside.

He is then alleged to have “proceeded to inflict severe damage to the interior of the aircraft”, including cutting wires and hydraulic lines, and destroying every gauge in the cockpit.

He is also said to have had with him capsules of a highly corrosive metal, known as gallium, which can eat through aluminium in minutes.

Several hours after entering the airport, O’Corrain was spotted as the flight crew returned to the aircraft to leave for their next destination and alerted airport security.

They then saw him escape out of a hatch in the aircraft’s roof and it is alleged “inflict substantial additional damage” to the plane’s exterior using an axe, “pouring unknown substances” and placing objects, including ball bearings, into the fuel tanks.



Gardai are said to have arrived a short time later and detained O’Corrain.

According to CNN, “Corrain is not in US custody”.

The US Department of Justice (DoJ) claims O’Corrain carried out the attack after months of planning and preparation.

It said in a statement: “The manner in which O’Corrain carried out his attack further demonstrated a detailed knowledge of, among other things, the layout of C-130H aircraft and how best to destroy critical components of the aircraft; which wires and components to cut and which not to cut, for his own personal safety; how to secure points of entry into the Aircraft, and what tools would be needed to do so; which chemicals, including gallium, could be used to corrode the aircraft’s primary material; and advanced knowledge that a US military C-130H aircraft would be located at Shannon Airport at the time of his attack.”

The DoJ added: “As a result of O’Corrain’s attack, the aircraft was effectively destroyed.



“The damage inflicted rendered the aircraft inoperable, and the aircraft, worth approximately 60 million dollars, will not return to active flight status.”

O’Corrain’s alleged attack followed a series of similar, though less serious, incidents carried out by others at Shannon Airport over the previous year.

The 48-year-old from Ireland is charged with destruction of government property, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.

US attorney Jamie McDonald for the Southern District of New York said: “These charges send a clear and powerful message that attacks on US military assets, and thus our national security, will not be tolerated.

“As alleged in the indictment, the defendant destroyed a valuable US military aircraft abroad and, in the process, posed a significant threat to others, including US service members, nearby.



“This indictment holds the defendant accountable for his serious crime and serves as a warning to others, wherever they may be, considering similar criminal activity.”

James C Barnacle Jr of the FBI New York field office said: “As alleged, Daithi O’Corrain carried out a deliberate, planned attack against a US military aircraft, causing tens of millions of dollars in damage and jeopardising critical military operations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This was not an act of spontaneous vandalism. The defendant allegedly spent months researching the aircraft, acquiring tools and materials, and preparing to maximize the destruction he could inflict.

“The FBI and our law enforcement partners will continue to pursue anyone who targets US military assets, regardless of where those attacks occur.”

News.title: Burnham’s Brexit babble lays bare his desperate bid to drag Britain back into EU at any cost
News.content:
PM’s EU babble







Next

IS Andy Burnham just making it up as he goes along, or being deliberately dishonest about Brexit?

Our loose-lipped PM was talking absolute rubbish when he suggested Britain leaving the EU was a factor in Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine.



It isn’t the first time he has spouted nonsense over our vote to quit the EU.

Last month, he said Russia meddled in the 2016 referendum — only to be slapped down by the security services.



Is babbling Burnham suggesting Putin would pull his troops out of Ukraine if Britain marched back into Brussels?

Or will he use any old drivel to support his dream of rejoining the EU?

At the Lord Mayor of London’s banquet on Monday, he served up the absurd claim that 17.4million Brits didn’t really vote for a proper Brexit.

Let’s keep it simple. They voted to take back control of our money, laws and borders.

That’s exactly what Boris Johnson’s deal delivered. Yet Burnham wants to surrender all of this in his “reset”.

He wants to open our doors for up to 100,000 young Europeans to live and work here, once again become a rule-taker on food regulations, and hand over billions for the privilege.



If we rejoined, 84 per cent of all tax revenue would fall under the power of EU officials and courts, duty-free shopping on holiday would be axed and our own ministers would be powerless to cut taxes on petrol and diesel.

Burnham forgets that Brexit freed Britain to lead the world in arming Ukraine while EU leaders sat paralysed over fear of losing cheap Russian gas.

In the next breath, Burnham lectured us that “we have to be more serious about growth”.

That takes some brass neck while his tax-and-spend Labour Government squeezes the life out of British businesses and wealth creators.

The only thing growing under Burnham is the bill for his Brexit betrayal — and hardworking Brits will have to pay it.



Crash & Milburn

ALAN Milburn’s long-awaited report into youth unemployment has thrown down a brutal challenge to the Government.

His ten-year plan suggests sensible ways to make it cheaper, simpler and less risky for firms to hire youngsters.

But he bluntly pinpoints the root cause of the crisis. It doesn’t make comfortable reading for Andy Burnham.

He says Labour’s hikes in employers’ National Insurance and the minimum wage, along with Angela Rayner’s Employment Rights Act, have scared off businesses from taking on junior staff.

And he warns the PM’s Brexit “reset” – letting EU under-30s flood the jobs market — could undermine the mission.



Milburn’s reforms will save just £200million a year by 2036, a drop in the ocean against a welfare bill hurtling towards £431billion.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But even this will crash and burn if the PM isn’t careful.

News.title: ‘Incredible man’, 42, tragically crushed to death by excavator after its mirrors were folded in as partner pays tribute
News.content:
‘TRULY LOVABLE' ‘Incredible man’, 42, tragically crushed to death by excavator after its mirrors were folded in as partner pays tribute







Next

MOVING tributes have poured on for an “incredible” man who was crushed to death by an excavator on a building site.

John Graveson, 42, was tragically killed by the Hyundai HW140 excavator on March 3, 2023, while working at a skip hire yard in Dukinfield, Manchester.



More than three years on, the company AMP NW Ltd has been found guilty of corporate manslaughter after a trial at Manchester Crown Court.

Owner Anthony Elston, 49, was convicted of a Section 2 Health and Safety at Work Act offence, while yard manager John Horan, 34, was convicted of a Section 7 offence under the same act.



Following his tragic death, John’s partner Shelly has now spoken about the “incredible man” she and his other loved ones had lost.

Shelly said: “As the legal process comes to an end, sadly our grief does not.

“John was an incredible man whose warmth and love left an indelible mark on everyone lucky enough to know him.

“He was a truly lovable, huggable soul who embraced life with a wide-open heart, finding his greatest purpose in the deep devotion he held for his daughter, his partner, his mum.

“Laughter, Love Island and music were the best medicine for a brilliant day. His presence was a source of comfort and light, making the void he leaves behind feel impossibly vast.

“John should never have gone to work and not turned home to his family, and this will be a devastating reality forever as his daughter reaches many milestones in his absence.



“Life is so much quieter without John in it. You are loved beyond any describing word with love from Manchester all the way up to Carlisle, to his mum and wider family.”

Greater Manchester Police said that on the morning of March 3, 2023, yard manager Horan, of The Crescent, Worsthorne, was operating a Hyundai HW140 excavator in the yard.

At the same time, John, who had worked at the site as a waste picker for about a year, was walking through the yard and moved alongside the excavator before continuing behind it.



As John passed behind the excavator, Horan placed the vehicle into reverse and began manoeuvring backwards.

Although the excavator’s reversing alarm was sounding and its blue warning lights were illuminated, Horan remained facing forwards and failed to see John behind the vehicle.

The excavator struck John and crushed him, causing catastrophic injuries from which he sadly died at the scene.

It was established that the excavator was fitted with a 360-degree camera system designed to provide the operator with full visibility while reversing, a court heard.

But at the time of the collision, the camera system was not activated and investigators also established that the vehicle’s side mirrors had been folded in.



The driver, Horan, reversed the excavator without making proper observations behind the vehicle, leading to the fatal crash.

Police say further enquiries, including extensive CCTV analysis from the weeks and days leading up to the incident, revealed a culture of unsafe working practices within the yard.

The footage showed that owner Elston, of Wicket Grove, Clifton, was present while these dangerous practices were taking place and these practices had become commonplace on site.

His failure to intervene or take effective action demonstrated a significant breakdown in the management of health and safety.

The investigation found safety controls, risk management measures and safe systems of work were inadequate and were not being consistently enforced prior to John’s death.



Sentencing for John Horan, Anthony Elston, and the company AMP NW Ltd (now known as Waste Solutions Mcr Ltd) is scheduled to take place on Thursday, 4 February 2027 at Manchester Crown Court.

Detective Chief Inspector David Moores from GMP’s Serious Crime Division said: “John Graveson went to work on 3 March 2023 expecting to return home to his family at the end of the day. Tragically, he never did.

“This was not the result of an unforeseeable accident. Our investigation uncovered an alarming pattern of unsafe working practices that had become normalised on site.

“The risks were obvious, persistent and entirely preventable. Case law tells us that, for corporate manslaughter to be proven, failings must be exceptionally serious.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“These were failings of the most serious nature. The evidence showed that management were fully aware of the risks present on site, yet failed to take the action needed to protect their workforce.



“Our thoughts remain with John’s family, who have shown immense dignity and resilience throughout this process. While no conviction can undo their loss, we hope this outcome serves as a stark reminder that employers who fail in their duty to protect their workforce will be held accountable.”

News.title: Nearly half of Trussell Trust food banks warn supplies are 'critically low' as they brace for winter
News.content:
Nearly half of Trussell Trust food banks warn supplies are 'critically low' as they brace for winter

Almost half of food banks (46%) run by Trussell said preparing for winter feels harder than in previous years, amid falling donations, rising operating costs and persistently high levels of need

View 2 Images More than four in 10 (43%) described their food donation levels as 'critical' ahead of winter (Image: WalesOnline/ Rob Browne)

Nearly half of Trussell Trust food banks report critically low supplies as they brace to provide one emergency food parcel every 12 seconds this winter.

‌



‌



Almost half of food banks (46%) run by the anti-poverty charity said preparing for winter feels harder than in previous years, amid falling donations, rising operating costs and persistently high levels of need. More than four in 10 (43%) described their food donation levels as "critical" ahead of the cold months. The Trussell Trust expects to provide more than 600,000 emergency food parcels this winter - equivalent to one every 12 seconds.

‌



Food donations were 40% lower last winter than during the same period in winter 2022, marking a sustained decline in donations. It means staff are increasingly having to buy food to ensure people can continue accessing emergency support, creating a growing financial challenge at a time when costs remain high and inflation is rising, the charity says.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Should the Budget have done more to help with the cost of living? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

Andy Burnham defends emergency kit list and gives verdict on stockpiling wine READ MORE :

View 2 Images Actor Bill Nighy urged people to donate to Trussell's campaign (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images for The British Museum Ball 2026)

The Trussell Trust said the gap between food bank need and donations has widened since the start of the cost of living crisis. Last year, food banks purchased a quarter (25%) of the food needed to support people - compared to 6% in 2021, according to analysis by the charity . The Trussell Trust said the pressures affecting families, such as higher energy and food costs, are also making food banks more challenging to operate.

‌



Sarah Adams, food bank manager at Chichester & District Foodbank, said running their food bank - including the cost of keeping the lights on - is becoming more expensive. She said: "It's not right that anyone in the South East doesn't have enough money to live on. Every week, our wonderful staff and volunteers provide a lifeline through emergency food parcels and practical support to everyone who needs it.

"We're really worried about winter. At our food bank, need is already up 13% on the last year – and that's before the colder months draw in. We are doing everything we can to support people in our communities, but the rising cost of food and energy will make it even harder for us to keep services running. Keeping the lights on and spaces open costs money, which is why any support you can give, whether that’s donating food or funds, will make a real difference."

‌



She continued: "This is probably the hardest winter we've ever seen. It's the first year we've ever had to buy food in November. Usually we buy a bit in the summer then the harvest and Christmas donations see us through. But we're already running out of things. We ran out of toilet roll yesterday. Donations are down 22% this year to date."

She said when she started seven years ago, the food bank was only buying 2% of its food. This figure is now at 12% and is expected to surge by the end of the year. Ms Adams added: "It's frightening. The money we're spending on food means money not spend on other services. In addition to food, we offer a lot of signposting and referral work. We also offer things like a hot meal for older people and activities for them.

‌



"It's tight this year. We could do with another staff member. There is nothing we can cut. We have to put the heating on, the lighting on. None of these are choices."

‌



The Trussell Trust's co-chief executive, Emma Revie, says: “Food banks continue to see people forced to skip meals, go without heating and sitting in the dark because they can't afford the essentials like toiletries, rent and household bills. A food bank recently reported hearing from people who put on coats and get into bed to keep warm because they cannot afford to heat their homes.

"One person who turned to a food bank described having less than £1 in their bank account and no food in the cupboards. This isn't right. Our food banks are a lifeline to people facing hunger and hardship across our communities - but they shouldn't have to exist in the first place. People's shelves are empty, so food banks can't be. We are encouraging anyone who is able to, to donate food or funds this winter."

‌



The Trussell Trust is encouraging anyone who can to donate directly to their local food bank or support The Trussell Trust's winter appeal. People can also support by donating food through the Tesco Winter Food Collection from 26-28 November. The charity is also urging people to visit their local food bank’s website to check which items are most needed right now.

Actor Bill Nighy urged people to donate to the campaign, telling The Mirror: "Unbelievably it seems to me in 2026 in Great Britain thousands upon thousands upon thousands of people are finding it more and more difficult, if not impossible, to feed their families, or warm their homes, or provide the basic requirements for a normal life. Decent people not lazy or careless. Hard-working people, sometimes with more than one job, who still, in the modern world, can't earn enough money to provide for their families. Winter makes all of this much worse. Christmas makes it sadder."

Article continues below

Survey data comes from Trussell’s Annual Food Bank Survey, which polled 168 food banks between September 3 and October 4 Oct 2026.

News.title: NHS staff warned ‘Don’t let curiosity kill your career’ over snooping on records
News.content:
NHS staff warned ‘Don’t let curiosity kill your career’ over snooping on records

After high-profile cases of patient records being wrongly accessed, the NHS has sought to educate employees with campaign highlighting the serious consequences of snooping

View 3 Images NHS England’s boss wrote to trusts earlier in the year year sharing details of the campaign launched this summer (Image: PA)

NHS staff have been warned against snooping on medical records – with a “Don’t let curiosity kill your career” campaign.

‌



‌



After high-profile cases of patient records being wrongly accessed, the NHS has sought to educate employees. NHS England’s boss wrote to trusts earlier in the year year sharing details of the campaign launched this summer.

‌



We today report troubling figures which reveal nearly 3,000 incidents of staff inappropriately accessing medical records have been logged by the NHS in recent years.

‌



To see more of the stories you value from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images In his letter in early July, NHS chief executive officer Sir Jim Mackey highlighted the 'lasting damage caused to public trust' breaches caused (Image: PA)

Thousands of incidents recorded of NHS staff wrongly accessing medical records READ MORE :

The stats come as last month it emerged two more NHS staff were under investigation for allegedly inappropriately accessing the medical records of Southport stabbing victims. It came after the University Hospitals of Liverpool Group in May said almost 50 staff had wrongly looked at victims' medical files.

‌



Meanwhile, another trust said last month a total of 15 NHS staff have been sacked for accessing medical records of victims of the 2023 Nottingham attack. In his letter in early July, NHS chief executive officer Sir Jim Mackey highlighted the “lasting damage caused to public trust” breaches caused.

He wrote: “Patients using NHS services rightly expect their information to be kept secure by the people who treat them. This is why recent reports in the media of staff accessing patient information in unauthorised circumstances are particularly worrying for us all.

‌



View 3 Images NHS England boss Sir Jim Mackey wrote: '...a small minority of individuals undermine the trust that patients place in them and cause unnecessary distress and harm by accessing records without legitimate reason.' (Image: PA)

“These instances may seem like benign curiosity to some, but that couldn’t be further from the truth – they are harmful to patients, damage trust and, ultimately, are illegal. The majority of NHS staff handle patient information responsibly and professionally every day. However, a small minority of individuals undermine the trust that patients place in them and cause unnecessary distress and harm by accessing records without legitimate reason.”

‌



The NHS boss stressed that “accessing patient information for personal reasons isn't just harmless curiosity”. His letter detailed that new guidance was being issued to staff, with a new campaign helping educate employees.

He wrote: “Making this messaging as visible as possible through posters and screensavers will support our efforts to ensure patients have the highest levels of confidence in the NHS.”

Article continues below

A campaign image shows a picture of a cat, with the message: “Don’t let curiosity kill your career”. It also adds: "Accessing patient records for curiosity or personal reasons causes harm, is unlawful and could end your career.”

News.title: NHS staff inappropriately accessed medical records nearly 3,000 times
News.content:
NHS staff inappropriately accessed medical records nearly 3,000 times

The data, from NHS trusts, covers a period that has seen high-profile cases – including Southport and Nottingham attack victims’ records being snooped on

View 3 Images Nearly 80 trusts provided precise stats for incidents of staff inappropriately accessing patient records between 2021/22 and 2025/26, totally nearly 3,000 (Image: PA)

Nearly 3,000 incidents of staff inappropriately accessing medical records have been logged by the NHS in recent years, troubling figures reveal.

‌



‌



The cases – recorded by trusts in England – “erode trust”, a patient group warned. The data covers a period that has seen high-profile snooping cases, including employees looking at Southport and Nottingham attack victims’ records.

‌



Patients Association chief executive Rachel Power said: "Cases like these erode trust, not only in the trust involved but in the wider NHS. Lack of transparency deepens that damage, especially in the context of previous data breaches and leaks.

‌



To see more of the stories you value from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images The findings are based on Freedom of Information requests submitted to 143 acute hospital and ambulance trusts in England (Image: Dominic Lipinski/Press Association)

Brits urged to check on elderly as first cold weather health alert of the season issued READ MORE :

"Patients need confidence that strong safeguards are in place, that inappropriate access will be detected and acted on without delay, and that they will be the first to know, not the last, when their confidentiality has been breached."

‌



The findings are based on Freedom of Information requests submitted to 143 acute hospital and ambulance trusts in England. Almost 80 trusts provided precise stats for incidents of staff inappropriately accessing patient records between 2021/22 and 2025/26, totally nearly 3,000.

Some trusts said the figures included staff accessing their own records. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital, King’s Lynn and Milton Keynes University Hospital (MKUH) both said the majority of incidents at their trusts involved staff looking at their own records.

‌



View 3 Images Patients Association chief executive Rachel Power said: 'Cases like these erode trust, not only in the trust involved but in the wider NHS.' (Image: PA)

But the NHS’s website warns: “Even if the record is your own, or a family member or friend has asked you to look at their record, you must not use your staff access to view it, unless this is part of an authorised work role and local process. You may see information that would not otherwise be disclosed to you or the person whose record it is, including information that may cause you harm, or which is about another person and which is confidential. “

‌



Trusts must report breaches that could pose a risk to a patient's rights to data protection regulator the Information Commissioner's Office within 72 hours. Of those providing precise data, University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay had the highest number of incidents across the period 2021/22 to 2025/26, at 242.

Last month it emerged two more NHS staff were under investigation for allegedly inappropriately accessing the medical records of Southport stabbing victims. It came after the University Hospitals of Liverpool Group in May said almost 50 staff had wrongly looked at victims' medical files. Meanwhile, another trust said that 15 NHS staff were sacked for accessing medical records of victims of the 2023 Nottingham attack.

‌



Ten NHS staff were removed from duty or suspended after a data breach involving the medical records of Noah Woods, it emerged in September. The three-year-old’s body was found in a Suffolk village that month after the child had gone missing. Meanwhile, last month Yorkshire Ambulance Service said the medical records of a man killed by a tiger at a wildlife park may have been accessed “without a legitimate reason”. William Chapman, 24, was killed at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster last month.

Anna Telfer, chief nursing officer at Morecambe Bay, said the trust has a "zero-tolerance approach" to breaches. She said: “Such breaches can have a significant impact on patients and their families, undermining their confidence and trust in the care they receive, and are wholly inexcusable. All NHS employees have a professional and legal duty to access patient records only when necessary for their role. We have robust systems in place to monitor access to electronic records, investigate concerns and act on any breaches.”

‌



Zoe Baxter, director of people and culture at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, King’s Lynn, said: “All but one of the 107 cases of inappropriate access recorded between 2024 and 2026 related to members of staff accessing their own records. The remaining case, which involved a patient’s medical record being inappropriately accessed, was investigated and reported to the Information Commissioner’s Office.

“We take issues such as this extremely seriously. Our staff are regularly reminded that patient records must only be accessed where there is a legitimate reason to do so. Accessing records out of curiosity or for personal reasons is unlawful, and any concerns are investigated in line with national guidance and disciplinary procedures.”

‌



Kate Jarman, MKUH chief patient and public services officer, said: “The high number of incidents is a reflection of our strong, proactive monitoring, and commitment to investigating potential breaches of confidentiality. Through rigorous daily auditing, we are able to detect concerns that might otherwise go unnoticed and take prompt action where inappropriate access is identified. Protecting patient confidentiality is a fundamental responsibility for everyone who works at MKUH, and where staff are found to have accessed records inappropriately, action is always taken in line with trust policies.”

Matthew Hopkins, acute and ambulance network director at the NHS Alliance, said: "NHS staff work hard every day to protect confidential patient information and any misuse of records is a serious breach of trust… Maintaining public confidence in the use of patient data is crucial."

Article continues below

Sir Jim Mackey, NHS chief executive, said: “These figures are extremely worrying and it's completely unacceptable that any staff would risk betraying patient confidentiality in this way and causing harm to families in our care. The NHS will not tolerate this behaviour – whether being done out of curiosity or to see their own notes or results, accessing a health record without a legitimate professional reason is never acceptable and is unlawful.

“It is right that trusts are now proactively identifying and investigating this abhorrent behaviour – and our new guidance makes it crystal clear that staff face immediate suspension, as well as dismissal, if they are found to have accessed confidential patient information without an authorised reason.”

News.title: American soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia handed over to US military
News.content:
American soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia handed over to US military

A US Army officer arrested in Gloucestershire on suspicion of spying for Russia has been taken into US military custody - the serviceman has been named in reports as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner

View 2 Images The US Army officer was reportedly based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire (file image) (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

A US Army officer who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia has been handed over to the US military.

‌



‌



Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Carroll Tyner has been named in reports as the serviceman. He was reportedly based at Imjin Barracks near Innsworth in Gloucestershire, which is home to the headquarters of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps.

‌



The 41-year-old was arrested in Gloucestershire last Tuesday by counter-terror police. The Metropolitan Police confirmed today (Tuesday) that the US serviceman arrested last week has been "taken into custody by the US military over suspected national security and espionage allegations".

‌



Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) worked closely with US authorities, including the US military and the FBI, during the investigation, the Met said.

View 2 Images The entrance to Imjin Barracks (file image) (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and find them easily on Google, make us your preferred source. It's free and easy to do - just click here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of CTP, said: "Following an extensive investigation, CTP presented our case to the CPS, who in turn engaged with the Attorney General’s Office and American partners.

"Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them to progress. This decision was made in line with existing international protocols."

‌



The officer was detained last week on suspicion of offences under sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act 2023, which cover obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service. Police said the country to which the allegations relate is Russia.

FBI director Kash Patel previously said the arrest involved "allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies". He said it was the result of close cooperation between US and UK authorities, including MI5.

‌



US Brigadier General Sean Stinchon hailed the operation as a "great example" of transatlantic partnership.

He said: "This case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the constitution.

Article continues below

"Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served."

A Kremlin spokesperson has denied that Russia has any links to the US officer.

News.title: Alan Milburn warns blueprint to tackle Neets crisis won't be 'pain-free' with some to lose support
News.content:
Alan Milburn warns blueprint to tackle Neets crisis won't be 'pain-free' with some to lose support

In his long-awaited report - spanning over 270 pages - the ex-Labour Cabinet minister Alan Milburn proposed a controversial welfare state shake-up for under-25s

View 4 Images The ex-Labour Cabinet minister proposed a controversial welfare state shake-up for under-25s (Image: Stefan Rousseau/Press Association)

Alan Milburn has warned his blueprint to tackle Britain’s ‘Neets’ crisis will not be “pain-free” with some young people set to lose financial support.

‌



‌



In his long-awaited report - spanning over 270 pages - the ex-Labour Cabinet minister proposed a controversial welfare state shake-up for under-25s. It is combined with a multi-billion pound boost in support schemes to help the almost one million young people between the ages of 16 and 24 back into employment, education, or training.

‌



Mr Milburn, who addressed Andy Burnham’s Cabinet on Tuesday with his findings, recommends an initial £500million cash injection in the 2027 spending review. By 2036-2037 he said this should rise to a £5.8billion annual boost to help over 440,000 youngsters back into work.

‌



His 10-year plan to radically reduce the UK's 'Neet' rate includes a first of its kind legal guarantee for young people to offer work or training and a duty on government to deliver. His proposal will be made possible by annual welfare savings of £3.6billion and £2.4billion in extra tax revenues from people in work.

But among the most contentious and politically thorny proposals, Mr Milburn proposes an entirely new and different benefits system for under-25s.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 4 Images Andy Burnham told Sky News the Milburn report was a 'watershed' moment (Image: Sky News)

His report argues the “best reform option is one that has never been tried before - the creation of a new and different system for young people from the one that serves older adults”.

‌



It involves a new “youth allowance” replacing the health element of Universal Credit (UC) and the personal independence payment (PIP) for 16 to 24-year-olds. Under the new system, the report says those with conditions such as anxiety, ADHD and autism "would be both expected and enabled to work".

But there will be a new and more financially generous “severe and complex needs” insurance scheme for the minority of young people where it is clear they will likely never be able to work, the report states.

‌



His report - published on Tuesday - is frank, adding: “These changes will not be easy to make. Nor will they be pain-free. They could mean some people get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.

“But the approach I have taken is to try to define what would give young people the best chance of building a good life, not just over a year or two but over the course of their lifetimes.”

‌



Launching his report at a press conference at Google’s offices in central London, Mr Milburn said: “Britain is at risk of losing a generation of young people, not because they lack talent, not because they lack ambition, not because they do not want to work. This is not a crisis of aspiration, it is a crisis of opportunity.”

He said “half measures will not do” because “the scale of the problem is just too big for that”.

‌



“We have reached a profound moment of choice for the country, it calls for a new approach to back the next generation, to make young people a top priority. This is not what we have been doing.”

Mr Burnham described the publication of the report as a “watershed moment”.

‌



He said: “I said to the cabinet this morning, I don't think a British Cabinet has sat around that table in 50 years or more and talked about a vision for young people, support from the very early years all the way through school and then into opportunity beyond school.”

But pressed on whether he was going to cut benefits for young people, the Prime Minister told Sky News: “I don't want anybody to lose out here. This is not about punishing anybody. It's about saving money because young people are moving from education, training and into work and there's no need for anybody to miss out.

‌



He insisted he would make the argument for reform with Labour backbenchers, telling Sky News: “Things are tough if you make changes on this scale. But I'm saying to you today, I've been in politics a long time. I have never in my years in politics seen a wholesale, whole government approach to supporting the next generation.

“That is what this represents, and I am absolutely confident that I can take this vision and get people behind it, indeed get the country behind it, because we will not place Britain in the position I want it to be in. If we have a generation of young people growing up without hope for the future.”

‌



Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden told MPs that Mr Burnham's Cabinet has endorsed the need for a whole new settlement for young people. MPs will get a vote on government plans next year, with a white paper due to be published once ministers have considered the whole report.

It will be combined with a response to the upcoming Timms review on the main disability - Personal Independence Payments (PIP). The DWP minister Sir Stephen Timms was tasked with the review after Keir Starmer was forced to abandon his botched welfare reforms in 2025. Mr McFadden said the government rejects attempts to label young people as "snowflakes and shirkers".

‌



View 4 Images Neets review author Alan Milburn heading into Downing Street to brief Andy Burnham's Cabinet on his findings (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

He said: "We reject that entirely. The fault does not lay with the young people themselves. They want to work. They want to learn. It is for us to make sure that they have a chance to do so.

‌



"So our message to young people, the message from me, from the Prime Minister, from the whole cabinet, is that we value you, we believe in you, and we want you to have a future.”

The government proposals set the stage for one of the first major tests of Mr Burnham’s premiership. Some left-wing MPs have already expressed concern, including Jeremy Corbyn’s former Shadow Chancellor, John McDonnell.

‌



He said: “The receipt of Pip and universal credit health elements keeps 120,000 young people out of poverty. So the question does remain: why is it that young people, if benefit cuts go ahead, are forced to pay for the new system and we’re not taxing wealth?”

Mr McFadden responded in the Commons: “We are putting forward this new settlement because we believe it is a better deal for young people Let’s get the support to the young people so that they have the experience of earning, of making their way, and that’s what this settlement offers.”

‌



But some of the key rebels involved in the 2025 welfare rebellion now serve in Mr Burnham’s Cabinet, including Louise Haigh, who is now the Prime Minister’s second-in-command.

Labour MP Dr Marie Tidball, who was close to tears during last year’s rebellion in a powerful Commons intervention, said she welcomed the “significant shift in the government’s approach to welfare and employment support and the reforms set out in the Milburn review”.

‌



She added: “I am pleased there won’t be crude cuts to benefits." Dr Tidball also vowed to continue speaking for disabled people’s organisations “as I have done since I was elected”.

‌



Appearing on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, Mr Milburn also insisted the package of proposals was not about “crude cuts” to the benefits bill.

Pressed on whether some young people might get more help from the state into work while losing a lot of money, he responded: “Overall, you’re absolutely right, the benefits bill will fall.

‌



“And the amount of money we’re putting into employment support will rise to enable more young people into work. At the moment for every £25 we’re spending on income support, on benefits for young people, we’re only spending £1 on employment support.”

He added: “Some people - I don’t deny this - some people will be worse off, initially. At the same time we’re putting in more money in kind, in support, in services, in opportunities, to enable young people to do what they want to do, which is to get a job.”

‌



The Resolution Foundation’s Ruth Curtice said the report rose to the challenge the country faces in providing enough education, employment, and training opportunities for young people.

But she added: “The proposed welfare reforms are likely to be the most contested aspect of this review even though they’ll play a relatively small role in tackling Britain’s NEET crisis.

‌



“The biggest winners may well be those already in work, while those with health conditions who struggle to work could lose out.

“The move away from a ‘left alone’ approach to welfare is welcome, though the overall benefit savings of £3.6 billion by 2036-37 that Milburn says his programme would achieve suggest that some young people – likely those whose health or disability prevents them from working – could be considerably worse off.”

‌



View 4 Images Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden told MPs that Mr Burnham's Cabinet has endorsed the need for a whole new settlement for young people (Image: House of Commons/AFP via Getty Images)

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation has previously estimated young people could lose out on about £50 a week if they are no longer entitled to claim the health element of Universal Credit (UC),

‌



And they could lose between £30 and £195 a week if they are also barred from the PIP disability benefit (Personal Independence Payment).

James Taylor, executive director of strategy at the disability equality charity, Scope, welcomed the “ambition to transform employment support for young people” but said they are “deeply concerned by proposals that could leave some young disabled people with less financial support”.

‌



He added: “PIP helps with the extra costs of disability, whether someone is in work or not. Taking that support away could make it harder, not easier, for young disabled people to get into work and live independently.

‌



“The Government must be ambitious about creating jobs and opportunities for young disabled people. But that ambition must not come at the cost of the vital financial support they need.”

George Bangham from the New Economics Foundation said: "There’s much to welcome in Alan Milburn’s review, including calls for more investment in employment support and a guarantee of a job, training or support for every young person. But the positives risk being overshadowed by his argument for cuts to health and disability benefits.

Article continues below

"There is little evidence that health benefits are too generous or that they are driving young people out of work, while cutting them is likely to push people into poverty and make it harder for them to find work.

“Cuts to benefits also don’t solve the fundamental problem that there aren’t enough opportunities for young people. Recent NEF research found that in Blackpool there are only five online vacancies for every 100 people out of work and on Universal Credit.”

News.title: Thomas Markle 'charged with child sex offences in Philippines'
News.content:
Thomas Markle 'charged with child sex offences in Philippines'

Philippine police have reportedly filed three charges against Thomas Markle Sr, 82, who is currently in police custody in the US after being charged with possession of child sexual abuse material

View 3 Images Thomas Markle Sr is currently being held in a US jail after authorities said he cut off his electronic tag from his ankle (Image: Pinellas County Sheriff's Office/Press Association)

Police in the Philippines have reportedly charged Thomas Markle Sr with possession of child sexual abuse material.

The Philippine National Police filed three charges against Markle Sr, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, on Monday, Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC.

The 82-year-old has reportedly been charged with two counts of offering, distributing, selling, exporting or importing any form of child sexual abuse or exploitation material (CSAEM) and one count of possession of CSAEM material, the BBC and ITV News report.

Earlier this month, Markle was arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The 82-year-old, who denies any wrongdoing, is currently being held in a US jail while awaiting a psychiatric evaluation ahead of a potential trial.

View 3 Images Markle Sr has previously denied the allegations against him (Image: Channel 5)

Markle was initially released on bail and placed under house arrest, but was detained last Tuesday after removing his electronic monitoring tag from his ankle, First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said.

He was first arrested by FBI agents on November 6 following searches of two Los Angeles storage units he had rented for nearly two decades. Agents seized around 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books which the FBI said contained suspected child sexual abuse material.

The investigation began after Markle's son and Meghan Markle's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, reported his father to police in the Philippines and the FBI in October. Markle Jr allegedly discovered illegal images in his father's belongings in Cebu City, where Markle Sr had been living until May.

Markle Jr also reportedly alerted authorities to the storage units in Los Angeles. Markle Sr has strongly denied the allegations made by his son, describing them as "sick lies".

View 3 Images Markle appeared at the Sean M Gibbons US Courthouse in Tampa, Florida, on November 6 (Image: Getty Images)

Meghan Markle, who has been estranged from her father since 2018, said last month that she had been made aware of the "troubling and disturbing allegations" against him in 2018.

In a statement issued through her spokesperson, the Duchess of Sussex said: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.

"In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection [Rasp]. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.

"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.

"Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."

News.title: British Airways Dreamliner gets stuck in mud after veering off Heathrow Airport runway before take-off
