Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Taylor Hinds (Arsenal), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Poppy Pattinson (London City Lionesses), Leah Williamson (Arsenal)



Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Grace Clinton (Manchester City), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Ella Toone (Manchester United), Keira Walsh (Chelsea)



Forwards: Aggie Beever-Jones (Chelsea), Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Isobel Goodwin (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Beth Mead (Manchester City), Jess Park (Manchester United), Alessia Russo (Arsenal) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Wiegman, whose latest 25-player squad includes 10 players with fewer than 10 caps, watched from the stands at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday as Goodwin scored for London City Lionesses with a terrific finish against Arsenal. She said of the 23-year-old: “We always knew she’s a huge talent [with] a high potential. We’re watching a lot of games over periods of time, all the time, so we [had] kept an eye on her anyway, but I think it also helped that she had that great goal and a great performance last Sunday.

“She has some different qualities. She’s really fast too. She can head – she showed that also in attacking set plays and defending set plays also – and she can score goals. Does she need to step up to the next level? Absolutely. But you can tell that she’s improving.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wiegman was unable to call upon several injured players, including Lauren James and Alex Greenwood. She included Manchester United’s Ella Toone, who was initially left out of September’s squad before being recalled for the playoff against Greece. Wiegman said of Toone: “She has impressed us really well. She responded really well. And going back to [her] club, she’s done well too. And that’s what has been fed back to me too.”

Cox is rare in getting an England call-up while playing in the second-tier WSL2. The 20-year-old is on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea.

The Lionesses face Ukraine on neutral territory in Spain in the away leg on 1 December before playing them at Wembley four days later.

Sports.title: Melbourne Cup horse found dead in a skip: Racing world shocked after horrifying discovery - as bizarre explanation is issued for 'respectful burial' blunder
Sports.content:
Melbourne Cup horse found dead in a skip: Racing world shocked after horrifying discovery - as bizarre explanation is issued for 'respectful burial' blunder

The racing world has been left in shock after a Melbourne Cup horse who died after suffering severe colic was found in a skip – with the equine specialists who were unable to save the horse only able to offer a baffling explanation.

So You Are was found among the general waste at Cleanaway's Lucas Heights facility in Sydney after the five-year-old gelding died on Monday.

The horse had been rushed to REC Equine Specialists at Randwick for emergency surgery after being struck down with colic.

The specialists euthanised the horse after it became clear he could not be saved – but managing partner Dr Jonathan Lumsden could only apologise 'unreservedly' for what came to pass after his death.

'REC Equine Specialists extends its deepest sympathy to the owners, trainer and connections of So You Are, and apologises unreservedly for the distress caused by footage shared on social media today,' Lumsden told news.com.au.

'On Monday 16 November, So You Are was brought to our hospital for emergency treatment of severe colic. Despite the best efforts of our veterinary team, he could not be saved and was humanely euthanised under anaesthesia. After his death, So You Are was collected by our contracted service provider and taken to a licensed landfill. He should have been promptly and respectfully buried.

Racing NSW stewards are investigating whether a horse found in a skip bin at Lucas Heights was So You Are

So You Are underwent emergency treatment at a specialist equine hospital but could not be saved

'What happened was unacceptable and disrespectful to So You Are and to everyone who cared for him. We are deeply sorry. So You Are was in our care. We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that.

'We should have known exactly how horses were handled after leaving our hospital, and we did not. That process is not good enough, and it must change. We have spoken with So You Are's owners and trainer to apologise personally.

'We are working with our service provider and the facility operators, together with Racing NSW, to establish how this happened and to put in processes to ensure it never happens again.

'Effective immediately, we have stopped using this service provider, we are reviewing how the service providers we contract care for horses after death, from collection to final burial, and will share the findings with So You Are's connections and Racing NSW.

'No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week. We will make sure it does not happen again. Out of respect for So You Are and those who loved him, we ask that the footage not be shared further.'

Builder Gregg Jowett raised the alarm after discovering the horse's body on Monday and posting a video to Facebook.

'I'm at the tip. They've tipped a horse in the f***ing bin,' he said in the footage.

'You're f***ing kidding me. That can't be normal. Does anyone know if that's legal? I'm disgusted by that.'

Jowett said he was concerned about the body being left in a bin accessible to people dropping off everyday rubbish.

'I get it, they do dispose of horses at tips. However, I can't see how they can just tip them into the bins that are open to the public for general mixed rubbish,' he said.

'One would assume they would head straight to the tip edge.'

Jowett claimed staff told him 'this is normal' before asking his followers: 'Am I wrong? Felt disturbing to be honest but I am a city slicker.'

After learning of the footage, So You Are's trainer Bjorn Baker and the horse's connections shared a shocked statement.

'Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains,' Baker said in a statement on Tuesday. 'He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death.

'I understand the specialist hospital facility REC Equine Specialists are investigating the circumstances, and I expect a full explanation of what occurred.

'My thoughts remain with the Ramsey family, and with all my staff, for whom this has compounded an already devastating loss.'

Mr Baker initially told the Sydney Morning Herald that So You Are had quickly become a favourite among his staff.

'He was a kind, beautiful horse. We only had him for a short time and he became a stable favourite,' he said.

The Herald reported that unnamed sources familiar with the situation believed a brand visible in the footage matched So You Are.

Racing NSW stewards are making inquiries into the discovery and the footage has prompted distressed responses from viewers, including people who said they had spent years caring for horses.

Trainer Bjorn Baker described So You Are as a 'kind, beautiful horse' who quickly became a stable favourite

Baker added that the horse deserved to have been treated with 'dignity' after his death

According to the Herald, normal practice involves a contractor taking a deceased horse for burial at a licensed landfill. Its sources said euthanised horses require appropriate disposal because of the drugs remaining in their bodies.

The circumstances surrounding how So You Are's remains came to be in the bin, including who was responsible for its transport and handling, have not been established.

So You Are was trained at Warwick Farm and owned by prominent breeder Stuart Ramsey and his wife Trish.

He won four races during the spring, including three Group 3 events at Rosehill, Randwick and Bendigo, before lining up in Australia's biggest race.

After winning the Bendigo Cup a week before Flemington, he started the Melbourne Cup as a $12 chance under jockey Rachel King.

With about 600m remaining, he was running second and chasing leader Royal Supremacy before eventually finishing eighth behind Point of Law.

Thirteen days later, the stable announced his death.

'He had been enjoying a well-earned spell when he was found showing signs of colic this morning,' its initial statement said.

'He was rushed to a specialist equine hospital for emergency veterinary treatment, but sadly could not be saved.'

The Daily Mail has contacted REC Equine Specialists, Cleanaway and Turangga Farm for comment.

Sports.title: 'We felt like medieval peasants coming up against a king': Insiders relive the battle to rid Blackpool of the Oystons, from tangerines stuffed in knickers to a bright orange GTI - and why 'insider dealing' claims mean club isn't out of the woods yet
Sports.content:
'We felt like medieval peasants coming up against a king': Insiders relive the battle to rid Blackpool of the Oystons, from tangerines stuffed in knickers to a bright orange GTI - and why 'insider dealing' claims mean club isn't out of the woods yet

In the south London pub where they are readying themselves for a League One match with AFC Wimbledon, Blackpool fans who fought for their club’s heart and soul, 10 years ago, receive a message informing them that half the squad have gone down with a sickness bug so severe that the starting XI will be very unusual.

Three players are too ill to leave the team hotel, the goalkeeper selected is yet to feature in the league this season and the EFL don’t consider this predicament serious enough to cancel the game. The club are already on a run of five defeats in seven.

Moments like this reveal the Blackpool fanbase’s deep sense of perspective, born of their long and often wretched fight to kick out one of British football’s most detested owners, Owen Oyston.

‘We’re still here and we’re watching our club home and away,’ says Andy Higgins, chair of the Blackpool Supporters Trust. ‘We have a good relationship with the club,’ says his friend Dave Ragozzino, with Higgins in the Earlsfield pub. ‘The club are asking us to tell fans what’s going on, and they know we will help. Ten years ago, our club’s owners were suing us.’

The story of the campaign which brought these fans and many more together is told in a superb new documentary The Battle for Blackpool, which screens this week, capturing its spirit, imagination and intelligence.

Oyston and his son Karl have both cooperated with the documentary-makers. Oyston Snr, wearing dark shades and his trademark fedora, is interviewed at his stately home in the Forest of Bowland, while his son Karl, clearly still consumed with hate and contempt for fans, is filmed clay pigeon shooting across their estate.

Blackpool fans watch their team fall to another League One defeat, at AFC Wimbledon on Saturday

The Tangerines are just two points above the relegation zone having lost five out of their last seven league fixtures

Their supporters fought a long and wretched battle against the club's former owner Owen Oyston (pictured in 2017)

The film’s stars are the supporters who led the fight – Christine Seddon, Tim Fielding, Ragozzino, two fans in a Mk1 tangerine Golf GTI and twin sisters of advancing years who embraced the campaign’s guerilla tactics.

Oyston Jr, who chaired the club at his mother’s request after his father was jailed for rape in 1996, tells the documentary-makers: ‘My father likes football. I didn’t.’

It was after he’d stumbled on a managerial genius in Ian Holloway, who took the club into the Premier League for a season in 2010-11, that a full sense of the family’s greed and entitlement became clear.

The Mail on Sunday's Nick Harris revealed that Oyston Snr had paid himself £11million out of the Premier League jackpot, while critics say virtually all the club appeared to get out of promotion was a new sprinkler system. The fight against the Oystons took hold. The Blackpool Supporters Trust, then chaired by Fielding, was its strategic and political wing, flanked by the imaginative sabotage activities of the Tangerine Knights group.

A plot to smuggle tennis balls into the ground for a home match against Burnley, in April 2014, and collectively throw them on the pitch, provides one of the documentary’s many glorious sections. Fans stuffed the missiles into their pants, socks and bras.

‘I had them in my knickers,’ says Christine Atkinson, who is interviewed with her twin sister, Pauline O’Rourke. ‘I didn’t have tennis balls. I had tangerines. It was softer. Less uncomfortable!’

The family of Karl Oyston mocked the tennis ball protest on social media. But it was when his father began suing ordinary fans, some pensioners, for criticising him that the protest escalated.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr tells the film-makers.

‘I had tangerines in my knickers,’ says Pauline O'Rourke (right), who is interviewed with her twin sister, Christine Atkinson, in the documentary about Blackpool's fight to get rid of the owners

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr (pictured in 2010) tells the film-makers

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ says Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke, interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Koudellas inside the tangerine GTI, parked up on Blackpool’s South Shore – one of the film’s many wonderful touches.

Ragozzino lost his job and faced a £150,000 legal suit. Fielding, a solicitor, was told it would cost more than £250,000 to defend himself against Oyston’s legal action. The Oystons forced him to pay them £10,000 in cash and issue a public apology.

Karl Oyston reveals how much he revelled in the war with fans, delighting in the ‘Oyston Out’ personalised number plate his wife bought for Christmas to maintain the mockery. ‘She thought it was highly amusing. Which it was,’ he relates.

Suing elderly Blackpool fans was his father’s idea, he says. ‘But as soon as the board makes a decision, you fight to the death to support it.’

Oyston Snr maintains he was perfectly entitled to pay himself £11m of the Premier League money. ‘Why wouldn’t we? Why shouldn’t we?’ he asks. ‘We own the company. We’d had 25 years of pouring money down the drain without the least prospect of seeing any of it ever again.’

It was Fielding who came up with the game-changing strategy – persuading minority shareholder Valeri Belokon to mount a successful legal challenge against the Oystons, eventually clearing the way for Simon Sadler, a Hong Kong-based financier and Blackpudlian to buy the club.

It’s not been a bed of roses these past few years. An interim club board, formed after Oyston was ousted, included Ben Hatton, later chief operating officer at Aston Villa, former Inter Milan CEO Mike Bolingbroke and Fielding. But a succession of good leaders have left.

Brett Gerrity, a one-time close friend of Sadler who persuaded him to buy the club, resigned in 2023. The two no longer get on. Ben Mansford, respected ex-CEO at Leeds and Barnsley, also unexpectedly left. Former sporting director David Downes was recently made CEO. Amid these comings and goings, Sadler has not appointed a successful manager since Neil Critchley left to assist Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa in 2022.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ says Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke (right), interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Coudellas inside the tangerine GTI

Christine Seddon was a leading figure in the fight to rid Blackpool of the Oystons

None of this has affected fans’ views of Sadler, a boyhood Blackpool fan whose investment is still giving the club a top eight budget in League One. He has spent money on upgrades to the stadium and training ground and the team’s playing surface is excellent.

But his own future at Bloomfield Road is in doubt. He is on trial in Hong Kong over accusations of insider dealing linked to his former hedge fund and could face a prison sentence if convicted.

That would mean him failing the EFL Owners’ and Directors’ Test and he would seemingly have to sell. The verdict in that case is expected next February. Sadler, who has pleaded not guilty to the charges, has revealed little of any contingencies he might have made. He is thought to be prepared to sell the club, though only if the buyer will be a true custodian.

‘He’s acutely aware of not putting Blackpool right back where it was with Oyston,’ says one source.

‘The club is so much better and professional than it used to be,' Seddon tells us. ‘But we are short of football business experience. We don’t have a proper board at the moment.

'Hedge fund management – our owner’s world – does not always translate well into football. It’s a steep learning curve.’

Oyston Snr revealed in a recent interview that he wants to buy the club back and gift a majority share to fans. ‘In 2015, we suggested to him that he walk away and leave the club’s assets to the fans,’ says Seddon.

‘He ignored us, yet now he’s suggesting this. These are deluded ramblings. Simon Sadler would not give Oyston the time of day.’

'When I hear some fans complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?”'

Karl Oyston tells the documentary-makers that he has not spoken to his 92-year-old father since the family’s 32-year ownership of the club ended in 2019. Will he ever see him again, he is asked. ‘No. That ship’s sailed,’ he replies.

Blackpool, backed by a loud, strong away following, fell to a 1-0 defeat at Wimbledon and boss Ian Evatt’s job will be on the line when they face fellow-strugglers Wigan on Saturday, so the film is a particularly timely reminder of how far this club’s fans have come.

‘Yes, we want results to be better,’ Seddon says. ‘But when I hear some complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?” Our club became an opportunity for people who were dismantling it for their own benefit. There were times when we thought we would lose it altogether.

'But we’re now in a place where we were beginning to believe we would never be. We’re thankful for that.’

The Battle for Blackpool will premiere in the UK on November 21 on Sky Documentaries and streaming service NOW

Sports.title: Pedro Neto is sent off for two yellow cards in under two minutes before bizarre touchline clash with Craig Bellamy - as Portugal beat Wales with Bruno Fernandes on target
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Pedro Neto lost his cool while playing for Portugal in their win over Wales as he received two yellow cards in as many minutes before clashing with opposing manager Craig Bellamy.

The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.

He was first booked for a high challenge on the back of Brennan Johnson's leg – a tackle which some may argue could have been a red in itself.

One minute and 59 seconds later, he was shown his second yellow when he slid in on Johnson again. He didn't appear to make too much contact, if any, but left the Wales man sprawling to avoid it.

German referee Sven Jablonski showed no hesitation in sending Neto off, but the winger wasn't going to take it lying down.

He had to be held back by captain Bruno Fernandes as he tried to confront Johnson, and seemingly managed to shout in his direction before reluctantly making his way off the field.

Pedro Neto was sent off while playing for Portugal against Wales after two yellow cards in under two minutes

He also had a confrontation with Wales manager Craig Bellamy (right) as he left the field of play

Before that, though, he had a conversation with Wales boss Craig Bellamy, with officials initially trying to separate the two, with Neto looking angry.

Bellamy, though, spoke to Neto and embraced him before finally walking down the tunnel.

The 26-year-old will now serve a one-game suspension, meaning he will miss the first leg of Portugal's Nations League quarter-final, which will be played in March.

Jorge Jesus's side secured top spot in their group with the win over Wales, which was achieved by Carlos Forbs's 70th-minute goal.

Fernandes had opened the scoring for his side in the 11th minute, but David Brooks and Sorba Thomas gave Wales an unlikely lead.

That was until Neto levelled things up just before half-time, and Forbs scored the winner, with ten-man Portugal able to hold on for all three points.

Wales finished bottom of the group with one win – against Norway – and five defeats from their six matches.

Captain Ben Davies said after the game: 'We showed a lot of character and we've shown good effort in these games where we've just come up short from a results perspective.

After expressing his frustration, the Chelsea star had to be directed off the field by captain Bruno Fernandes (right)

He had in fact scored for his side in the game, bringing them level before the half-time interval

'There is a lot to take from this going into the games in March and we have to feel confident because we've been playing well.

'We know the boys up top can be so dangerous, and if teams want to come here and play man-for-man against us, we've got a lot of speed and we have to be good on the ball. That comes with risk sometimes, like you saw with the chances that they had, but I'd rather play this way and go toe-to-toe with these teams and have a go.

'We competed in the campaign and we were not a million miles off like the table might suggest. I thought we put in some very good performances, we just wished we had some better results.'

Neto, meanwhile, will now return to his club side Chelsea ahead of a busy Christmas period.

He has started all but one Premier League game so far and has been a key player under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues will take on Leeds at Stamford Bridge this weekend as club football returns.

Sports.title: I can understand why fans are frustrated about lack of progress under Pocognoli, admits Andy Robertson
Sports.content:
Andy Robertson says he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the new manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no issue with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he said. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap

‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he said. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the new players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he said. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11 players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’

Sports.title: Inside Wales' 'giddy' celebrations after historic win over the All Blacks - and the unseen Principality Stadium moment that summed up a day Welsh rugby will never forget
Sports.content:
On the wall of his home near Cwmbran, Taine Basham – one of Wales’ all-conquering New Zealand heroes – has a signed cover picture of The Stereophonics’ album Performance and Cocktails. On it, the Welsh band’s lead singer Kelly Jones has a personal message.

‘To Taine,’ Jones wrote, before using one of his most iconic lines, taken from the hit song I Wouldn't Believe Your Radio. ‘You can have it all if you like.’

On Saturday evening, fresh from ending his country’s 73-year wait for a victory over the All Blacks, Basham posted the image to his Instagram page. For one night only, after years of despair, Wales’ players and supporters really did feel like they have it all.

‘I Wouldn’t Believe Your Radio,’ is one of my favourite songs,’ Basham told Daily Mail Sport, less than 48 hours after what was one of the most famous results in Welsh rugby history. ‘Jamie Roberts, who I played with at the Dragons, knows Kelly well. I love my music and so does he, so he asked if he wanted Kelly to sign the picture for me.

‘After a few pints in Cardiff on Saturday night, I thought the lyrics went well with the result we’d had, so I posted it. I got a few new followers and likes from it!’

Like the rest of a proud rugby nation, Jones would probably have been shocked at what was one of the international game’s biggest ever upsets. By beating New Zealand 35-28 and sealing a first win over the great rugby nation since 1953, Basham and the rest of Steve Tandy’s squad sealed their place in history.

By beating New Zealand 35-28 and sealing a first win over the great rugby nation since 1953, Taine Basham (pictured) and the rest of Steve Tandy’s squad sealed their place in history

When replacement scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams kicked the ball dead to end the game, bizarrely it was caught in the stands by WRU chief executive Abi Tierney (left, with Basham)

Giddy with joy, Wales’ players celebrated their success in Cardiff sports bar Ludo, before heading to The Piano Works nightclub on St Mary Street – just yards from Principality Stadium, where history was created. ‘Some boys went out, some met their families, but by the time midnight came I was knackered and jumped in a taxi home,’ Basham said.

After playing his part in an heroic defensive rearguard, it was no surprise Basham felt a sense of tiredness. Surely, though, after sending a nation home in raptures, his fare was taken care of?

‘It probably cost me too much,’ Basham said. ‘The driver kept saying it would be £5 cheaper if I paid cash. He had no idea who I was! I was so tired I just wanted to get home, so I tapped my card. I crashed out when I got in, but woke up early. I was sore and then I had my kids jumping all over me.

'The last time I’d played against New Zealand four years ago, my phone was inundated and I didn’t reply to people. A few said I’d changed! This time, my phone blew up again, but I made sure to get back to everyone.’

When replacement scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams kicked the ball dead to end the game, an entire country started a party they could barely believe was happening. Daily Mail Sport has learned Morgan-Williams’ kick was caught successfully in the stands by none other than Welsh Rugby Union chief executive Abi Tierney. It summed up a day that anyone with Welsh blood will remember forever. Like Wales’ players, Tierney needed this result badly after two years or more of Wales struggling both on and off the field.

No one saw this result coming, least of all New Zealand. The New Zealand Herald's Gregor Paul had said pre-match Wales were ‘condemned to play the role of the Dickensian orphan, frequenting the soup kitchens and roaming the streets hoping for a penny to be put in their hat’. Kiwi television also poked fun at Wales’ decline. It said the WRU’s ‘groin-sniffing goat (mascot) is probably a greater threat to New Zealand than the Welsh.’ Another channel described the Wales match as the ‘easiest on our end-of-year-tour.’ Such confidence was misplaced.

The insults – particularly the description of Wales as ‘Dickensian orphans’ – were needless, however. It was humble pie all round for All Blacks fans on Monday morning, even if Paul doubled down on his bizarre hatred for Wales post-match.

Known as an organisation that backs the All Blacks to the hilt, the Herald described Wales as ‘the appendix of Britain’ and said their moment in the sun was a ‘pity win’ after they ‘won favour with the Gods’. Paul added of the Welsh: ‘They only see the sun twice a year, have come to view fish finger sandwiches as a delicacy worthy of being on brasserie menus and they are gripped by a crippling fabric shortage which leaves everyone barely covered when they head for a Friday night drink.’

Louis Rees-Zammit touches down for Wales' fifth try in the famous win - their bravery in turning down kicks at goal was rewarded

Adam Beard and Ryan Elias hold up New Zealand's Scott Barrett. The Welsh defence was phenomenal on Saturday

The All Blacks don’t lose many games and being beaten by Wales has clearly not landed well. ‘That result sets the bar now in terms of performance,’ Basham said. ‘When we put on the Welsh jersey, we believe we can beat anyone, especially at home.’

At Wales’ Vale of Glamorgan hotel on Monday, Tandy’s rugby stars were coming back down to earth. The country’s football side led by manager Craig Bellamy had also moved in ahead of their Nations League clash with Portugal on Tuesday.

The autograph hunters who had besieged the hotel site, however, were still more interested in football than rugby. New Welsh and Liverpool sensation Lewis Koumas was mobbed, leaving the likes of Adam Beard and Max Llewellyn to enter the lobby with ease. Some things don't change even when you beat New Zealand.

There were, unsurprisingly, big smiles everywhere you looked. Back-up No 9 Morgan-Williams made the most of his moment in the spotlight with a podcast appearance. Forwards coach Danny Wilson greeted Daily Mail Sport with a huge grin and praised the impact of the Welsh crowd in the team’s success.

On Monday morning, the Wales squad members not involved against New Zealand started to sweat out the beer they’d consumed on Saturday night with a fitness session.

The focus has now started to turn to this weekend’s meeting with Australia. It’s a game that needs to be won if Wales are to show their downing of the All Blacks was not just a glorious one-off. ‘Anything is possible at home,’ Basham said. ‘It will be hard to top last weekend, of course it will be. But now we want to keep on building from this.’

Welsh rugby’s struggles in this World Cup cycle meant there were 20,000 unsold tickets for New Zealand. The WRU hope their shock success will increase sales for Australia.

Last Saturday, Wales showed bags of heart, defensive desire and no little bravery. They were skilful, too. Dafydd Jenkins and James Botham led the miraculous forward effort, Jenkins making a world record-equalling 38 tackles. Botham was in tears at the final whistle, summing up the mood across the country.

Wales' jubilant players celebrate their country's first win over the All Blacks in over 70 years at full time

Taine Plumtree is embraced by Blair Murray. Players are already turning their attention to replicating these scenes against Australia on Saturday

Wales turned down kicks at goal to score five tries. Captain Dewi Lake, Eddie James and Tomos Williams also stood out. But to a man, Wales were phenomenal as they sparked astonishing scenes of celebration both in Cardiff and across the country.

Basham starred against New Zealand in 2021 but prior to his latest meeting with them, he had not started an international in four years. He was only called into the team as a No 8 replacement for the injured Aaron Wainwright.

‘It’s not really sunk in yet,’ Basham admitted. ‘I think we’ll reflect on it more at the end of the campaign. We’ve always had belief. I want to keep putting my hand up for future selection. I want to continue to stay involved. We want to get a result this weekend too.’

Basham declared himself to be in a ‘dream’ after playing his part in the New Zealand success. The whole country is, undoubtedly, still on cloud nine too and will be for some time.

Sports.title: Man City MUST stop the rot, old rivals Chelsea and Leeds set for Stamford Bridge blockbuster and Mauricio Pochettino's baptism of fire: SEVEN reasons we're excited for the return of the Premier League
Sports.content:
After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

And what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in new colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

Can City stop the rot?

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

City have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games

Expect chaos at the Bridge

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

After comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side currently sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

The Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league

Thomas Frank is back in the dugout

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

And he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his new team currently sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a new manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side

Arsenal face St James' Park test

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

However, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park

Can Brighton maintain their strong start?

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

They remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

But somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

The squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period

Wirtz is finding his Flo

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp

Poch is back

There is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he said goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his new club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

And that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Sports.title: Undefeated UFC star who nearly died in nightclub drug overdose breaks his silence: 'My body gave out'
Sports.content:
UFC star Tommy McMillen has admitted he potentially 'mixed the wrong kind of substances' leading up to his emergency trip to the hospital earlier this month.

It was revealed last Thursday that McMillen, who boasts an undefeated professional record, had been found unresponsive in a Scottsdale, Arizona, club the Sunday prior.

Reports revealed that responding officers immediately administered Narcan to the MMA star after noticing a 'white, powdery substance' on the ground near him.

Following the terrifying medical emergency, McMillen was transported to a local medical facility where he was successfully stabilized by healthcare professionals.

In the days that followed, the 28-year-old's trainers ensured that McMillen was back in training and now the rising UFC star has offered a candid account on the matter.

On The Joe Rogan Experience podcast, McMillen explained: 'I was in the middle of the club and I had a few different substances on me and maybe [I] just mixed the wrong kind of substances. Or maybe [I] had a bad batch of something.

🚨 Tommy McMillen opens up about his overdose, and says he needed two doses of Narcan and didn't regain awareness until around 5 AM



Tommy says it's a wake up call, but it won't stop him from partying



🗣️ Joe Rogan: "Stay off the f*cking pills man. You're risking dying. The… pic.twitter.com/V05YlEn8S7 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 17, 2026

UFC star Tommy McMillen has admitted he potentially 'mixed the wrong kind of substances' leading up to his emergency trip to the hospital earlier this month

The UFC star made the admission during an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience

'I guess my body gave out and I started to choke... stuff was coming out of my mouth and I was, like, choking on it. And then I was unresponsive. I don't remember any of this. They had to give me two Narcans, take me to hospital and give me an IV.

'I think that happened at 11pm that night. I didn't wake up until 5am the next day.'

After explaining that he was unconscious for about 'six to seven' hours, McMillen said: 'I try to be smart most the time. [But] If I'm really drunk and already faded, my decisions... my judgement starts to go down a little bit.

'I probably would've swallowed the whole bag of something and just not even known because I was that faded', the featherweight star added.

Following the explanation, podcast host Joe Rogan interjected to offer a plea to McMillen. 'NARCAN is very effective. If that stuff wasn't around, you might be dead.

'Stay off the f***ing pills man. You've got to keep away from pills. You're risking dying. The amount of fentanyl it takes to kill you is so little.'

However, despite the harrowing medical emergency and Rogan's request, McMillen suggested that his party days are far from over.

'It's a wake up call. But I don't know if I'm just going to stop partying and go cold turkey,' he explained.

McMillen boasts an undefeated mixed martial arts record through 12 professional fights

McMillen also opened up on his upbringing in Great Falls, Montana

He continued by opening up on his upbringing in Great Falls, Montana, where he claims he was exposed to substances from an extremely young age.

'It's one of the number one meth capitals in the world. It's a very small town, and a lot of people from my hometown fall victim to fentanyl-laced stuff. It's bad. It's terrible.

'I love the people there. They're super supportive, but there's something about that town. Even my friends who moved away say you can only go back for a couple of days. It's one of those places where dreams go to die.

'Nobody has any sense of direction or wants to do big things. Everyone just parties. That's why I developed that partying habit. It's all I did growing up.

'When I started partying around fifth grade and getting into substances, it was the only thing that made my mind shut off. I could finally just sit and enjoy life like a normal kid.'

McMillen, who fights out of Glendale, Arizona, has been steadily building a fierce reputation since turning professional in 2019 and racking up 12 consecutive victories.

His most recent fight saw him secure a dominant unanimous decision victory over Marwan Rahiki in September.

The UFC has not yet released an official statement regarding the concerning weekend incident involving their promising undefeated featherweight fighter.

Sports.title: NBC commentator Dan Hicks' cause of death revealed after heartbroken TV host wife announced 'sudden' illness
Sports.content:
Legendary NBC broadcaster Dan Hicks died of a lung infection, according to reports.

The 64-year-old was best known for calling the action at the Olympics, on the PGA Tour and at Notre Dame football games. He also worked NFL games for NBC between 1992 and 1998.

His death sparked an outpouring of tributes from across the sporting world and on Tuesday, the California Post reported that Hicks' immediate cause of death was multifocal pneumonia.

The announcer reportedly passed away at a hospital in Connecticut on November 11. According to the Post, he had also faced a build-up of fluid in the lungs, an infection and a rare issue with his immune system called autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

Following his death, Hicks' wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm, shared a statement on behalf of their three daughters: Hannah, Ellery, and Riley.

'Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness,' Storm said.

Legendary NBC broadcaster Dan Hicks died of a lung infection, according to reports

Hicks and Hannah Storm met in the late 1980s when they were both working at CNN

Tiger Woods is interviewed by Hicks after winning the TOUR Championship in 2018

'He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.

'Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together.

'He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered.

'Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time. There are simply no words to express how much he will be missed.'

Hicks called many iconic sporting moments including the US swim team's comeback at the 2008 Beijing Olympics and Tiger Woods' dramatic putt to force a playoff at the 2008 US Open.

Following the broadcaster's death, Woods paid a heartfelt tribute to his 'great friend.'

'Dan Hicks was beloved by all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him. His kindness, warmth, and presence will be deeply missed,' the golf legend wrote.

'Like so many in the golf world, Dan was a great friend to me both on and off the course. I had the utmost respect for him and the incredible job he did for our sport for decades.

'Our thoughts are with Hannah and their daughters during this incredibly difficult time. I hope they find comfort in knowing how much he meant to so many people and the lasting impact he made on everyone whose life he touched.'

NBC Sports executives Rick Cordella, Sam Flood and Molly Solomon responded to the tragedy with their own statement on Hicks' impact.

Hicks' wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm, shared a statement on behalf of their family

The NBC broadcaster speaks with ex-Ryder Cup captains (L-R) Jack Nicklaus and Tony Jacklin

'Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person,' the statement began. 'In his 34 years at NBC sports, he was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history.

'From Olympic swimming and skiing to Notre Dame football, numerous other high profile events and especially as the signature voice of our golf coverage for the last 26 years, Dan's blend of knowledge, style, enthusiasm and humor informed and entertained fans for decades.

'But far beyond his on-air excellence, Dan was a better person who welcomed teammates with a smile, a joke, or a word of encouragement, sometimes all three in the same sentence.

'Our heartfelt condolences and love to his wife Hannah and his daughters Hannah, Ellery and Riley.'

After growing up in Tucson, Arizona, Hicks remained in the area by enrolling at the University of Arizona, where he began doing radio. Later, he became a weekend anchor at Tucson's KVOA before working as a sports reporter for upstart cable network, CNN, in 1989.

It was while working for CNN in Atlanta that Hicks met his future wife, Storm, whom he married in 1994.

While Storm was becoming a staple of NBA coverage at NBC, Hicks joined the network, where he'd go on to work top golf majors, NFL playoff games and Notre Dame football. Coincidentally, Storm happens to be an alum of the South Bend, Indiana school.

'My favorite call of his was the 4x100m Freestyle Relay comeback at 2008 Beijing Olympics,' one fan wrote on X, adding: 'incredible call on an incredible moment.'

'Dan Hicks was as soothing as a sports-event host could be,' another fan wrote. 'He was like golf itself: pastoral, convivial, inviting. Clear and unpretentious in his command. He always made a golf telecast better. This is tough, tough news.'

Storm and Hicks got married in 1994 and had three daughters: Hannah, Riley and Ellery

Former NBC Universal executive Mark Lazarus released his own statement on Hicks' passing.

'I am heartbroken by the sudden loss of our friend Dan Hicks,' read Lazarus's statement. 'For decades, I had the privilege of working alongside Dan, but our friendship extended far beyond NBC Sports.

'Dan was one of the very best at what he did, but what I will remember most is the person he was: a loyal friend and a devoted husband and father. My family and I are thinking of Hannah, their children and the entire Hicks family. We will miss him.'

ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro has also issued a statement on the network's behalf.

'We are deeply saddened by the sudden passing of Dan Hicks, a respected voice in sports broadcasting and husband of longtime ESPN anchor Hannah Storm,' Pitaro said.

'Hannah is a cherished member of the ESPN family, and our hearts are with her, their three daughters and all who knew and loved Dan, including his NBC colleagues, during this incredibly difficult time. We extend our deepest condolences and stand alongside Hannah and her family.'

Sports.title: Top jockey Nico de Boinville ‘dragged out’ of weighing room after threat made against him
Sports.content:
Top jockey Nico de Boinville ‘dragged out’ of weighing room after threat made against him

Nicky Henderson’s first choice rider has revealed he was assigned extra security at Plumpton where he rode in two races at Plumpton on Monday

View Image Nico de Boinville: received a threat (Image: (Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images))

Top jockey Nico de Boinville has revealed that he was ‘dragged out’ of the weighing room after a threat was made against him.

As stable jockey to Nicky Henderson, the 37-year-old rides some of the best jumpers in the country. He is set to be reunited with Supreme Novices' Hurdle winner Old Park Star when for his chasing debut at Ffos Las on Wednesday.

De Boinville was riding at Plumpton on Monday where he took two mounts for Henderson who were both beaten favourites. Evens favourite Ginolo finished fifth of six and Ionian third of six as the 13-8 favourite.

Value Scope Extra: Hitintheheadlines could make front page news READ MORE :

OLI BELL: Paul Nicholls is the GOAT and the schadenfreude around his downswing is surprising READ MORE :

However on Tuesday de Boinville revealed that he had been alerted by security after the first race that he could be in danger.

Speaking to Racing HQ he said: “After the first race yesterday the security detail at Plumpton – they're very good, top-level people who dealt with the Brighton bombings and things like that – came in and dragged me out and said there's been a threat called in to me, so I needed security for the rest of the day.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"The threat came into the yard and then the PJA and then BHA, and then it gets called through to the racecourse. It's the trials and tribulations of being a jockey.

“It's bizarre. I'm going to work like everyone else and you don't expect that when you go to work. I feel sorry for whoever it was and I hope they get the help they need. It was probably because I got beat."

A BHA spokesperson said: "The BHA condemns all abusive or threatening behaviour towards our participants, who rightly should expect to be able to go about their jobs without being subjected to anything of this kind.

"We work closely with our colleagues across racing's representative bodies and, where appropriate, will take whatever action necessary to ensure the safety of everyone in our sport."

Sports.title: Arsenal legend Peter Storey dead aged 81 as tributes pour in for England icon
Sports.content:
Arsenal legend Peter Storey dead aged 81 as tributes pour in for England icon

Arsenal have announced the death of club legend Peter Storey, who played for the Gunners more than 500 times

View 2 Images Peter Storey has died (Image: Ed Lacey/Popperfoto via Getty Images/Getty Images)

Former England and Arsenal star Peter Storey has died aged 81. Storey was a key member of the Gunners' 1971 double-winning side, helping the team win the First Division title and the FA Cup under Bertie Mee.

‌



‌



Confirming the news of his death on Tuesday, Arsenal said: "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time."

‌



Storey played for Arsenal 501 times across 15 years and remains eighth on Arsenal's all-time appearance list. The north London side plan to pay tribute to the club legend ahead of their Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The midfielder was well known for his versatility and earned 19 caps for England under legendary manager Alf Ramsey. His first cap came in 1971 in a 3-0 win at Wembley against Greece.

Storey's career started when he joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961. It was four years before he made his first-team debut, shortly after his 20th birthday.

‌



The Surrey-born star was introduced as a left-back in a defeat to Leicester but impressed enough to play in the remaining 29 matches that season. Storey made a name for himself as a 'tough guy' after injuring Manchester City legend Mike Summerbee in the 1966/67 season.

View 2 Images Peter Storey has died aged 81 (Image: PA)

‌

But with the arrival of iconic Arsenal boss Mee, Storey cemented himself as an Arsenal legend, switching to right back and midfield as the Gunners improved beyond measure. His career saw him also earn the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup in addition to Arsenal's double.

‌



Storey's time at Arsenal ended on a sour note as he was suspended for refusing to train with reserves and he eventually move to Fulham on a free transfer in 1977. He helped the Cottagers avoid relegation in a team that included the likes of George Best, Bobby Moore and Rodney Marsh, before retiring part way through the next season.

Tributes poured in for Story, following the news of his passing. Arsenal fan Piers Morgan said: "Sad news. Superb player and key member of the great McLintock-led team that first made me an Arsenal fan. RIP Peter."

‌

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard fight cancelled at short notice
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard fight cancelled at short notice

Undefeated cruiserweight Jai Opetaia planned to move up a division to face former world champion Deonay Wilder in Cardiff next month

View Image Tyson Fury takes on Anthony Joshua next month

Australian Jai Opetaia has pulled out of his clash with Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff on December 11.

‌



‌



Undefeated cruiserweight Opetaia planned to move up a division to face former world champion Wilder, who was beaten twice by Fury in their epic trilogy. Wilder, 41, would have been returning to the ring following his points win over Britain’s Derek Chisora in April. But while Wilder may remain on the card, possibly in a rematch with Derek Chisora, Opetaia will not feature in the Welsh capital.

‌



Opetaia's withdrawal weakens an already-limited undercard with only two fights now confirmed for the main card in Wales, with Martin Bakole taking on Solomon Adebayo and Da’Mazion Vanhouter facing vs Michael Essomba. And before the co-main event was cancelled, promoter Eddie Hearn slammed the lack of Brits among the supporting cast.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

Anthony Joshua names two things he has which Tyson Fury does not READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua reveals Oleksandr Usyk advice for Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

"Opetaia vs Wilder is a great fight. I think that is an intriguing fight. If it happens. Now, the other two, on what planet would you ever put those two fights on the main card of Fury vs AJ?" he told iFL TV. "Da’Mazion Vanhouter... never heard of him. No disrespect. Build him (Vanhouter) on another f****** undercard. Not on the biggest fight in British boxing history. What about Joe Cordina? What about a two-time world champion from Wales? Mental. As it happens, I am going to land Joe Cordina a big fight in January anyway, but where's the thinking behind it?

‌



"I do not want to throw him under a bus, but I know he won't mind me saying it... I just got off the phone with Spencer Brown. Speechless. Martin Bakole vs the other fella who I have never heard of (Solomon Adebayo) and (Da’Mazion) Vanhouter... put them on the prelims. Thankfully I have got nothing to do with it."

And despite the fight scheduled to take place in less than a month, the organisers' application for a 1am start time has been met with concerns from local residents. Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau makes next move after LIV Golf collapse but faces lengthy ban
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau makes next move after LIV Golf collapse but faces lengthy ban

Bryson DeChambeau is among the nine players who've agreed to join the DP World Tour following the recent collapse of LIV Golf, marking his return to the sport's established tours

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau is coming back to mainstream golf (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Bryson DeChambeau has joined the DP World Tour for 2027 following the collapse of LIV Golf. But the two-time major winner is still set to be banned from the American circuit as he makes his return to the mainstream.

‌



‌



DeChambeau, 33, had maintained his commitment to LIV Golf despite Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund deciding to withdraw its funding in April. The breakaway tour confirmed earlier this month that intends to wind down operations, leaving a host of players looking for a new venture.

‌



As first reported by the Telegraph, DeChambeau was successful in submitting his application to join the European Tour before Sunday's deadline. Thanks to winning the 2024 US Open, the American boasts Category 1 status and can play in whichever tournament he chooses.

‌



But it could be a while until DeChambeau plays professionally on home soil. The PGA Tour typically has a one-year ban on players dating to their most recent LIV appearance - August in DeChambeau's case.

Scottie Scheffler's agreement with manager as PGA Tour star loses out on millions READ MORE :

There could be hope for DeChambeau and other stars such as Jon Rahm, however. On Monday, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said: "We've heard from our fans and we know they want the best players playing together, and we share that view, I have said from day one, when I took this job, I'm interested in doing whatever makes the PGA Tour better.

‌



"That said, as we have a membership organisation, we have rules and as I've shared before they exist to ensure fairness and competitive balance. Rules matter and they will be enforced. We engaged in thoughtful discussion on the topic of LIV players with both boards today.

"As far as we have read, bankruptcy proceedings are ongoing and the process is complex. I hope to have more to say at the beginning of the new year but until that time I will not speculate on the outcome or individual decisions that players make."

‌



Should the PGA Tour lift its ban after LIV Golf collapsed? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images LIV Golf lost its funding from Saudi Arabia earlier this year (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



DeChambeau - who's already confirmed to be taking part in Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge, a DP World Tour event, in South Africa next month - is one of nine players to make the move from LIV Golf to the DP World Tour, joining Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith. The others are Abraham Ancer, Lucas Herbert, Michael La Sasso, Joaquin Niemann, Carlos Ortiz and Thomas Pieters.

DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings commented: "There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months.

Article continues below

"As golf's global tour, we have taken a pragmatic approach to this unique and unprecedented situation as we go into next year, always with the best interests of our entire membership at the forefront of our minds."

Sports.title: UK Snooker Championship preview - on sale now
Sports.content:
UK Snooker Championship preview - on sale now

Our special edition brings you all you need to know ahead of the tournament, which starts at York's Barbican on November 28.

View 2 Images YORK, ENGLAND - DECEMBER 07: Mark Selby of England poses with trophy after winning the Final match against Judd Trump of England on day 9 of the 2025 UK Championship in Snooker at Barbican Centre on December 7, 2025 in York, England. (Photo by Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Ronnie O’Sullivan has won it eight times, Mark Selby is back to defend it, Judd Trump has unfinished business and a new generation of Chinese superstars are determined to take it home. Our special edition on sale now features interviews, season so far, top young players and a Virgo special.

Welcome to the UK Championship, where reputations count for plenty but guarantee absolutely nothing.

With £312,500 awaiting the winner at the Barbican, there is more than just pride at stake as the world’s finest players descend on the city to fight it out for the opening Triple Crown event of the season.

View 2 Images

For defending champion Selby, it is another opportunity to further his place among snooker’s all-time greats.

China’s remarkable rise has transformed the sport’s landscape and nowhere is that more evident than in the emergence of Zhao Xintong and Wu Yize.

Zhao, the 2025 world champion, climbed to the top of the world rankings in August on his way to the Wuhan Open final, becoming just the second Chinese player, after Ding Junhui, to do so.

However, he is no longer China’s only superstar. Wu, just 23, announced himself on the grandest stage in May when he defeated Shaun Murphy 18-17 in a thrilling World Championship final at Sheffield’s Crucible Theatre.

But write off the old guard at your peril, particularly when one of them happens to be the greatest player snooker has ever seen.

O’Sullivan turns 51 in December, but the Rocket remains the sport’s most magnetic personality and biggest draw.

Nobody has won the UK Championship more often than his eight triumphs, a remarkable collection stretching from his teenage breakthrough in 1993, aged just 17, to his most recent success in 2023, an astonishing 30 years later.

Trump, meanwhile, arrives with his own reasons for wanting to make amends. The Bristolian lifted the trophy in 2024, defeating Barry Hawkins in the final, before falling agonisingly short of retaining it last year.

The list of contenders certainly does not end there.

Australia’s Neil Robertson, a three-time UK champion, possesses the scoring power to dismantle almost anyone.

John Higgins and Mark Williams, fellow members of snooker’s celebrated Class of ‘92 alongside O’Sullivan, continue to defy the passage of time and have five UK titles between them.

Murphy, the 2008 champion, remains a threat, while Kyren Wilson will be eyeing a first UK Championship to complete the Triple Crown after his Masters and World Championship successes in 2026 and 2024 respectively.

Sports.title: David Raya becomes next Arsenal star to land new deal after huge Declan Rice agreement
Sports.content:
David Raya becomes next Arsenal star to land new deal after huge Declan Rice agreement

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is set to follow Declan Rice in committing his long-term future to the Premier League champions after agreeing a new contract

View 2 Images David Raya will commit his future to Arsenal (Image: Marc Atkins)

David Raya will be rewarded for his evolution into one of the world's best goalkeepers with a new contract after reaching an agreement in principle over fresh terms with Arsenal.

‌



‌



The 31-year-old joined Arsenal on loan initially in the summer of 2023 and quickly established himself as the Gunners' first-choice keeper. His move was made permanent the following year for a further £27million, with Raya a standout in the imperious defensive united which helped Arsenal finally taste Premier League glory once again last season.

‌



Raya's previous terms were set to expire in 2028. But he is now poised to commit his future to the champions beyond that, as first reported by The Athletic.

‌



News of an agreement with Raya continues the trend of positive contract news this week for Arsenal, who have made an impressive start to the defence of their Premier League crown.

It's said Rice, signed from West Ham in a £105m deal back in 2023, will join Bukayo Saka as one of Arsenal's top earners once he puts pen to paper on his new contract.

Timber and Raya both played their role in Arsenal recording a league-best 19 clean sheets last season. The Gunners defence was the meanest in the Premier League, conceding just 27 goals in total.

Raya had previously hinted that a move to Spain could be on the cards after admitting he would like to "experience the Spanish league" in an interview last month, though he did also stress that he was "very happy" at Arsenal.
