World.title: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
World.content:
El Salvador’s security minister has confirmed the troops will leave once kidnapped technicians are rescued.

Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country.

On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”.

Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence.

The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti.

But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found.

“If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said.

That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay.

Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge.

“The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday.

He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years.



“During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week.

A ‘mano dura’ approach

The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead.

Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions.

Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations.

The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security.

Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials.

His heavy-handed approach has led to a sharp decline in crime but has also been widely condemned for human rights abuses.

Critics have warned that transplanting such tactics to Haiti could spark a backlash, leading to greater instability and risks to civilians.

They have also criticised the lack of long-term planning for El Salvador’s troop deployment; a sudden withdrawal, for instance, could worsen the situation for Haiti’s security forces.

Bukele is campaigning for a third term in El Salvador’s February presidential election, and analysts speculate his actions in Haiti could be used as a campaign tool to drum up support.

A series of international actions

The Salvadoran deployment is the latest in a series of international interventions in Haiti.

Such foreign involvement is often controversial. The United States, for instance, has sent troops to Haiti on multiple occasions in the 20th century, occupying the country for decades and seizing control of its central bank.

More recently, a United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) arrived in Haiti in April, to help address the widespread gang violence.

Gangs control more than 80 percent of the capital region. The conflict has killed more than 22,000 people since 2022. UN reports attribute more than half of the deaths in the first nine months of the year to security operations, including the deaths of 300 civilians.

The UN also says almost 2,000 people have been displaced since the arrival of Salvadoran troops.



But Pelissier said Haiti’s government had not reported any civilian casualties in the latest operations, which he described as professional.

“The best to do is to avoid, as much as possible, human rights violations, and that’s what we are doing together,” the minister said.

World.title: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19
World.content:
Russia’s Defence Ministry says preliminary findings on the crash point to equipment failure.

A military plane has crashed in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, according to a statement from the Russian Defence Ministry, cited by local media.

The Antonov An-12 transport aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000km east of Moscow. The An-12 typically has a crew of six.

Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash, but preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure.

“A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by the RIA Novosti news agency.

Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk, posting on Telegram from the scene of the accident, said emergency crews had extinguished a fire. He said crews were helping to investigate the accident.

Seredyuk, in a video posted online showing the site of the accident near the village of Yagunovo, said the plane had been flying through the region when it crashed.

The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top criminal investigation agency, launched an inquiry into possible violations of flight safety rules, a standard practice following crashes.

The An-12 is a Soviet-built four-engine turboprop transport plane that has been in service since the late 1950s. More than 1,000 were built, and some still remain in operation in Russia and other nations.

In September, a Russian Tupolev Tu-95 military aircraft crashed in the eastern region of Amur, killing six crew members and injuring a seventh.

World.title: US Fed’s Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has been trying to fire Cook since August 2025.

United States Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has declined, through her lawyers, to appear next month before a Trump administration committee that is considering whether she should be fired, calling the process unfair and committed to a predetermined outcome.

The refusal extends the wrangling between the White House and Cook’s lawyers regarding her appearance before the committee, which the administration of US President Donald Trump initially demanded for November 6.

Administration officials have called on Cook to appear before the committee to address allegations that she committed mortgage fraud in 2021, before she joined the Fed’s board of governors, a charge she denies. Cook has not been charged with any crime.

Trump has sought to fire Cook since August 2025, and she has argued that the president’s efforts to do so represent a threat to the Fed’s independence and reflect Trump’s desire to force the central bank to reduce borrowing costs.

“Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution’s unique status and independence,” Abbe David Lowell, Cook’s lawyer, wrote in a letter released on Tuesday to White House counsel William Scharf. The three-person panel set up by the White House to consider the allegations “appears to be a facade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook”, the letter said.

In June, the US Supreme Court blocked Trump from removing Cook while litigation over the attempted firing continues, finding that “the fact of independence but also the appearance of independence is key to the Federal Reserve’s design”.



Trump officials have threatened to move ahead with the hearing even without Cook, and in a November 3 letter said that the three-member committee “reserves the right to draw adverse inferences against you” for not participating.

The unusual “committee of inquiry” set up by the White House consists of Kevin Hassett, Trump’s top economic adviser; Andrea Lucas, whom Trump appointed to lead the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission; and Keith Sonderling, Trump’s pick for Department of Labor secretary.

The Supreme Court said in a footnote to its June ruling that Trump could try again to fire Cook if the administration provided her adequate notice and an opportunity to respond. The committee of inquiry is an effort to meet those conditions.

Under the law governing the Fed, the president can only fire a Fed governor “for cause”, but the Supreme Court didn’t address whether Cook’s actions met that standard. The committee will ultimately recommend whether there is cause to fire Cook, the White House has said.

World.title: Trump’s Whirlwind Asia Trip Begins in the Philippines
World.content:
A painting by the Russian artist Alexey Sergienko depicted the leaders of the United States, Russia and China. It was unveiled in St. Petersburg, Russia, on Thursday.

President Trump sets off this week for meetings in Asia that will culminate in a summit with two strongmen he has often praised: President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia.

It will be the first time the three men, who command the world’s largest nuclear arsenals, will have sat down together. Mr. Trump plans to discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world and the war against Iran, according to a White House spokeswoman. He is not expected to bring up Russia’s war with Ukraine.

Mr. Trump will travel first to Manila, then to southern China, and will meet with regional leaders confronting an array of uncertainties. Those include the course of the war between the United States and Iran, high energy prices and mounting concern over the risks of artificial intelligence.

For Mr. Trump, the trip will be a pivot to foreign policy and relationships after American voters delivered a swift rebuke to his party in the midterm elections. His trip also comes as his administration faces scrutiny over a scandal involving the former chief executive of Nvidia, the tech giant, which has raised questions about Chinese espionage and American tech exports.

Echoes of Yalta

The highlight of Mr. Trump’s trip is expected to be his meeting with Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin on Thursday in China.

The prospect of their summit has drawn comparisons to the 1945 conference in the Crimean city of Yalta, where the leaders of the United States, the Soviet Union and Britain met to decide the shape of postwar Europe.

The White House has said that Mr. Trump wants to discuss the threat of nuclear proliferation. U.S. officials have expressed concerns about China’s accelerating nuclear buildup, expected to reach 1,000 nuclear warheads by 2030.

The last nuclear arms control treaty between the United States and Russia expired in February. Trump administration officials have said that any new agreement on nuclear arms control must include China, but Beijing has shown no interest in the topic. China has an estimated 620 nuclear warheads, compared with the more than 5,000 that Russia and the United States have each, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.

Image DF-61 nuclear missiles were displayed at a military parade in Beijing last year. China, which has the world’s fastest-growing nuclear arsenal, has made clear it that is not interested in arms control talks. Credit... Tingshu Wang/Reuters

U.S. administration officials said they did not expect a deal out of the meeting, which they characterized as a starting point for discussions.

The gathering has prompted concern in Ukraine that Mr. Putin might push for a deal, deciding Ukraine’s fate without Kyiv’s involvement. A U.S. administration official said Ukraine was not expected to be part of the discussion between the three leaders.

U.S. Partners Look for Reassurance

Mr. Trump will start his trip in the Philippines, the oldest American treaty ally in the Asia-Pacific region, as the United States faces questions about its support for its partners in a region where China’s military and economic might continues to grow.

In Manila, President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. plans to discuss with Mr. Trump the South China Sea, where the Philippines and China have competing claims. Philippine officials have said that they hope Mr. Trump’s visit might result in more American military assistance.

Image President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. of the Philippines spoke at a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila on Sunday. Philippine officials hope Mr. Trump’s visit might result in more U.S. military aid. Credit... Pool photo by Lisa Marie David

Mr. Trump is also expected to meet with leaders of ASEAN, a Southeast Asian grouping of 11 nations, as well as a gathering of the so-called Quad grouping of the United States, India, Australia and Japan.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese of Australia said on Sunday that he expected “lots of engagement” with Mr. Trump during the meetings.

“Obviously, that’s our most important ally,” he said. “But we want to see something constructive come out of that, including we want to see a de-escalation in the conflicts that are around the world.”

Chinese analysts described the meeting of the Quad group, formed in part to counter China, as an effort by Mr. Trump to project power after his party’s defeat in the midterms. “Its symbolic value outweighs its practical value,” Xu Liping, a senior scholar at Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, told Shanghai Observer, a state-run outlet.

The Spy Scandal

After Manila, Mr. Trump will travel to the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, where he will meet Mr. Xi on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation.

Jensen Huang, a key adviser who accompanied Mr. Trump on his last trip to China, will not be by his side. Mr. Huang helped shape the president’s views about technological competition with China and persuaded him to loosen restrictions on selling advanced chips to China.

Mr. Huang stepped down from his role at Nvidia after revelations that he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence officials believe was collecting intelligence on Mr. Huang for Beijing. China has rejected the allegations, calling them “smears.” Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment.

So far, the president has not raised the issue with Mr. Xi and is not expected to during their meeting on Thursday. But the saga is likely to cause unease in China about whether Washington will impose tighter controls on the export of technology to the country.

As a result, U.S.-based analysts speculated that Mr. Xi might try to use his personal relationship with Mr. Trump to forestall such restrictions.

Image In September, Jensen Huang, then Nvidia’s chief executive, sat at the same table as Mr. Trump during a White House state dinner for Mr. Xi. Mr. Huang had traveled with Mr. Trump to China before, but will not this time. Credit... Doug Mills/The New York Times

Yun Sun, director of the China program at the Stimson Center in Washington, said Mr. Huang’s downfall would likely mean “there is going to be more anxiety on the Chinese side about their access to American chips.” She expects Mr. Xi to emphasize the importance of easing U.S. controls on chip exports to China during their meeting.

Cooperation between China and the United States on artificial intelligence may be more difficult after the Nvidia scandal.

Still, there may be progress on the creation of a notification system that would allow the countries to alert each other about national security issues related to artificial intelligence, which the two sides agreed to in September.

“There’s some shared concern on both sides that U.S. or Chinese models might be misused by bad actors and cause damage to the U.S., China, or other countries,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution focusing on China’s technology development.

Xi May Have a New Calculus

When Mr. Xi sits down with Mr. Trump in Shenzhen, he will be dealing with a president who will soon face a new constraint at home: a Democrat-controlled Congress.

Lawmakers may pressure Mr. Trump to tighten export controls against China or accelerate weapons sales to Taiwan, according to Ali Wyne, a senior research and advocacy adviser focusing on U.S.-China relations at the International Crisis Group. That means that “Xi will have to work much harder to keep Trump on side,” Mr. Wyne said.

Mr. Trump will be the first American president to visit China twice in one calendar year.

Analysts say the leaders’ summits, which have included state visits in Beijing and then in Washington, have been the only thing holding together a fragile détente between the two countries as they clash over A.I., export controls, Taiwan and other issues.

The two sides declared a trade truce last year when they met in Busan, South Korea. That deal, which was to expire this month, has been extended until January.

Image Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi after their meeting in Busan, South Korea, last year. Analysts say their summits have been the only thing holding together a fragile détente between the countries. Credit... Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times

China’s restrictions on the export of crucial rare-earth metals and rare-earth magnets, which are needed to manufacture most modern technology, remain one of the most difficult unresolved issues.

Mr. Trump is likely to raise this with Mr. Xi, according to a senior U.S. administration official who said that China’s continued restrictions is one reason Washington only agreed to a two-month extension of the trade truce.

Ana Swanson contributed reporting from Washington, Aie Balagtas See from Manila, and Laura Chung from Sydney, Australia.

“Obviously, that’s our most important ally,” he said. “But we want to see something constructive come out of that, including we want to see a de-escalation in the conflicts that are around the world.”

Chinese analysts described the meeting of the Quad group, formed in part to counter China, as an effort by Mr. Trump to project power after his party’s defeat in the midterms. “Its symbolic value outweighs its practical value,” Xu Liping, a senior scholar at Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, told Shanghai Observer, a state-run outlet.

The Spy Scandal

After Manila, Mr. Trump will travel to the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, where he will meet Mr. Xi on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation.

Jensen Huang, a key adviser who accompanied Mr. Trump on his last trip to China, will not be by his side. Mr. Huang helped shape the president’s views about technological competition with China and persuaded him to loosen restrictions on selling advanced chips to China.

Mr. Huang stepped down from his role at Nvidia after revelations that he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence officials believe was collecting intelligence on Mr. Huang for Beijing. China has rejected the allegations, calling them “smears.” Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment.

So far, the president has not raised the issue with Mr. Xi and is not expected to during their meeting on Thursday. But the saga is likely to cause unease in China about whether Washington will impose tighter controls on the export of technology to the country.

As a result, U.S.-based analysts speculated that Mr. Xi might try to use his personal relationship with Mr. Trump to forestall such restrictions.

Image In September, Jensen Huang, then Nvidia’s chief executive, sat at the same table as Mr. Trump during a White House state dinner for Mr. Xi. Mr. Huang had traveled with Mr. Trump to China before, but will not this time. Credit... Doug Mills/The New York Times

Yun Sun, director of the China program at the Stimson Center in Washington, said Mr. Huang’s downfall would likely mean “there is going to be more anxiety on the Chinese side about their access to American chips.” She expects Mr. Xi to emphasize the importance of easing U.S. controls on chip exports to China during their meeting.

Cooperation between China and the United States on artificial intelligence may be more difficult after the Nvidia scandal.

Still, there may be progress on the creation of a notification system that would allow the countries to alert each other about national security issues related to artificial intelligence, which the two sides agreed to in September.

“There’s some shared concern on both sides that U.S. or Chinese models might be misused by bad actors and cause damage to the U.S., China, or other countries,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution focusing on China’s technology development.

Xi May Have a New Calculus

When Mr. Xi sits down with Mr. Trump in Shenzhen, he will be dealing with a president who will soon face a new constraint at home: a Democrat-controlled Congress.

Lawmakers may pressure Mr. Trump to tighten export controls against China or accelerate weapons sales to Taiwan, according to Ali Wyne, a senior research and advocacy adviser focusing on U.S.-China relations at the International Crisis Group. That means that “Xi will have to work much harder to keep Trump on side,” Mr. Wyne said.

Mr. Trump will be the first American president to visit China twice in one calendar year.

Analysts say the leaders’ summits, which have included state visits in Beijing and then in Washington, have been the only thing holding together a fragile détente between the two countries as they clash over A.I., export controls, Taiwan and other issues.

The two sides declared a trade truce last year when they met in Busan, South Korea. That deal, which was to expire this month, has been extended until January.

Image Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi after their meeting in Busan, South Korea, last year. Analysts say their summits have been the only thing holding together a fragile détente between the countries. Credit... Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times

China’s restrictions on the export of crucial rare-earth metals and rare-earth magnets, which are needed to manufacture most modern technology, remain one of the most difficult unresolved issues.

Mr. Trump is likely to raise this with Mr. Xi, according to a senior U.S. administration official who said that China’s continued restrictions is one reason Washington only agreed to a two-month extension of the trade truce.

Ana Swanson contributed reporting from Washington, Aie Balagtas See from Manila, and Laura Chung from Sydney, Australia.

World.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
World.content:
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.

The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".

Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight.

Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.

While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.

The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014.

The $3.6bn (Â£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.

World.title: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
World.content:
Moscow uses Crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.

The attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on Crimea, dictated by Ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from Russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".

Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea â the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.

There is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.

Moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.

In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.

Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.

In 2018, Putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of Russia and Crimea in a Russian-made truck. That section of the road now lies on the seabed.

Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

World.title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as firm reports bumper results
World.content:
Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it is not reinstating ousted co-founder Jensen Huang.

In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Colette Kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "We've got this."

The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (Â£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping by almost 4% in after-hours trading.

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy for China.

"The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said during a Tuesday call with financial analysts.

The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same time period.

Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise another 13% in the next quarter.

World.title: Thomas Markle charged over child sex abuse material in Philippines
World.content:
Police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.

The charges were filed on Monday, Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC.

Earlier this month, Markle, 82, was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The FBI said agents, after searching storage units Markle rented, seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books, that they allege contained child sex abuse material.

Markle, who is in custody in the US, has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney for comment.

Elmido told the BBC that Philippine National Police had charged Markle Sr with "two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM [child sexual abuse and exploitation material], and one count of possession of CSAEM material".

Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

Earlier this month, Markle Sr was arrested and charged in the US. He had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida, but was taken back into custody last week after prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor.

Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

In a previously shared statement after the allegations against her father emerged, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

World.title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
World.content:
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.

Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.

Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.

At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.

The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.

Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.

Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.

Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.

"It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.

But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.

"It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that."

World.title: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board
World.content:
A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media.

The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement.

The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way.

Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police.

Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby".

The governor added that the "main task" now was to help investigators carry out their work.

He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby.

CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen.

The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area.

It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board.

An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.

World.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
World.content:
A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.

There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.

According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.

There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.

They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.

All settlements are illegal under international law.

World.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
World.content:
After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.

Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.

The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.

The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections.

The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.

PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.

"These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination."

World.title: 140 UNIBEN graduates earn 1st class honours
World.content:
A total of 140 undergraduates of the University of Benin (UNIBEN) have earned First-Class Honours as the institution prepares to graduate 11,357 students at its 2025/2026 convocation.

Edoba Omoregie, vice-chancellor of UNIBEN, disclosed this on Tuesday in Benin at a pre-convocation news conference.

Mr Omoregie, a professor, explained that 8,789 undergraduates and 2,568 postgraduate students would receive various degrees.

“The Senate of the university has found the 8,789 undergraduate graduands worthy in character and learning to be awarded their first degrees.

“140 undergraduates earned First-Class Honours, 2589 obtained Second-Class Honour, Upper Division, 4465 Second-Class Lower and 513 Third-Class degrees,” he said

The vice-chancellor said no student would be awarded a pass degree.

Mr Omoregie disclosed that 484 of the postgraduate students had earned doctoral degrees, while 44 would receive Master of Philosophy degrees.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The postgraduate category also comprised 1,409 master’s degree recipients and 631 postgraduate diploma graduands.

The vice-chancellor said the university would also confer honorary doctorate degrees on three distinguished alumni and award the title of professor emeritus to a retired professor.

Recorded achievements

Mr Omoregie described the 2025/2026 academic session as peaceful and successful, attributing the achievement to commitment of the university’s stakeholders.

On academic development, he said all 34 programmes presented for accreditation during the session received full accreditation.

He added that the university’s Doctor of Veterinary Medicine programme had been restored and accredited by the National Universities Commission.

Mr Omoregie said the institution had expanded from 17 faculties when he assumed office to 22, alongside the establishment of five centres and institutes.

“In less than two years in office, we have introduced a lot of innovation in line with best global practices in order to reposition the University of Benin as one of the best academic, if not the best academic institution in this country,” he said.

He also highlighted the university’s digital transformation efforts, particularly the development of an in-house student information management portal.

According to him, the portal manages the records of certificate, diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate students and supports transcript processing.

He said the initiative had reduced the university’s dependence on external service providers and improved the management of academic records.

According to him, convocation activities will begin on 24 November with an interfaith service and the Founder’s Day lecture.

The lecture, titled: “The Wealth Beneath Our Feet and the Wealth Within Our Minds: Rethinking Leadership, Education, and National Development,” will be delivered by an alumnus and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan.

He said the convocation lecture, scheduled for 26 November, will be delivered by Attahiru Jega, a professor and former chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission and special adviser to the President Bola Tinubu on Presidential Livestock Reform.

According to him, the lecture is titled: “Reinvigoration and Revitalisation of the Nigerian University System: What Is to Be Done?”

The vice-chancellor thanked the university’s staff, students, alumni and other stakeholders for their contributions to its development.

(NAN)

World.title: Bank official testifies on N500m disbursements from ONSA account to private company during Dasuki’s tenure
World.content:
A bank manager told the FCT High Court in Abuja on Tuesday that the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) sent N500 million to a private company while Sambo Dasuki was in charge of the office.

Obazele Anthony, the fourth prosecution witness presented by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), said Real Properties Investment Limited (RPIL) received “N500 million from NSA” on 20 November 2014.

Mr Dasuki served as NSA between 2012 and 2015, at the height of Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria’s North-east, during the administration of then-President Goodluck Jonathan.

The EFCC accused him, along with former Sokoto State Governor Attahiru Bafarawa, his son Sagir Bafarawa, former Minister of State for Finance Bashir Yuguda, and Dalhatu Investment Limited, of N19.4 billion in arms-procurement fraud.

Since 2015, Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants have been facing 25 counts of misappropriation, criminal breach of trust and receiving stolen property.

The charges accuse them of diverting N19.4 billion from the NSA office’s account. The money was said to be meant for procurement of arms to firm up the offensive against Boko Haram terrorists during former President Goodluck Jonathan administration, between 2014 and 2015.

This case is one of the twin indictments Mr Dasuki is facing before separate judges of the FCT High Court regarding his management of the arms procurement funds.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He and his co-defendants in the two cases denied the allegations.

Utilisation of N500 million

Led in evidence by EFCC’s lawyer Rotimi Jacobs, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), on Tuesday, Mr Anthony narrated the utilisation of the N500 million transferred into Real Properties Investment Limited by ONSA.

The company transferred N1.5 million to an individual identified as “Alhaji Mutiu Idowu”, N7.5 million to Kalaks Investment Limited, N1 million to Real Oil Mills and N140,000 to Adekola Adeoye.

Similarly, it also sent N10 million to Mr Idowu, N100 million to Senator Rashidi Ladoja, N250 million to Meristem Wealth Management Limited and a fixed deposit of N100 million.

Mr Ladoja is a former governor of Oyo State, was a Third Republic senator and is the present Olubadan of Ibadan. Details of his connection to the case remains sketchy at the current stage of the prosecution’s case.

Witness not privy to transactions’ purpose

Defence lawyers – A.O. Ayodele for Mr Yuguda, A.A. Usman for Mr Dasuki and James Olatoke, a SAN, for the Bafarawas – took turn to cross-examine the witness.

The witness confirmed during the rounds of question that the bank did not flag the transactions as suspicious.

The prosecution witness, who maintained that he neither worked with ONSA nor knew the purpose of the transactions, said the payments to the individuals and firms listed were not on the authority of the NSA.

He confirmed that he was not the compliance officer, did not author the documents EFCC presented in court, and was not involved in any of the transactions.

He named the compliance officers who signed the Real Properties Investment Limited account statement. He said the officials were still alive.

The witness also confirmed that “somebody signed on behalf of some of the compliance officers,” whose names were listed on the documents.

He also noted that Mr Bafarawa was not a beneficiary of any of the transactions.

Thereafter, the witness was discharged, and the trial judge, Yusuf Halilu, adjourned the case until 15 December.

World.title: Heirs Holding to play leading role to play key role at inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit
World.content:
Heirs Holdings, the pan-African investment group founded by African investor and philanthropist Tony O Elumelu, will play a leading role at the inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit (WAIIS 2026), taking place 16-18 November in Sierra Leone.

As a Principal Partner of the Summit, the Group is bringing its senior business leadership, investment expertise and extensive operating experience across critical sectors of the African economy to advance the region’s integration and investment agenda.

Mr Elumelu, Group Chairman of Heirs Holdings and a member of the Summit’s Private Sector Advisory Board, is leading private sector mobilisation for the event, convened under the leadership of His Excellency Julius Maada Bio, President of Sierra Leone.

He will be joined by senior executives from across the Group’s portfolio, including Obong Idiong, CEO of Heirs Technologies, who will speak at the Investment Opportunity Session on connecting West Africa’s markets through payments, data and digital networks and Peter Ikenga, CEO of Transcorp Power, who will co-chair the power session alongside Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, Côte d’Ivoire’s Minister of Mines, Oil and Energy.

The Summit brings together African Heads of State, policymakers, institutional investors, development finance institutions and business leaders to accelerate economic integration and unlock investment opportunities across West Africa.

A longstanding advocate of Africapitalism and a business turnaround expert, Elumelu champions the principle that Africa’s development must be driven by African entrepreneurs and businesses, with long-term private investment creating both economic and social wealth. His leadership at WAIIS reflects a conviction that regional integration must move beyond policy commitments to practical commercial partnerships, cross-border investment and the development of competitive African enterprises.

Heirs Holdings’ prominent role at WAIIS is reinforced by its scale, investment footprint and track record of building businesses across sectors critical to Africa’s economic transformation. As of 31 March 2026, the value of its portfolio companies stood at approximately US$15.08 billion. With investments and operations spanning 24 countries and a workforce of more than 40,000 people across the Group and its portfolio companies, Heirs Holdings is a significant pan-African private-sector investment platform.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

For Heirs Holdings, West African integration represents a significant opportunity to expand the region’s economic potential and attractiveness to investors. A more connected region creates larger markets, strengthens intra-regional trade, facilitates the movement of capital, attracts investment, creates jobs, and enables African businesses to achieve greater scale and compete more effectively in the global economy.

As governments, investors and business leaders convene in Sierra Leone, Heirs Holdings reaffirms its commitment to working with public and private sector partners to turn regional integration into a commercial reality that will create lasting economic and social value across the continent.

Heirs Holdings is a leading pan-African investment company. Its investment portfolio spans the energy, power, banking, insurance and financial services, technology, real estate, hospitality and healthcare sectors, operating in twenty-four countries worldwide.

Heirs Holdings is inspired by Africapitalism, the belief that the private sector is the key enabler of economic and social wealth creation in Africa. Driven by this philosophy, Heirs Holdings invests for the long-term, bringing strategic capital, sector expertise, a track record of business success, and operational excellence to its portfolio companies.

World.title: Tinubu campaigns in Kebbi, approves dry port as ex-governors declare support
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi, describing the facility as strategic towards boosting the state’s economy.

He also thanked the people of the state for their massive turnout and warm reception during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the Haliru Abdu Multi Purpose Stadium in Birnin Kebbi. President Tinubu said he would not take their support and confidence for granted.

One of the campaign’s highlights was former governors declaring they would work for President Tinubu’s re-election because he supported the state in times of need.

The former governors are Adamu Aleiro, Sai’du Dankingari and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Atiku Bagudu.

The president reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to complete ongoing landmark infrastructure projects, especially the Illela-Badagry Superhighway, which passes through Kebbi, as well as other federal road networks within Kebbi State.

He commended Kebbi State Governor Nasir Idris for complementing the federal government’s road-construction efforts and promised to expand the state’s agricultural programmes.

“We will expand the existing agricultural programmes. We will support rice mills in Birnin Kebbi, Argungu, Bagudo and Yauri.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We will ensure that the Zuru–Rijau Road is actualised, while the Koko–Dabai road will soon be completed through the Kebbi State Government platform. We will rehabilitate the Goronyo–Argungu irrigation scheme and the Zauro Polder Project so that your farmers can farm year-round,” the president said.

On security, President Tinubu pledged to strengthen further the national security architecture and support sub-nationals’ capacity to fight crime by signing the state police bill into law.

“We are mindful of the challenges in Zuru, Danko/Wasagu, Sakaba, Bagudo, Arewa, Shanga and some parts of Maiyama. We shall work together to end insecurity.

“In the meantime, we have deployed more troops to the state. We have provided more equipment to the military and police. We have approved new operating bases in Zuru, Bagudo and Yauri.

“By the grace of God, the days of bandits terrorising our innocent farmers are numbered, as we step up efforts to ensure that no farmer in Kebbi will be afraid to go to his farm again,” the president assured.

He further stated his administration’s determination to ensure peaceful elections while thanking APC leadership, supporters, and residents of Birnin Kebbi for their solidarity and impressive turnout.

In his remarks, Vice President Kashim Shettima reminded the audience of the support President Tinubu gave to late former President Muhammadu Buhari, enabling him to consolidate and win the 2015 presidential election.

He urged the northern voters to reciprocate the gesture.

The vice president told the gathering that President Tinubu sacrificed his resources and comfort to give the North what it wished in 2015. He also thanked the North for giving the president 60.2 per cent of the votes that gave the APC victory in 2023.

“The North repaid that kindness, and we are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in the coming election in January because you have rejected the lies, the distortions, the half-truths.

Earlier, the host governor, Nasir Idris, commended the president for graciously approving his request to fully operationalise the Kebbi Inland Dry Port and other critical road projects in the state.

Governor Idris assured the president of their support towards his re-election bid as a mark of appreciation for his support for the state’s socio-economic development.

The APC National Chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda, commended some guests’ testimonies on President Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructure development in the country, especially in education, health, and security.

He assured the president that the North has resolved to support his re-election in 2027.

AbdulAziz Yari, the director-general of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), thanked Kebbi residents for the massive turnout and commended the president for his massive investment in the state’s economy.

Mr Yari urged Kebbi residents to come out en masse and vote for the president in the forthcoming 2027 general elections.

He said the creation of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development was deliberate, aimed at addressing farmer-herder clashes in the north and supporting the ongoing construction of the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, designed to ease traffic along the corridor in line with the vision of Nigeria’s founding fathers.

Mr Yari urged voters to disregard the deceitful voices of the opposition parties.

The Kebbi APC Presidential campaign rally was attended by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, Governors Uba Sani of Kaduna, Dauda Lawal of Zamfara, Mala Buni of Yobe, Babagana Zulum of Borno and Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto.

Others include Speaker of the House of Representatives Tajudeen Abbas; Senators Adams Oshiomhole and Ali Sheriff; Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Housing Muttaqha Darma; and former governors Ahmed Yerima of Zamfara, Ibrahim Shema of Katsina, and Abdullahi Ganduje.

The APC campaign train has continued to criss-cross the country, engaging party stakeholders and Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 17, 2026

World.title: Fake News: Unilorin, Al-Hikmah VCs charge Mass Communication graduates to champion truth, tackle misinformation
World.content:
The Vice-Chancellor of Al-Hikmah University, Ilorin, Lateef Oladimeji, charged Mass Communication graduates to promote responsible journalism, combat misinformation, and restore public confidence in the media amid the rapidly evolving information landscape.

Mr Oladimeji, a professor, delivered the charge at the maiden Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Alumni Congress of the Mass Communication Alumni Association, University of Ilorin (MCAAUIL), held at the ICT Lecture Theatre of the university, themed “Together Again: Strengthening Our Alumni Legacy.”

He urged the graduates to embrace emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital platforms, while upholding the profession’s ethical standards.

The VC stressed the need to champion accuracy, inclusiveness, and accountability, and to invest in continuous learning as the media industry evolves.

The Dean also called on the alumni association to establish structured mentorship programmes that link alumni with current students and support practical training and industry exposure.

He further urged the association to sustain a strong relationship with the university’s Department of Mass Communication.

University’s ambassadors

Declaring the AGM open, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Abdulwahab Egbewole, said the institution consistently emphasised that its graduates are not merely recipients of certificates but ambassadors expected to project the university’s identity across global media, public service, corporate organisations, classrooms and creative industries.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Egbewole, a professor, represented the Dean of the Faculty of Information and Communication Sciences, and communications professor Saudat Abdulbaqi said the mass communication department consistently produced storytellers, gatekeepers, and communication strategists.

The Unilorin VC also acknowledged the department’s efforts in producing public intellectuals who contributed to shaping national discourse and projecting the university’s image.

He commended the alumni association, particularly its pioneer National President, Abdulgaffar Arikewuyo, and members of his executive for their commitment to the department’s development.

The Vice-Chancellor specifically acknowledged their contributions to upgrading departmental facilities, supporting the training studio, providing scholarships and financial assistance to indigent students, and facilitating mentorship programmes.

According to him, the association’s interventions helped bridge the gap between the town and the gown, describing its contributions as a shining example for other alumni associations to emulate in supporting the university.

Character development

Mr Egbewole also urged students of the department to demonstrate the same commitment to character development and academic excellence so they could eventually join the alumni association and contribute to their alma mater’s growth.

Also speaking, the Head of the Department of Mass Communication, University of Ilorin, Rasaq Adisa, described the department as a model within the faculty after the alumni association installed a solar-powered inverter system.

Mr Adisa, a professor, said the installed solar system provided a more reliable power supply for teaching, research and other academic activities.

The mass communication head also noted that the improved power supply made the department a convergence point for other departments within the faculty.

He appreciated the association for its interventions and appealed for further support, while urging the newly elected executive to build on its predecessor’s achievements and take the association to greater heights.

Association’s genesis

In his welcome address titled “Returning to the Place That Made Us,” the outgoing National President, Mr Arikewuyo, recalled that the association’s vision was conceived in 2019 under the leadership of Lambe Mustapha, the then Head of Department.

The former president also acknowledged those who pioneered the idea of bringing graduates together, regardless of location and profession, to support one another, mentor younger students, and give back to the institution that shaped their lives.

Mr Arikewuyo, a doctorate degree holder, said the initiative, which began as a WhatsApp group with fewer than 100 members, had grown into a community of nearly 1,000 alumni.

The MCAAUIL leader described the physical gathering of members for the association’s maiden AGM and election of new executives, following years of virtual meetings, online interactions and telephone conversations, as more than an ordinary meeting but a memorable homecoming to the classrooms, corridors and familiar surroundings that shaped their academic journeys.

He explained that the association had translated its vision into practical interventions over the years through annual awards and cash prizes to promote academic excellence and recognise outstanding graduating students.

He said the association has also contributed to the renovation of the departmental newsroom, provided financial assistance to students struggling to pay their fees, facilitated Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme (SIWES) placements, and purchased and installed a solar inverter to ensure uninterrupted power supply in the department.

In his acceptance speech, the new National President, Aderemi Adeagbo, Head of the Department of Mass Communication at Ire Polytechnic, appreciated the outgoing executive for its achievements and pledged that the new leadership would build on its foundation and strive to surpass its accomplishments.

Mr Adeagbo assured members that his administration would uphold the dignity and integrity of the association while strengthening networking and mentorship among graduates, current students and lecturers of the department.

New executives

Following an election conducted through a consensus arrangement, Mr Adeagbo emerged as the new National President of the association.

Other members of the new executive include Fatimah Mustapha, National Vice-President; Faruk Jolayemi, National General Secretary; David Ann, National Assistant General Secretary; and Hafeez Akewusola, National Treasurer.

Also elected were Aminah Shakirudeen as National Financial Secretary, Preye Campell as National Publicity Secretary, and Victor Ayomide as National Auditor.

Mahmud AbdulRaheem, Abdulgaffar Arikewuyo, and Medinah Oladotun are members of the BOT.

The newly elected executive members were sworn in by the Chairman of the Electoral Committee, Mahmood Alaya.

Special awards were presented to some distinguished alumni for their contributions to the association, including Balqeez Lambe, Felix Micheal and Titi George, while certificates of excellence were given to others.

World.title: Why Tinubu should be re-elected as president – Fashola
World.content:
Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola, said on Tuesday that President Bola Tinubu should be re-elected for second term based on the policies he has introduced during his administration.

Mr Fashola, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and former Minister of Works and Housing during the late President Muhammadu Buhari’s tenure, listed the reviewed minimum wage, the stundents’ loan scheme oveerseen by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), harmonisation of tax laws, stamp duty waivers on lease agreements and introduction of CNG as the policies.

Mr Fashola, who appeared as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday evening, admitted that there were gaps between policies and results, but said, “We are seeing the roll-out slowly, and in the fullness of time, you will see the impacts.”

“These are the compelling reasons why we must not abort this journey mid-term and exchange it for uncertain promises without assurances,” the former governor added.

Mr Fashola also defended the subsidy removal policy, which Nigerians have blamed for the growing economic hardship accros the country.

He noted that without its removal, Nigeria would lose foreign income.

Mr Fashola, who succeeded Mr Tinubu as Lagos State governor in 2007 and served in that capacity for two terms ending May 2015, emphasised that the president’s policies did not cause hardship but described it as a collective global issue.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“There is no need to deny that the cost of living is now a global challenge. Any right-thinking person will concede to that, and Nigeria is not immune to that challenge,” he said.

He blamed Nigeria’s economic hardship on the world’s recovery from the global COVID-19 pandemic, Russia/Ukraine and the Middle East wars.

He called on the opposition to argue on how to increase the benefits of the Tinubu administration’s reforms for Nigerians rather than proposing to bring back subsidies.

Mr Fashola said this to oppose the African Democractic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s remarks on his plan for the petrol subsidy.

The former Vice President, Mr Abubakar, promised to review existing crude oil supply commitments, including those linked to borrowing, to make more oil available to domestic refineries under his proposed production-based petrol subsidy if elected president in 2027.

As the 2027 general elections draw close, many members of the ruling All Progressives Congress are intesifying their campaigns for Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

On 3 November, the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, also noted that Mr Tinubu should be elected on the strength of his performance in the last three and a half years.

World.title: Akwa Ibom fishing communities to petition oil regulators, National Assembly over recurring pollution
World.content:
Residents of Ntan Mbat, a fishing community in Ibiono Ibom Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, have resolved to petition petroleum regulators and the National Assembly over recurring oil pollution they say is destroying their fishing livelihoods.

The residents said oil sheen regularly appeared on their fishing waters, particularly during the rainy season, despite years of complaints to government officials and their political representatives.

They announced the decision on Monday during a community training on environmental rights, grassroots organising and advocacy organised by Peace Point Development Foundation (PPDF), in partnership with the Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF), at Ntan Mbat Community Hall.

The proposed petitions will be directed to the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) and the National Assembly, with the community seeking an investigation into the suspected source of the pollution and its effects on their environment.

Ntan Mbat comprises four villages: Edem Ntan Mbat, Obot Ukim Ntan Mbat, Obot Enang Ntan Mbat and Usuk Ntan Mbat.

Residents said the pollution originates from the direction of Esuk Ntan Mbat, an area within the community that is not recognised as a separate certified village. They identified three oil wells, reportedly drilled and capped in the 1950s, as requiring investigation.

Although residents could not pinpoint the precise source of the oil sheen, they said the affected water bodies connect to the Calabar-Itu River, raising concerns about the potential spread of pollution beyond the immediate area.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Decades of complaints, threatened livelihoods

Friday Akpan, the village council chairman of Ntan Mbat, said the community had repeatedly approached government officials and political representatives at the state level over the recurring pollution but had yet to receive a meaningful response.

“Every rainy season, oil will spill all over the community. We, as a community, will call on the government to come to our plight, especially at the state level, through our representatives in the past, but nothing is forthcoming,” he said.

Mr Akpan said the training had introduced residents to the regulatory institutions and public authorities responsible for addressing environmental pollution.

“We are delighted over the training of today. It has opened our eyes to the regulators and duty bearers we will now approach: NOSDRA, NUPRC and the National Assembly. We will petition them to come and look into the matter,” he said.

The village head of Obot Ukim, Enefiok Bassey, also commended the organisers, saying he would mobilise the heads of the other three villages to jointly write to the relevant authorities. He said the recurring oil sheen had severely affected residents who depend on fishing for their livelihoods.

“When we see the oil sheen on the water, which usually happens during the rainy season, we don’t see fish to catch at all,” he said.

The consequences, residents said, extend beyond those who venture into the water to fish.

Fish dryers and sellers also depend on the catch brought home by fishermen. A decline in fish catch therefore affects the entire fishing value chain, reducing income for households that depend on the trade.

Learning to demand accountability

The training was designed to help residents move from individual complaints to organised community advocacy, with emphasis on documenting environmental incidents, gathering evidence and identifying the institutions responsible for responding to them.

In a presentation, Umo Isuaikoh, coordinator of PPDF, discussed the Nigeria Socio-Ecological Alternatives Charter and the Niger Delta Alternatives Convergence, highlighting the need for development that protects communities, ecosystems and livelihoods.

He explained that the frameworks advocate protecting rivers, creeks and mangroves; community participation in decisions on extractive activities; environmental restoration; and a transition away from dependence on oil.

For fishing communities, the principles include ensuring that fishers are consulted on decisions about their fishing grounds, that environmental damage is prevented, and that compensation, where established, restores lost livelihoods rather than merely providing temporary financial relief.

Mr Isuaikoh’s presentation also emphasised that environmental protection should not be separated from economic survival.

For communities whose livelihoods depend on fishing, he explained, the destruction of waterways translates into declining fish stocks, reduced household income and threats to food security.

In another presentation, an environmentalist, Peace Udoh, addressed grassroots organising and advocacy for environmental justice

She called on residents to document changes in their environment, including declining fish catches, unusual water colour, dead fish, disappearing mangroves and other signs of ecological degradation.

She said community members possessed valuable knowledge about their environment because of their longstanding interaction with the rivers and creeks.

She encouraged fishers to record where they fish, the quantity and species of fish caught, unusual changes in water conditions and the dates and locations of suspected pollution incidents.

According to her, such records, when properly documented and verified, could provide evidence to support community demands for government intervention.

She also stressed the importance of collective action, urging residents to work together, engage regulators, attend public hearings, approach the media and build alliances with other fishers through the fishnet alliance.

“Your experience is data,” she told participants, explaining that individual observations could become stronger evidence when systematically documented and independently verified.

Ms Udoh asked Ntan Mbat residents to communicate their experiences through local radio, community meetings, WhatsApp voice notes and partnerships with media organisations.

“We are not against development, but development should not destroy our water and our future,” she said, urging residents to demand accountability peacefully and collectively.

The training comes amid growing concerns about the environmental consequences of ageing and abandoned petroleum infrastructure in Akwa Ibom and other Niger Delta communities.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on 10 November that residents of communities in Ikono and Ibiono Ibom were learning to document environmental pollution after decades of complaints about oil allegedly seeping from abandoned wells drilled and capped in the 1950s.

In September, PREMIUM TIMES also reported that residents of oil-bearing communities in the two local government areas had demanded an urgent assessment, remediation and protection of abandoned oil wells and ageing petroleum infrastructure.

The residents’ latest decision to approach regulators and lawmakers signals a move from raising complaints through local political channels to seeking formal regulatory and legislative intervention.

World.title: 2027: Stakeholders warn against vote-buying, security agencies’ partisanship in Akwa Ibom
World.content:
Stakeholders at a multi-stakeholder peace forum in Akwa Ibom State warned that vote-buying, political manipulation of security agencies and declining public confidence in the electoral commission could threaten the peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections.

They called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies, political parties and other critical institutions to take proactive steps to address the challenges before the elections, warning that failure to do so could deepen electoral violence and undermine public confidence in the process.

The stakeholders spoke on Thursday at a one-day multi-stakeholder peace forum organised by Youth for Change Initiative, with technical support from the Foundation for Partnership Initiatives in the Niger Delta (PIND), in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.

The forum, themed “Peaceful Elections: Strengthening Stakeholders’ Collaboration for Electoral Peace in the 2027 General Elections,” brought together representatives of security agencies, traditional and religious institutions, civil society organisations, the media, and women and youth groups.

Presenting a paper at the event, civil society actor Ekom Akpan identified vote-buying, political desperation, and public distrust in INEC as major threats to credible elections.

Mr Akpan said electoral violence was not an isolated election-day occurrence but a recurring problem that required sustained intervention before, during and after elections.

He questioned whether the 2027 elections would produce another cycle of violence and bereaved families, urging stakeholders to prevent a repeat of past experiences.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He called on security agencies to take vote-buying seriously, warning that politicians could exploit economic hardship to manipulate voters.

“Hunger should not be weaponised to ensure vote-buying,” he said, urging citizens to reject inducements and develop the values needed to hold elected officials accountable.

Mr Akpan said there is a declining public confidence in INEC. He said past experiences such as glitches on the INEC Result Viewing Portal and disturbing discoveries had weakened Nigerians’ belief in the commission’s ability to deliver credible elections.

He asked the electoral body to rebuild public trust through deliberate transparency, timely communication and openness in its preparations.

He also challenged security agencies to show their neutrality, alleging that political elites had, over the years, used security operatives to manipulate elections.

“Beating me in an election does not mean we are enemies,” he said, urging political parties and candidates to present clear manifestos for public analysis rather than promote hostility.

Mr Akpan further called on politicians to campaign with ideas instead of insults and called on religious leaders to speak truthfully to political office holders rather than merely echo government positions.

He also appealed to traditional rulers to remain neutral and cautioned against using women as instruments of political mobilisation without meaningful participation in political decision-making.

Vote-buying, ethnic politics

In a goodwill message, Ahmed Isa, who represented the Hausa community in Akwa Ibom, called on voters to assess candidates based on their competence, track records and policy proposals rather than ethnic or religious affiliations.

He advised voters not to be swayed by candidates’ theatrical performances at campaign rallies but to demand their manifestos and examine what they intended to achieve if elected.

“Hold your aspirants and leaders accountable. When you succumb to vote-buying, you have sold your destiny. You cannot ask the person for anything during governance,” he said.

Similarly, traditional ruler Precious Udo of Ifa Ikot Abia Ntuen urged voters to vote according to their conscience and resist intimidation and vote-buying.

The Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Journalists, Akwa Ibom State Council, Nsibiet John, charged journalists to begin scrutinising candidates’ manifestos and investigating the possibilities of their campaign promises ahead of the elections.

Mr John warned against assuming that the outcome of the 2027 elections was already determined, saying stakeholders must begin preparing for possible challenges, including technological failures during the electoral process.

He advocated the establishment of professional election-monitoring situation rooms to track developments and facilitate timely responses to emerging challenges.

He also cautioned journalists against publishing unverified information capable of heightening political tensions, urging them to investigate questionable reports before dissemination.

“The media in Akwa Ibom State offers itself to stand as a reliable partner for peaceful and credible elections,” he said.

40 peace monitors deployed

In her welcome remarks, the Executive Director of Youth for Change Initiative, Joy Ubong, said the organisation was implementing a project to prevent and mitigate election-related violence through community-based early warning systems, stakeholder collaboration and media-driven peace advocacy.

She said the project targets eight local government areas: Abak, Esit Eket, Etim Ekpo, Ibeno, Ibesikpo Asutan, Ini, Nsit Ubium and Uyo.

According to her, Youth for Change Initiative has established, trained and inaugurated a 16-member Community Stakeholders Network comprising state and non-state actors to coordinate responses to reported conflicts and violence.

She said the network would work with 40 trained peace monitors deployed across the eight local government areas to observe developments, identify early warning signs, document incidents and report potential threats for timely intervention.

Ms Ubong identified early warning and response, responsible media reporting, and multi-stakeholder collaboration as the initiative’s three main approaches.

She appealed to stakeholders to verify information and avoid circulating inflammatory statements, stressing that peaceful elections were a shared responsibility.

World.title: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates over violence
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify political candidates found, through established court convictions, to have instigated or participated in electoral violence, irrespective of their party affiliations.

The upper chamber also called on state governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadia under their control, for political activities.

The resolutions followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi (Bauchi Central) on Tuesday, expressing concern over the growing incidence of political violence, intolerance and attacks on political leaders and their supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Senate condemned what it described as the increasing frequency and spread of political violence across the country, warning that attacks on political leaders, supporters and political gatherings posed threats to national security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 elections.

It also urged security agencies to conduct impartial and transparent investigations into reported incidents of political violence in Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states, identify the perpetrators and their sponsors, and ensure their prosecution in accordance with the law.

The lawmakers further called on the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings nationwide.

They urged the establishment of effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to prevent attacks and other forms of violence ahead of the elections.

The Senate also mandated its Committees on National Security and Intelligence, Police Affairs, and INEC to engage relevant institutions and report back within one week on measures to prevent political violence and safeguard the 2027 general elections.

The motion followed reported attacks on political figures and gatherings, including the incident involving President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade after he observed Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque, Garki, Abuja.

Presenting the motion, Ningi recalled reported attacks on former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and other political stakeholders in Benue, the disruption of a political procession involving supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and the Obidient Movement in Asaba, Delta State, on November 7, which reportedly left one person dead and five others injured, as well as an attack on the convoy of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in Sokoto State.

He warned that failure to investigate and prosecute those responsible for political violence could encourage further attacks, deepen political divisions and undermine public confidence in the electoral process.
