World.title: Being Deposed as a Governor in Cuba with No Details Made Public
World.content:
The deposed governor of Camaguey, Cuba, Jorge Enrique Sutil Sarabia

By Amado Viera

HAVANA TIMES – On Saturday, November 14, during the debut of a radio program he will appear on every two weeks to “establish direct communication with the people,” Walter Simon Noris, the Communist Party’s first secretary in Camagüey, was so intent on focusing on his achievements at the helm of the province that he ended up with almost 20 minutes of airtime to spare.

He could have used precisely that time to reveal the “errors incompatible with his responsibilities” that had cost Governor Jorge Enrique Sutil Sarabia his position four days earlier. The accusations against the latter were so serious that the official announcement of his dismissal described it merely as a “resignation at his own request,” rather than softening it with terms such as “release from duties” or “assignment to other responsibilities,” which Cuban bureaucratic language typically uses in cases involving disgraced officials who have not been implicated in corruption or other similarly serious offenses.

Sutil had been “elected” governor of Camagüey in May 2023. At the time, the position of first secretary of the Communist Party was held by Federico Hernandez a party official from Granma province who would be dismissed two years later so that his involvement in a beef-trafficking network extending all the way to Havana could be investigated. The last information about him, several months later, was that he was in the capital awaiting legal proceedings in which several farm owners, private business owners, and a sizable group of Agriculture Ministry officials would also stand trial.

To get an idea of the magnitude of Sutil’s blunder, it is enough to note that, even under those circumstances, Hernandez’s removal had been described in official statements as a “release from duties as part of a renewal process.” That was far more lenient language than the wording used now.

“And What Do You Expect Me to Do?”

Sutil had arrived at Quinta San Zenon—the seat of the Camagüey provincial government—to replace Yoseily Gongora Lopez, a young politician who had taken advantage of her position to undergo a marathon series of cosmetic surgeries in Havana between 2021 and 2022. Thanks to those procedures, she managed to lose nearly 50 kilograms (110 pounds) and overcome her obesity. The problem was that she did so at the most critical point of the pandemic, when the province was on the verge of collapse. Gongora not only neglected the crisis but also clung to her office, aware that the preferential treatment she was receiving was due to her status as governor.

“If you ask me, it wasn’t an improvised decision but one based on pure calculation. Faced with a choice between improving her health and sacrificing herself to fulfill the responsibilities for which she had been elected, she chose the former. She must have known it would cost her career as a government official. That’s why, when she returned to lead the province, she didn’t make the slightest effort. You could see her at meetings and during official visits and realize she was there simply to go through the motions,” explained an official with the Camagüey provincial government.

Despite the controversies surrounding her, when Gongora was removed from office, she received “recognition for the effort, work, and dedication devoted to government service.” She was also appointed to a comfortable administrative position at Artex, a state-owned company that markets cultural performances and products.

Sutil’s final weeks as governor are reminiscent of that period under his predecessor. In fact, the only photograph published by the state press of the meeting at which he was dismissed shows him sitting in the second row of the officials presiding over the meeting, staring blankly into space and almost leaning against the wall. It was much the same way Gongora could sometimes be seen during her final official appearances.

There has been considerable speculation on social media about the reasons behind Sutil’s dismissal. More than one online content creator has claimed credit for bringing it about through alleged revelations concerning fuel trafficking, influence peddling, and other economic crimes. But the truth is that no one has been able to provide evidence beyond the testimony of sources who requested anonymity. Not a single incriminating document has come to light.

What is beyond dispute is that during the weeks preceding the former official’s “resignation”—when he had already been effectively excluded from major decision-making—some changes did occur in the way the province was run.

For example, the previous weekend, a massive cleanup campaign was launched in the city of Camagüey. The fuel needed to carry it out, which had been unavailable for weeks, suddenly appeared. State-operated minibuses also resumed service, transporting thousands of people daily at fares far lower than those charged by private operators. And several people connected to the Ministry of Public Health confirmed that the fleet of electric vehicles delivered to the province just a few months earlier to support healthcare services had been reorganized. These were the same vehicles that could often be found just about anywhere except at hospitals.

“It would be unfair to accuse Sutil of being directly responsible for so many things going wrong, but it’s equally true that he allowed them to happen. Even when problems were reported directly to him or were so obvious that there was no way to ignore them. I remember that about a year ago, a highly respected doctor approached him to denounce the shady dealings surrounding fuel sales in dollars. One specific example was the Sputnik gas station, where people who controlled places in line charged customers for their turns, and the regulations limiting the number of liters each customer could purchase were blatantly violated. ‘And what do you expect me to do?’ was Sutil’s response. That’s no way to run a province,” the official interviewed pointed out.

The former governor was not even capable of making simple decisions that would have been widely applauded by his fellow citizens, such as restoring order to Agramonte Park and Republica Street, the two busiest public spaces in the provincial capital, now overrun by skateboarders, beggars, and vehicles moving about as they please.

By the time rumors of his possible dismissal began to spread, Sutil had virtually no supporters left. In three years, he had exhausted the political capital he brought to office. Faced with that obvious reality, the government’s efforts have focused on preventing the details of his downfall from becoming public. There is little more they can hope to accomplish.

World.title: Leo XIV after his tour: “There is no need to hate each other or use such violent language”
World.content:
Leo XIV after his tour: “There is no need to hate each other or use such violent language”

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 16:37 UTC Full article

Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, “in many situations intentionally provoked”, at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome

Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, “in many situations intentionally provoked”, at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome after an eleven-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, in which he also said his health is good and recounted that he spoke with Argentine President Javier Milei about caring for those most in need.

Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, “in many situations intentionally provoked”, at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome after an eleven-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, in which he also said his health is good and recounted that he spoke with Argentine President Javier Milei about caring for those most in need.

“There will no doubt continue to be differences of opinion. But there is no need to hate each other, to use such violent language and to create, even within families, an inability to dialogue and rediscover unity,” the pontiff said. He blamed part of the problem on algorithms and “a polarisation that is not accidental”, citing his visit to Argentina as an example: “How is it possible that people of the right and the left were together in the streets, celebrating and rejoicing over something much more important than a political debate?” The media, he added, have a “very great” role in reducing polarisation.

On his meeting with Milei, the Pope said his message “is not political”. “Although in some countries there are those who try to push me to the right or the left, asking me to criticise or not, I speak of the encyclical Magnifica humanitas. And that is precisely what I spoke about with President Milei: respect for human beings and the need for greater consideration, especially for the neediest in Argentine society,” he explained. “He was willing to listen to this message. It was very positive.” The Pope also argued for a fairer redistribution of wealth and for “strengthening the working class, individuals and social movements”.

On his health, after the removal of a lung tumour on October 13, he said: “I cannot say I am at 100%, but I am quite well.” He reiterated that he will need no further treatment and said he has not signed any letter of resignation: “For now, I see no need, thank God.”

On clergy abuse, he called on bishops to take “responsibility for accompanying the victims”. He ruled out doctrinal changes for now, and said why Francis never returned to Argentina would remain “a mystery”. He promised Mexican faithful a visit: “I will come, I will come!”

The plane landed in Rome at 8.48 a.m. local time on Tuesday. According to El País, more than 13 million people attended his events in the three countries.

World.title: Venezuela uses US$12 billion in US-supervised oil revenue to prop up the bolívar
World.content:
Venezuela uses US$12 billion in US-supervised oil revenue to prop up the bolívar

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 16:30 UTC Full article

An oil pump jack in Venezuela, where crude sales under US oversight have funded dollar sales to prop up the bolívar.

Venezuela has spent most of the more than US$12 billion earned from oil sales under US supervision on propping up the bolívar, with modest results: inflation has slowed but remains the world's highest, and consumption has yet to recover.

Venezuela has spent most of the more than US$12 billion earned from oil sales under US supervision on propping up the bolívar, with modest results: inflation has slowed but remains the world's highest, and consumption has yet to recover.

According to a US State Department report cited by El País, the account through which Washington has supervised Venezuelan revenue since the January 3 military operation received US$12.263 billion by September 30, almost all from crude sales. Some 98.7% has already been disbursed at the request of Venezuela's Central Bank, which used it mainly to sell dollars to commercial banks to prevent shortages and keep the currency's price from soaring. Venezuela now sells its oil without discounts, at just over US$90 a barrel, and has raised output to 1.22 million barrels a day.

The intervention has had some effect. According to the Central Bank, October inflation was 6.2%, the lowest of the year and the third consecutive month below 10%. The bolívar lost 67% of its value against the dollar in the first ten months of the year, but over the past two months the decline has been around 6%, and the gap between the official and parallel dollar has narrowed from 50% in January to about 15%. Even so, prices rose 245% between January and October, and annual inflation stands at 376.9%. The minimum wage has been frozen at 130 bolívares since March 2022.

Economists blame the limited results on the design of exchange rate policy. “There are too many restrictions on access to the official market,” said Leonardo Vera, president of the National Academy of Economic Sciences, which pushes buyers to the parallel dollar and fuels prices. “The slowdown in inflation is very slow, too slow for the effort that has been made,” said José Guerra, a former opposition lawmaker and professor at the Central University of Venezuela. “The market does not trust the government's word.” Jesús Palacios, of the Andrés Bello Catholic University, called for a single exchange rate and fiscal reforms, with a deficit of 7.2% of GDP, according to that university's economic research institute.

The government of acting President Delcy Rodríguez last week signed a memorandum with ExxonMobil for the US oil company's return to the country.

World.title: Falklands close November with cricket, archery and hockey after opening Sports Complex
World.content:
Falklands close November with cricket, archery and hockey after opening Sports Complex

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 13:40 UTC Full article

Cricket against Costa Rica, the archery competition, and Princess Anne alongside the lawn bowls team during the opening of the Complex.

The Falklands are going through a month of intense international sporting activity, a week after the official opening of the new National Sports Complex in Stanley.

A series of T20 cricket matches against the visiting Costa Rica side was played in the archipelago in recent days. Running alongside it is an archery competition with international teams, under the name North South Archery Tournament.

Also in recent weeks, hockey teams across different age groups competed in Iquique, Chile, in the Drakons Cup.

The local calendar closes at the end of the month with the Falklands Games, scheduled for November 27, 28 and 29.

The National Sports Complex, opened on November 10 by Princess Anne during her visit to the archipelago, required an investment estimated at around £5 million, funded by the Falklands government with contributions from private sector companies. It is the first major investment in the Islands’ sporting facilities since the construction of the Stanley Leisure Centre and Swimming Pool some thirty years ago.

The facilities include a floodlit all-weather football and rugby pitch; an indoor centre for archery, lawn bowls and cricket nets, known as the Gold Centre; and a 50 by 52 metre sports hall for synthetic ice hockey, indoor football, basketball, netball, volleyball, tennis, table tennis, weightlifting and climbing. Exercise studios also allow for yoga, Pilates, dance exercise, ballet and spin classes. The complex complements the existing Stanley Leisure Centre, which houses the swimming pool.

The opening was attended by officials from international sporting bodies in whose competitions Falklands teams take part: Katie Sadleir, Chief Executive of Commonwealth Sport, and Andrew Inkster, of the International Island Games Association.

The Falklands competed in July 2025 at the Island Games held in the Scottish archipelago of Orkney, where 24 island groups took part, and expect to attend the next edition, to be held in the Faroe Islands from July 3 to 9, 2027, with 27 island teams anticipated. The archipelago also took part in the Commonwealth Games held in Glasgow, Scotland, between July 23 and August 2 this year.

Mike Summers, of the Falkland Islands National Sports Council, said work would continue towards delivering the Sports Strategy agreed by the Legislative Assembly, encouraging every sector of the community to get involved in sport, both competitively and recreationally, in an environment that promotes inclusion and the values of sportsmanship.

World.title: FAO Food Price Index remained relatively stable during October
World.content:
FAO Food Price Index remained relatively stable during October

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 13:23 UTC Full article

World wheat prices declined following four consecutive monthly increases, largely reflecting subdued international demand and improved production in Argentina

The benchmark measure of world food commodity prices edged lower in October, as weaker import demand contributed to month-on-month declines in the price indices for cereals, dairy products and meat, according to new data released by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

The FAO Food Price Index (FFPI), which tracks monthly changes in the international prices of a basket of globally traded food commodities, averaged 133.9 points in October 2026, down 1.6 points (1.2%) from its revised September level, as lower price indices across most commodity groups more than offset a sharp rise in sugar and a marginal increase in vegetable oils. Despite the monthly decline, the index stood 5.9% above its level a year earlier but remained 16.4 percent below its March 2022 peak.

The FAO Cereal Price Index fell 4.5 percent from September. World wheat prices declined following four consecutive monthly increases, largely reflecting subdued international demand and an improving production outlook, particularly in Argentina. Expectations of easing constraints on Black Sea export flows added to the downward pressure on prices, although continued disruptions to Black Sea logistics limited the decline.

International maize quotations also eased after reaching a three-year high in September, weighed down by harvest-related pressure in the United States of America, expectations of ample supplies in major exporting countries in South America, and renewed prospects for an easing of tensions in the Black Sea region. By contrast, the FAO All Rice Price Index increased by 1.6 percent in October 2026, as harvest delays in some rice exporting countries added to the upward price pressure exerted by adverse weather conditions and rising costs.

The FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index increased marginally, by 0.3 percent from September, as higher soybean and sunflower oil quotations more than offset lower rapeseed oil prices. Soybean oil quotations rose to their highest levels since late 2022, driven by continued firm demand from the biofuel sector and seasonally declining supplies from South America. Meanwhile, sunflower oil quotations rebounded from multi-month lows amid persistently tight export availabilities from the Black Sea region.

The FAO Meat Price Index fell 1.2 percent from September, while remaining slightly above its year-earlier level. Quotations declined for pig, ovine and bovine meats, while poultry meat prices remained broadly stable.

The FAO Dairy Price Index was down 1.1 percent from September, with the October decrease reflecting declines in international butter and cheese quotations amid ample supplies and subdued buying interest. The declines more than offset further increases in milk powder prices.

The FAO Sugar Price Index marked its fourth consecutive monthly increase to reach its highest level since December 2024 after rising 6.6 percent from September and 28.8 percent from a year ago. The rise was mainly driven by rainfall-related disruptions to sugarcane harvesting and crushing operations in Brazil's key Centre-South producing region as well as concerns over production prospects in India, the European Union and Thailand in the 2026/27 season.

World.title: S.S. ‘United States’ Is Now the World’s Largest Artificial Reef
World.content:
S.S. ‘United States’ Is Now the World’s Largest Artificial Reef

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 13:19 UTC Full article

An aerial view of the S.S. United States making 35 knots across the Atlantic in 1952

The World’s Fastest Ocean Liner finally hits the ocean floor. The 53,330-Ton S.S. ‘United States’ is now the world’s largest artificial reef. Longer than the “Titanic,” once carried celebrities and politicians across the Atlantic in midcentury style. Now, after decades of uncertainty and rust, it’s taking on a second life as an underwater refuge for marine creatures and curious divers, according to a piece from the Smithsonian Magazine.

Finally at 8:59 p.m. central time, the S.S. United States slipped below the waves, starting a new chapter as a home for marine life and a destination for divers from across the world, which is quite some time from June 29, 1952, when a state-of-the-art ocean liner, nearly 1,000 feet long, opened up to the public. Some 70,000 people flooded to its berth in New York City to catch a glimpse of the S.S. United States before it hit the Atlantic for its maiden voyage.

Almost immediately, the liner proved worthy of the intense interest. On July 3, 1952, the S.S. United States reached England in a record-breaking three days, ten hours and 40 minutes, a speed that has yet to be surpassed to this day by any passenger liner. In its 17-year run, the ship would go on to host numerous notables, including Marilyn Monroe, Walt Disney, Salvador Dali, and even the Mona Lisa, after the painting’s one and only trip to the US.

However last week more than 70 years after its record-setting maiden voyage, crowds once again came out in droves to see the legendary liner depart on one last journey. This time, the S.S. United States was heading to the bottom of the sea for a new life as an artificial reef in the Gulf of Gulf of Mexico.

Designed by the prolific 20th century naval architect William Francis Gibbs, the ocean liner represented the peak of post-World War II maritime technology. Over 100 feet longer than the Titanic, the United States contained no wood except the ship’s grand pianos, built with fire-resistant mahogany. “She will have more aluminum in her than Mr. Gibbs cares to say, a design feature that will contribute to the dual goal of strength and relative lightness,” George Horne reported for the NY Times in 1951.

Throughout the 1950s and ‘60s, the liner completed more than 800 journeys across the Atlantic, carrying more than 1 million passengers, including many celebrities and politicians.

Throughout its 17-year tenure, the S.S. United States carried four presidents: Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy and a young Bill Clinton, who took it to study at Oxford University as a Rhodes Scholar in 1968.

With its intricately designed interior featuring patriotic art, amenities including a movie theater and its unparalleled speed, the S.S. United States provided many passengers with lasting memories.

But as airline travel became more accessible, the age of luxury ocean liners soon drew to a close. In 1969, the S.S. United States was abruptly decommissioned. Even crew members were shocked by its sudden withdrawal from service. Several left personal belongings on board, assuming they would go back to work the next day, only to show up to locked gangway doors.

For the next nine years, it languished as a reserve ship for the U.S. Navy, ready to for action if the need arose. But there was no need, and in 1978, the ship was put up for sale.

In the following decades, the ship passed from port to port, from owner to owner, each with different plans for the ship: floating condominiums, hazardous waste removal in Ukraine, a revived cruise liner. But no idea garnered enough money or momentum to last. By 2024, the ship had foundered on a Philadelphia pier for decades.

When the pier’s landlord raised the daily dockage fee to US$1,700—US$ 620,500 per year—the S.S. United States was evicted and faced the possibility of getting scrapped. Instead, Florida’s Okaloosa County purchased the ship for US$1 million, with plans to turn it into the world’s largesgt artificial reef. The county already has a fleet of sunken ships off its coast, but the S.S. United States is its crowning jewel.

Officials expect the liner-turned-reef will become home to a variety of marine species, including red snapper, grouper, amberjack, mackerel and tuna. The ship will also be open to divers.

“She’s being reefed and will remain intact and will become a vibrant and dynamic marine habitat,” Susan Gibbs, the conservancy’s president and granddaughter of the ship’s designer, tells the Guardian’s Richard Luscombe.

The conservancy plans to run a museum adjacent to the pier where diving expeditions will set out, featuring the ship’s iconic smokestacks, alongside other parts of the ship’s interior and a collection of artifacts and memorabilia.

Unlike the liner’s legendary maiden voyage, the trip from Philadelphia to the ocean floor was far from speedy. After a handful of false starts and a last-ditch lawsuit, it took months of preparation at a port in Alabama to ready the vessel for its voyage to the bottom of the sea, the New York Times’ Jesse Pesta reports.

Workers removed the ship’s wiring, ductwork, glass and anything that could potentially pose a danger to divers or marine life. They also cut strategic passages through the ship’s interior to create open pathways that would reduce stagnant water and enable divers to easily pass in and out. Finally, they removed off the ship’s two iconic, six-story smokestacks, earmarked for the future museum. The S.S. United States was finally ready for sinking.

The ship then set out from Destin, Florida. A crew cut holes in the ship and removed more than 400 portholes. Water flooded in, but as night descended, it still hadn’t sunk.

“She was designed to be unsinkable, and that fact has definitely given our crews some challenges today,” Nick Tomecek, a spokesperson for Okaloosa County, told ABC 6. Or, as William Francis Gibbs once bragged, “You can’t set her on fire, you can’t sink her and you can’t catch her.”

World.title: Orsi praises “excellent” ties with Milei and Lula’s re-election ahead of the Mercosur summit
World.content:
Orsi praises “excellent” ties with Milei and Lula’s re-election ahead of the Mercosur summit

16th Monday, November 2026 - 23:47 UTC Full article

Orsi also praised Lula’s regional role and described his October 25 re-election as “fundamental”

Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi described his government’s relationship with Javier Milei’s administration in Argentina as “excellent” and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election in Brazil as “fundamental”, in a Mercosur assessment given in Madrid less than three weeks before the bloc’s summit of heads of state in Montevideo on December 4.

“The relationship is excellent,” Orsi said of Argentina at a breakfast forum organised by Nueva Economía Fórum, according to Europa Press. “Things we had never achieved, we did achieve with this government.” The Uruguayan president, of the left-wing Broad Front, attributed the good ties with Milei’s government to fluid contact even from “different philosophies and positions”, citing as examples progress on dredging the access channel to the port of Montevideo and the resolution of tensions over HIF Global’s green hydrogen plant project in Paysandú. Both countries also agree on the need to make Mercosur more flexible and modern.

Orsi also praised Lula’s regional role and described his October 25 re-election as “fundamental”. “It is good news because of the positions both candidates took on integration,” he said.

The remarks come at a time of strong tensions within the bloc. Relations between Argentina and Brazil are at their lowest point following Milei’s repeated attacks on Lula and the departure of defeated candidate Flávio Bolsonaro from Brazil via Argentine territory. Paraguay is also going through an institutional crisis after the removal and arrest of President Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, with his successor, Pedro Alliana, sworn in ten days ago.

The Montevideo summit, which will close Uruguay’s pro tempore presidency, is expected to address the debate on making the bloc more flexible and ongoing trade negotiations with Canada, the United Arab Emirates, Vietnam and Japan. The trade agreement with the European Union has applied provisionally since May 1.

World.title: Venezuela accuses Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi of “interference” over call for free elections
World.content:
Venezuela accuses Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi of “interference” over call for free elections

16th Monday, November 2026 - 23:42 UTC Full article

Uruguay and Venezuela broke off diplomatic relations in 2024, after the Uruguayan government refused to recognise Nicolás Maduro’s proclamation as winner of the presidential election

Venezuela’s government on Monday rejected as “interference” remarks by Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi, who had said hours earlier in Madrid that he cannot recognise a democratic government in Venezuela until free elections are held. Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco replied that the country’s future “belongs to the sovereign will of Venezuelans”.

Orsi, of the left-wing Broad Front and Uruguay’s president since March 2025, was speaking at a breakfast forum organised by Nueva Economía Fórum in the Spanish capital, during a visit in which he also met Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. “Let’s call things by their name. Since my election campaign and before, Venezuela did not function as a democracy. What needs to happen in Venezuela is a roadmap that culminates in free and transparent elections,” he said. He added that “until there are free elections” he cannot “recognise a democratic republican regime”, but that this does not prevent restoring relations. “Uruguay does not only have relations with democratic countries or with our style of democracy. Countries relate as countries, not as friends,” he said.

Blanco replied on X that a president’s agenda “should be marked by attention to the affairs of his population and the development of his country”. “Mutual respect, sovereign equality and cooperation between our countries are the basis for a constructive dialogue that contributes to peace, stability and Latin American integration,” he wrote. Blanco, a former opposition aide, was appointed foreign minister in late October by acting President Delcy Rodríguez.

Uruguay and Venezuela broke off diplomatic relations in 2024, after the Uruguayan government refused to recognise Nicolás Maduro’s proclamation as winner of the presidential election, which the opposition says was won by Edmundo González Urrutia. In June 2025, the two countries reactivated consular services in Montevideo and Caracas, although Uruguay maintained its political position. Rodríguez has governed as acting president since January, after Maduro’s removal from power in a US military operation, and on October 29 promised elections organised by a “renewed” electoral authority, though without setting a date.

World.title: Sunday evening planning felt less rushed after a shift at the start
World.content:
Sunday evening planning felt less rushed after a shift at the start

16th Monday, November 2026 - 21:29 UTC Full article

At 6:15 p.m., the dishwasher is humming and Monday's lunch is still undecided. I used to leave planning until I was already thinking about bed, which made even a short list feel like one more job.

Try moving your Sunday planning 15 minutes earlier and following a fixed sequence. You can sort errands, meals and work tasks without scheduling every hour, then finish with a small plan for Monday.

Move the Start Time Forward

Pick a dependable cue that happens before your usual planning time, such as clearing the dinner plates. If you normally sit down to plan at 8:30, set a 15 minute earlier start at 8:15, rather than waiting until you feel ready for bed.

Connect the cue to something you already do: when the plates are stacked, the kettle goes on, and you are already spinning the reels in the Big Bass Mission Fishin demo open your notes app. Set a stop time too. A 15 minute timer is enough to get started; if you need more, decide in advance that you'll stop after 25 minutes instead of letting the list sprawl.

Gather the Week's Loose Ends

Use one place for everything you need to remember this week. A single sheet of paper on the kitchen counter or one note on your phone works better than a work calendar, a text to yourself and a scrap of paper by the door.

Write each item as a short action, not a vague subject. “Pick up library holds” gives you a next move; “library” leaves you to work out what it means later. Keep going until you have the tasks, appointments and errands that are competing for space in your head.

Capture What Is Already on Your Mind

Get the items down before you decide which ones matter most. Add the half-finished work email, the laundry that needs moving and the dentist appointment to the same list, even if they belong to different parts of your life.

Use a due date or time only when you already know it. Write “submit form by 10 a.m. Tuesday” if that deadline is confirmed; don't guess a time for “sort the hallway cupboard.” You are recording reminders, not making promises to fit every task into the week.

Sort by What Needs Attention First

Mark anything attached to a fixed Monday appointment or deadline so it stands out. A star beside “bring signed form to school” is enough if you have to leave home at 8:10; you don't need to rewrite the whole list as a schedule.

Move the ideas that can wait to a later list. “Compare phone plans” may be worth doing, but it does not have to become a Monday commitment just because it occurred to you on Sunday. Keep the main list focused on what has a real time pressure.

Choose Monday's First Moves

Choose one small task you can begin without hunting for materials or clearing an hour. Before you finish planning, use this short sequence:

- Check Monday's calendar for appointments and fixed deadlines.

- Choose the first work or home task you can start easily.

- Prepare one item you will need, such as your bag, notebook or lunch container.

If I choose a time limited session in the Big Bass Mission Fishin demo, I treat it as paid entertainment with a budget set beforehand, like a cinema ticket, and an end time already on the clock. Keep that separate from the Monday plan: it should not take the place of preparing for an appointment or starting a necessary task.

Leave open space for the parts of Monday you can't predict, like a late bus or a colleague's request. You are choosing a first move, not trying to pre solve the whole day.

Set a Limit for Small Rewards

Pick one modest after work treat before the week gets busy. It might be a favorite snack from the corner shop, an episode of a show or a walk with a takeaway coffee. Decide what you can comfortably spend before choosing paid entertainment, and keep that amount separate from bills, groceries and savings.

Set an end time as well as a budget. If you want to watch one episode, choose the show before you sit down and stop when it ends, rather than letting autoplay decide how late you stay up. A small treat feels better when it doesn't create another problem for Tuesday morning.

Avoid Common Planning Mistakes

Don't turn your list into a timetable for every hour. Leave room for breaks, delays and the tasks that appear once the day begins. If you want a schedule, record only fixed appointments and the start time of your first task.

When a new idea pops up, write it on the later list unless it has a deadline or appointment attached. If planning keeps running past your stop time, shorten the list to fixed commitments and Monday's first move; don't push the start later and recreate the bedtime scramble.

Try the earlier start for one Sunday, then adjust the cue or duration to fit your routine. After the first week, Monday should begin with less guesswork; before you close the page, note your first task and the time you'll begin it.

World.title: A new museum in Yucatán tells the story of a controversial figure in Mexican history
World.content:
A museum dedicated to one of Mexico’s most notorious colonial figures has opened in a former convent in Yucatán state.

The museum examines the legacy of Diego de Landa, a Spanish friar whose campaign against Maya religious practices included burning their books and sacred objects.

But while chastised for that, he is also credited with leaving a detailed account of Maya life and religion — one that remains an important source for scholars studying the civilization he helped suppress.

The museum features nine display panels, a painting of Landa and a 25-minute video in the former San Miguel Arcángel convent in Maní, about 100 kilometers south of Mérida.

The permanent exhibition, with a title that translates as “Friar Diego de Landa: The Bishop and His Legacy,” is housed in a modest space, a room formerly used by the parish priest.

It traces his life from his upbringing in Spain to his tenure as Yucatán’s second bishop.

Born in 1524, Landa was a Franciscan missionary who arrived in Yucatán in 1549 and learned Yucatec Mayan. He became a regional leader of his religious order before becoming bishop.

He is remembered particularly for the July 12, 1562, religious proceeding in Maní known as an auto-da-fé, when Maya manuscripts, codices, religious images and other sacred objects were burned.

Historian John F. Chuchiak IV of Missouri State University researched and curated the exhibition. At last week’s opening, he challenged accounts that Maya people were burned during that event, saying the fire consumed objects and books.

That distinction does not erase the violence of Landa’s broader campaign. Encyclopaedia Britannica reports that about 4,500 Maya were tortured over three months and nearly 200 died.

Several years later in Spain, while his conduct was under investigation, he wrote “Relación de las cosas de Yucatán,” a detailed account of Maya life and religion. He died in Mérida in 1579 at age 54.

The exhibition, organized through the parish and the Archdiocese of Yucatán, also cites documents indicating that, as bishop, Landa opposed forced labor and other abuses of Maya communities.

Parts of the exhibit include QR codes that provide access to translations into Mayan, English and German.

The museum’s hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays, with Monday visits by appointment by calling (997) 155-3601 or (997) 112-9774. The admission price of 60 pesos (US $3.25) includes a tour of the former convent.

With reports from Por Esto, Diario de Yucatán and Yucatán Magazine

World.title: Mexico among leaders in tech exports, ranking fourth among APEC nations
World.content:
Mexico is a leader in the percentage of exports in the medium- and high-tech manufactured goods category, ranking fourth among the 21 Pacific Rim countries gathered at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Shenzhen, China, this week, according to the latest APEC report.

The report shows that 70.6% of goods Mexico exported were in the medium- and high-tech categories, trailing only Taiwan (81.9%), Hong Kong (77.9%) and South Korea (75.6%). That ranking puts Mexico ahead of China (61.6%), the United States (46.5%) and Canada (31.7%).

Overall, trade in medium- and high-tech manufactured goods in the APEC region quadrupled between 2000 and 2025, reaching US$14.6 billion, with Northeast Asia and the Americas combining for over 82% of regional trade in these goods last year.

Mexico also ranked fourth in the region for the share of these goods in its total merchandise imports in 2025, at 61.7%, behind Hong Kong (71.8%), Singapore (64.3%), and Taiwan (62.4%).

High-tech manufacturing is gaining momentum, according to the report, with trade in these products growing faster than overall merchandise trade over the past decade.

Mexico is well positioned to build on its recent success owing to its strong manufacturing sector, skilled workforce and close trade links with Canada and the United States, particularly in high-value-added sectors such as the automotive, semiconductors and digital services industries.

APEC comprises 21 countries which, together, account for around 62% of global GDP and half of global merchandise exports.

The region is projected to grow by 3.4% in 2026, owing to significant investment in technology and trade, which has helped bolster economic activity amid higher energy prices and geopolitical tensions, another APEC report stated. However, growth is expected to fall to 3.1% in 2027.

“Rising energy costs, geopolitical tensions, increased trade restrictions and tighter financial conditions are creating pressures that could weaken growth in the near term,” Carlos Kuriyama, the director of APEC’s Policy Support Unit, stated.

Trade growth will also likely slow due to ongoing geopolitical tensions and trade policy uncertainty. While APEC’s product and service exports will increase by 6.9% in 2026, they are expected to fall to 3.8% in 2027.

President Sheinbaum is in Shenzhen, China, attending the APEC event, marking the first time a Mexican president has attended in three years. Mexico’s participation will give it the opportunity to strengthen relationships, define priorities and build agreements ahead of its hosting of the 35th Economic Leaders’ Meeting in 2028.

With reports from El Economista

World.title: Sheinbaum and Xi mark a ‘new era’ in Mexico-China relations
World.content:
Listen to this article

In a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Tuesday, President Claudia Sheinbaum declared that her visit to China marks “a new era” in Mexico’s relationship with the East Asian country.

She also told the Chinese president and general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party she was “convinced” that the bilateral meeting would “strengthen collaboration” between the Mexican and Chinese governments and the Mexican and Chinese people. In subsequent remarks to reporters, Sheinbaum described her meeting with Xi as “very good” and “very, very frank.”

For his part, Xi told Sheinbaum that China and Mexico are “good friends” and that advancing relations is “important for both countries,” according to a readout published by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The two leaders and members of their respective cabinets met in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting, which starts in the southern Chinese city on Wednesday. Sheinbaum previously met with Xi at the G20 leaders’ summit in Brazil in November 2024.

Mexico seeks to strengthen ties with China in areas including science, technology and clean energy

In public remarks to Xi, Sheinbaum thanked the Chinese president for his invitation to the APEC CEO Summit, at which she spoke on Tuesday.

She noted that Mexico will host the APEC Leaders’ Meeting in 2028 and told Xi it would be a “pleasure” to welcome him to that event.

Sheinbaum said that the Mexico-China relationship is “the result of deep bonds of friendship and shared principles, such as cooperation, development and shared prosperity.”

“Mexico and China share a vision of development and prosperity, and our nations have strengthened their relationship in order to cooperate on a variety of issues,” she said.

“On this occasion, we are interested in strengthening cooperation in areas related to science and technology, agriculture, clean energy, water resources, health and, of course, culture and tourism,” Sheinbaum said.

According to a statement issued by Mexico’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE), Sheinbaum and Xi “highlighted opportunities to deepen bilateral cooperation on health, river cleanup and restoration, sustainable water management, biodiversity conservation, waste management guided by circular economy principles, the fight against climate change and the development of resilient cities, as Shenzhen’s model shows.”

“They also agreed to strengthen scientific cooperation by training talent, conducting joint research in strategic areas such as mathematics, agriculture, biotechnology and clean energy, and developing bilateral initiatives, including the Young Scientists Exchange Program,” the SRE said.

The ministry also said that Sheinbaum and Xi “expressed their desire to keep strengthening” the Mexico-China relationship through the two countries’ Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which was launched by Xi and former Mexican President Enrique Peña Nieto in 2013.

SRE: Sheinbaum and Xi discussed ‘opportunities to deepen trade’

Mexico and China don’t have a free trade agreement, and the former country angered the latter when it imposed new and higher tariffs on Chinese goods at the start of 2026.

Mexico’s tariffs on China — seen in part as an effort to appease U.S. President Donald Trump, who has accused Mexico of being a transshipment hub for Chinese goods — were not mentioned by the SRE or the Chinese Foreign Ministry in their statements.

The SRE did say that the Mexican and Chinese presidents “discussed opportunities to deepen trade,” adding that Sheinbaum “said Mexico is interested in moving toward a more balanced and diversified economic relationship.”

China’s exports to Mexico — which include electronic equipment and electric vehicles — are worth far more than its imports from Mexico, leaving it with a large trade surplus. Some imports from China pose a threat to Mexican manufacturing sectors, giving the Mexican government added incentive to impose higher tariffs on them.

Sheinbaum told reporters in Shenzhen that she and Xi had spoken about increasing Mexico’s exports of various products to China, “from avocados to tequila.”

Asked whether she and the Chinese president spoke about Mexico’s relationship with the United States, the president responded:

“The issue was raised, but we always talk about our trade agreement with the United States, and [say] that we will always do what is best for Mexico.”

Xi says China and Mexico should ‘deepen political mutual trust’

The statement issued by the Chinese Foreign Ministry said that “given the complex and volatile global landscape, advancing China-Mexico relations at a higher level, across wider areas, and in greater depth is important for both countries as they implement their respective national development strategies and promote unity for strength among the Global South.”

The ministry said that in his meeting with Sheinbaum, “President Xi stressed that China and Mexico should first continue to treat each other with sincerity, deepen political mutual trust, keep growing bilateral relations in the right direction, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all areas and at all levels, and work together to ensure the success of events celebrating the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations next year.”

The Chinese Foreign Ministry also said that “Mexico firmly adheres to the one-China principle and attaches great importance to its relations with China.”

“In the course of implementing Plan México, Mexico is ready to strengthen cooperation with China in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, manufacturing, artificial intelligence, agriculture and water conservancy and promote exchanges in health, education, culture and tourism, so as to elevate bilateral relations to a new height,” the ministry added.

While Mexico is clearly seeking to strengthen — and broaden — its relationship with China, Sheinbaum is mindful of the need to safeguard Mexico’s relationship with the United States, its largest trade partner. For example, the president — who will meet with Trump in Shenzhen on Wednesday — has made it clear that Mexico is not seeking a free trade agreement with China, the world’s second largest economy.

One apparent motive for China to seek closer ties with Mexico is the country’s proximity to Beijing’s foremost strategic rival — the United States.

Sheinbaum requests a panda for CDMX’s Chapultepec Zoo

In remarks to reporters after her meeting with Xi, Sheinbaum noted that a Chinese company is supplying trains to Mexico (for the under-construction Mexico City-Pachuca railroad) and reiterated that Mexico is “very interested” in learning more about China’s “smart hospitals.”

México quiere un nuevo panda en el zoológico Chapultepec: Durante su visita a China, Sheinbaum solicitó al presidente Xi Jinping un ejemplar para el zoológico capitalino 🇨🇳🐼🇲🇽 https://t.co/FMPpElrSXv — Quadratín México (@QuadratinMexico) November 17, 2026

She subsequently revealed that she asked Xi for a panda for the Chapultepec Zoo, located in Chapultepec Park in Mexico City.

One panda, a female called Xin Xin, already lives at the zoo. She was born at the Chapultepec Zoo in 1990.

Given that Mexico and China are on friendly terms and seeking even closer ties, it would appear likely that China will grant Sheinbaum’s request for a panda. According to Reuters, since its founding in 1949, “the People’s Republic of China has used panda diplomacy to boost its international image, either by gifting or lending pandas to foreign zoos as goodwill animal ambassadors.”

World.title: Sheinbaum and Canada’s Carney meet in China, reaffirming their support for the USMCA
World.content:
President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met Tuesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, with both expressing firm support for the renewal of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada free-trade agreement (USMCA).

Their support contrasts with mixed signals from different U.S. Cabinet members regarding elements of the agreement, sometimes to the point where the Mexican team may not be sure who they’re negotiating with. Also, U.S. President Donald Trump has cast doubt over whether there will be any renewal at all.

In that light, the bilateral meeting Tuesday brought together two leaders with a common challenge, though each has responded to Trump’s economic aggression (such as tariffs on both countries) in different ways — Sheinbaum seeking common ground on other issues and Carney in full pushback mode.

But those concerns gave way at the meeting to praise for how strong the mutual relationship between Mexico and Canada has grown. Both leaders agreed to deepen that bilateral relationship.

According to official reports, the leaders endorsed their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and highlighted the first anniversary of the Mexico-Canada Action Plan 2025-2028, which has launched scores of initiatives across its four pillars: prosperity, mobility, security and sustainability.

They also stressed the importance of expanding the action plan based on the positive results obtained, particularly in boosting trade and investments between both countries.

“Our trade between Mexico and Canada, Canada and Mexico has increased, and also the investments of Mexican businesses in Canada and of Canadian businesses in Mexico,” Sheinbaum said. “There is an extraordinary relationship.”

According to Canadian official figures, Mexico invested nearly CA $1 billion in mining and food production, while Canadian investments in Mexico reached CA $3.7 billion in the country’s manufacturing, renewable energy, and mining industries.

Moreover, Carney noted that bilateral trade increased 18% this year and 60% in the last five years. “We are already seeing and contemplating many more opportunities for exchanges between us,” he said.

Sheinbaum and Carney also highlighted increased market access for Canadian agricultural and agri-food products, the success of trade missions to both countries, and the potential for further growth in advanced manufacturing, agriculture, critical minerals, energy, pharmaceuticals and transportation.

Beyond trade, the leaders highlighted cooperation to strengthen health security, develop biotechnological production, facilitate labor mobility, and improve the economic well-being of Indigenous peoples.

The USMCA was, in fact, discussed, but no details were provided to the press or public.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: MND local Puerto Vallarta: Troubles and triumphs with City Hall, trash removal and tourism
World.content:
This week, Mexico is commemorating the 116th anniversary of the start of the Mexican Revolution. Meanwhile, Puerto Vallarta’s City Council is waging its own revolution against the mayor. Residents are also up in arms over major lapses in trash collection service. On other fronts, Puerto Vallarta won a significant victory over trash in the sea, and the city defended its spot as one of the top 10 international travel destinations for Thanksgiving.

Rebellion at the City Council

Frustration continues to rise among residents and local leaders in Puerto Vallarta over the mismanagement of city finances and essential public services.

Last week, four City Council members and the city attorney resigned from the Green Party, which holds majority control over city government, to form an independent faction. This came just a day after several other key administrators resigned. In their resignation letter, council members cited financial mismanagement, payroll delays, debt and failures in services such as garbage collection, water, street lighting, road maintenance and security as their reasons.

The independent faction will be led by City Council member Víctor Manuel Bernal Vargas, who committed to continue working from City Hall without “being beholden to the political party that brought them into office.”

Puerto Vallarta Mayor Luis Ernesto Munguía González has been facing increasing scrutiny over his leadership and was recently ranked the second-worst mayor in Mexico in an October survey conducted by Rubrum, a polling firm and intelligence agency headquartered in Mexico City.

Trash collection crisis

City Council members and residents alike are fed up with lapses in trash collection in various parts of the city. Residents of El Remance, Paso Ancho, Benito Juárez, Lomas del Coapinole and other areas mostly outside the tourist zone have reported trash building up for several days to several weeks on street corners (even in front of a day care center in La Bobadilla), causing bad odors and posing a public health hazard.

Angered by trash piling up on their streets, residents of El Remance, Paso Ancho and Benito Juárez set up a traffic blockade of garbage to demand action from the city government. Garbage was cleared from their communities, but the city still lacks a consistent pickup schedule and sufficient points of collection.

The Public Services Department blames aging vehicles and fuel supply issues for why only 26 out of its fleet of 35 garbage trucks are operational. But local business and municipal leaders say the problem is due to financial mismanagement at the city, which has impacted funds for fuel and paying staff.

Trash fishing tournament removes nearly 1.5 tons of garbage

On a more positive note, on Nov. 8, more than 300 people participated in the third annual International Trash Fishing Tournament hosted by local nonprofit Limpia tu Mar. Volunteers removed nearly 1.5 tons of debris from the sea, bringing the total amount of garbage collected to more than 6 tons since the event launched in 2024.

More than 140 people on 28 boats hauled up trash from the bay, while another 130 volunteers conducted cleanup efforts along the hard-to-reach beaches and coastal areas. The event was originally scheduled for Oct. 18, but had to be moved to Nov. 8 due to Hurricane Trudy (which luckily didn’t make landfall).

Limpia tu Mar started the event not just as a one-day cleanup effort, but to draw greater attention to the bigger problem of the impacts of marine waste on local ocean habitats. The group’s aim is to stop plastic waste and other trash from reaching the water in the first place by encouraging responsible disposal of waste and reducing, recycling and reusing nonbiodegradable containers and packaging.

Puerto Vallarta ranks among top destinations for Thanksgiving

Challenges be damned (what city doesn’t have its issues?), Puerto Vallarta remains among the top 10 international travel destinations for Americans for the Thanksgiving holiday, according to Allianz Partners’ 2026 Top Thanksgiving Destinations report. The city ranked eighth this year, down from its third-place ranking in 2025.

Mexico claimed four of the top 10 spots this year, with Cancún ranked No. 1, San José del Cabo second and Mexico City taking 10th place. Restaurants and venues across the city are preparing for the influx of neighbors to the north and offering special Thanksgiving dinners, including at the lush landscape of the Vallarta Botanical Gardens.

I, for one, look forward to hosting my parents from the U.S. over the holiday. An unusual twist, I know; generally it’s the adult children and grandkids visiting the grandparents around here. But seeing as though it’s the season of families getting together over the holidays, in the next events roundup, I’ll share some great all-ages activities and events happening in November and December that are fun for the whole family.

Debbie Slobe is a writer and communications strategist based in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco. She blogs at Mexpatmama.com and is a senior program director at Resource Media. Find her on Instagram and Facebook.

World.title: EU agriculture chief arrives in Mexico with US $5.5B investment strategy
World.content:
The European Union (EU) is preparing to invest 5 billion euros (US $5.5 billion) in strategic sectors in Mexico, European Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Christophe Hansen announced before arriving in Mexico on Monday.

A delegation comprising 120 representatives from 22 European countries is in Mexico through Thursday, meeting with government officials and businesspeople in order to strengthen economic relationships with an investment agenda linked to Mexico’s development priorities.

Hansen said the visit — featuring high-level business leaders representing key sectors of the European agri-food industry — reaffirms the EU’s commitment to a more dynamic and diversified agri-food relationship with Mexico.

“By working together, we can promote more sustainable agri-food value chains and ensure that businesses of all sizes … can benefit from the opportunities offered by our closer cooperation,” he said.

A key objective is to connect European companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, with Mexican importers, distributors and retailers, facilitating contacts and long-term business partnerships.

The meetings will also foster exchanges between the respective agri-food sectors and identify new business opportunities for companies and consumers on both sides, in the context of the modernized EU-Mexico Global Agreement (MGA).

The new investments Hansen announced go beyond agriculture and include the energy, transportation, pharmaceuticals and healthcare sectors. They also include projects related to the circular economy, digital transition, water and biodiversity.

Hansen said nearly US $140 million is currently being allocated through grants and loans to forestry and sustainable agriculture projects, including a $275,000 project aimed at boosting sustainable coffee production, protecting biodiversity and improving economic opportunities for local producers.

🇪🇺🤝🇲🇽 Our modernised agreement with Mexico means fewer barriers, more export opportunities for EU agri-food products ➕protection for 568 European Geographical Indications 🧀🍫 in a trusted & growing market — Christophe Hansen (@CHansenEU) May 27, 2026

Hansen’s visit comes just six months after Mexico and the EU signed the MGA, which aims to significantly facilitate agricultural trade by reducing Mexican tariffs on European agricultural products by 95%.

Hansen said the MGA will also strengthen technical cooperation in sanitary and phytosanitary matters, including food safety, traceability, animal and plant health, as well as the surveillance and control of pests and diseases.

EU agri-food exports to Mexico are valued at US $2.75 billion, he calculated.

The EU is presently Mexico’s third largest trading partner, while Mexico ranks second among the EU’s Latin American trading partners. Mexico-EU trade has quadrupled in the past 25 years.

With reports from El Economista, Mexico Business News and EEAS Newsroom

World.title: At APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, Sheinbaum promotes Plan México to global business leaders
World.content:
President Claudia Sheinbaum promoted Mexico as an investment destination in an address to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday.

In a 13-minute speech, she also touted Plan México — the federal government’s overarching economic and industrial policy — and spoke about a range of initiatives and achievements of her two-year-old administration.

Desde Shenzhen, China, les comparto mi participación en APEC CEO Summit 2026; en representación de México, expusimos a líderes económicos y empresarios del mundo que el desarrollo con bienestar es posible. https://t.co/3AEDA9Wve3 — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 17, 2026

According to a Xinhua news agency article posted to a Chinese government website, the APEC CEO Summit 2026 brings together “business and political leaders from across the Asia-Pacific and beyond to discuss regional economic cooperation and future development.”

“Under the theme ‘To Prosper and Win the Future Together,’ the two-day event has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland,” the article says.

“Participants include representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, as well as heads of several international organizations and representatives of business associations from Russia, the United States and other economies.”

In addition to speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Sheinbaum will attend the APEC Leaders’ Meeting during her visit to Shenzhen. She arrived in the southern Chinese city on Monday and is scheduled to return to Mexico on Friday.

Mexico ‘guarantees’ conditions for investment, says Sheinbaum

Promoting Mexico as a destination for foreign investment, Sheinbaum touted Mexican talent as well as the country’s geographic location and its trade agreements with other nations, among other competitive advantages.

“We have engineers. We are among the top five countries in the world in terms of the number of engineers produced. We have public universities, research centers, highly educated young people and a strong industrial tradition,” she said.

“We have the capacity to participate in major global value chains, but also to innovate and build strategic industries. We have a privileged geographic location, an extensive network of trade agreements, an economy integrated into the world’s major markets, natural resources, expanding infrastructure and, above all, the human talent of a hardworking people,” Sheinbaum said.

“Mexico guarantees conditions for investment, certainty and a long-term vision for development,” she said.

As part of Plan México, the federal government is seeking to attract more foreign investment to Mexico and strengthen and support the country’s vast manufacturing sector.

Foreign direct investment in Mexico reached a record high of almost US $35 billion in the first six months of 2026, but the pace of year-over-year growth, at 2.1%, was not particularly strong.

By speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Sheinbaum had the opportunity to court investment from major companies in APEC economies and beyond.

Three of Mexico’s five leading sources of foreign investment in the first half of 2026 are APEC members, namely the United States, Canada and Australia. Investment from China has increased in recent years, but the East Asian economic powerhouse was not among the top investors in Mexico last year.

Insecurity, uncertainty surrounding the future of the USMCA free trade pact — which the U.S. government has so far declined to extend to 2042 — and Mexico’s controversial judicial reform, which introduced the popular election of judges, are seen as among the factors discouraging investment in Mexico.

US $432-billion Plan México is ‘a vision for the nation,’ says Sheinbaum

At the start of her address, Sheinbaum highlighted that Mexico is the world’s 11th most populous country and 13th largest economy.

“But above all, we are a nation with a history stretching back thousands of years, where Spanish is spoken, but so are 68 indigenous languages,” she said.

Sheinbaum went on to say that Mexico is building its “own” economic model with “roots in our history, our cultural greatness, and the strength, talent and capabilities of our people.”

“This transformation began in 2018. And starting in 2024, with the election of Mexico’s first female president, we gave it a new dimension through Plan México,” she said.

“Plan México is a vision for the nation. It is the decision to turn our capabilities, resources, strategic position, and talent into drivers of development grounded in sovereignty and social justice,” she said.

She said that the plan is based on “five principles,” namely “shared prosperity; energy and food sovereignty; public, private, and public-private investment in infrastructure; incentives for private investment; and environmental responsibility in the face of climate change.”

Sheinbaum also said that Plan México “has a humanist vision” in which “the economy is at the service of the people” rather than the other way around.

“For decades, it was argued that the wealth of a select few had to grow first, and that over time, the benefits would trickle down to the rest of society. In Mexico, we are proving that the path can be very different,” she said.

Sheinbaum said the government and private companies are expected to invest a total of US $432 billion in infrastructure under Plan México between 2024 and 2030.

“We are transforming the country’s productive capacity, connecting regions, bringing markets closer together, improving logistics, and creating jobs,” she said.

“At the same time, we are promoting investment in industry and services through incentives, certainty, streamlined administrative procedures, and new development hubs aligned with each region’s economic strengths. This has enabled us to become the fifth-largest economy in the world in terms of foreign direct investment,” Sheinbaum said.

In her closing remarks, she said she hadn’t traveled to China “just to offer investment opportunities.”

“We came to share a vision for the future,” she said.

“A vision in which Mexico grows and, at the same time, all economies become stronger and prosperity is a shared achievement,” Sheinbaum said.

Sheinbaum touts ‘well-being’ initiatives

In various ways, Sheinbaum’s address at the APEC CEO Summit was similar to her annual government report (informe) speeches, the most recent of which she delivered on Sept. 1. The difference was that her speech in Shenzhen on Tuesday was delivered on the world stage and was directed at international businesspeople and leaders rather than a domestic audience.

In a vast auditorium in China’s tech capital, Sheinbaum acted as cheerleader in chief for Mexico, and also for the fourth transformation (4T) political project she leads. She highlighted that since Andrés Manuel López Obrador — the founder of the 4T — became president eight years ago, Mexico’s minimum wage has increased 154% in real terms and some 17 million people have been lifted out of poverty, according to World Bank data.

Sheinbaum also spoke about Mexico’s various social programs, and declared that her government is establishing a “verdadero estado de bienestar” — a phrase that can be read as a “true welfare state” or, more broadly, a country that prioritizes people’s well-being.

In addition, she highlighted her government’s major investment in highway, rail, electricity, water, port and housing projects.

Sheinbaum’s speech to the APEC CEO Summit came a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to address the event. Li Qingshuang, vice-chairperson of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, said on Sunday that leaders from 12 APEC economies, including Canada, Chile and South Korea, will attend the APEC CEO Summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or participate in panel discussions.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: VidantaWorld unveils US $1.5B luxury theme park in Nuevo Nayarit
World.content:
VidantaWorld has soft-opened BON, a theme park at the VidantaWorld Nuevo Nayarit amusement park, which the company presented as the “first luxury theme park in the world.”

Located 15 minutes from the Puerto Vallarta International Airport, the park is currently open to VidantaWorld guests only, with plans to open to the general public in April 2027.

BON is only the latest addition to the already packed entertainment complex, which features the BON luxury hotel, five additional resorts, three golf courses, a water park and regular Cirque du Soleil performances.

BON, which stands for Beauty of Nature, required an investment of US $1.5 billion and was unveiled to the international tourism industry during the 2026 London World Travel Market (WTM).

The luxury proposal relies on offering a nightly limited capacity “to preserve an uncrowded, luxury-paced experience,” BON said in a statement cited by People magazine. In its initial stage, the park intends to open Tuesday through Saturday from 5 p.m. onward.

“With BON we wanted to propose something different: more space, more time, more service and the freedom to experience everything at your own pace,” Iván Chávez, executive vice president of Grupo Vidanta said at WTM.

Rather than relying on established entertainment franchises, BON’s creative universe boasts seven themed worlds that feature original stories and characters inspired by Mexico’s traditions, pre-Columbian cosmovision, culture and natural environment.

Some of the attractions include The Rise of Soluma, a suspended roller coaster inspired by the jungle and jaguars; Floresta Drop, a drop tower that emulates a 40-meter-high flower stem; Time Quest, a family-friendly ride decorated with pre-Columbian motifs; and Carousel of Colors, featuring local animals and painted alebrijes.

Guests can also enjoy a parade featuring dancers and floats, plus a light and water show on the main lagoon complete with water fountains and mapping.

To develop the project, BON collaborated with some of the world’s leading attraction engineering companies, responsible for popular roller coasters at both Disney and Universal. This includes Vekoma from the Netherlands (Disney World’s Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind), Liechtenstein’s Intamin (Universal Islands of Adventure’s VelociCoaster) and German Mack Rides (Universal Epic Universe’s Stardust Racers).

When finished, the park will boast 20 attractions alongside retail areas, multiple restaurants, lounges and shows.

With reports from El Universal and Travel Mole

World.title: Argentina’s Pampa Sets Up AI Data Centre Arm
World.content:
ARGENTINA · BUSINESS

Pampa Energía, one of Argentina’s largest power generators, has set up a company with the legal power to build AI data centres. Its new single-shareholder company, Pampa AI S.A.U. (a sociedad anónima unipersonal, meaning one owner), was created by a deed signed on 26 October 2026 in Buenos Aires.

The Official Gazette, Argentina’s government legal journal, published the notice on Tuesday 17 November 2026. The notice gives the new company a board and a statute, but it does not link it to any specific site or project.

Pampa Energía has given its AI data-centre ambitions a legal home. The Gazette notice shows who runs it and what it may do, but not who will buy its computing.

Big Picture

Pampa’s chairman, Marcelo Mindlin, has said that the group can offer almost 800 megawatts (MW) of power capacity, available from next year. He said at Argentina Week, an investment-promotion event in Paris, in October 2026 that Pampa has land, water and turbine experience for a data-centre complex in Vaca Muerta, which lies in Neuquén province in Patagonia.

A megawatt is a million watts of power. The 800 MW is generation capacity, not the size of any data centre.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 60.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Vaca Muerta is a large shale gas and oil field in Neuquén, and Pampa is one of the gas producers there. That gas could in principle fuel power plants that feed a data centre.

Pampa AI’s statute lets it do far more than rent out server halls. The notice is silent on which activities come first.

What the Gazette Notice Says

Pampa AI S.A.U. was created by public deed number 803 on 26 October 2026 in Buenos Aires, with its seat at Maipú 1 in the city. S.A.U. stands for sociedad anónima unipersonal, a company with a single shareholder.

That shareholder is Pampa Energía S.A., which subscribes and pays for all of the capital. The amount is 30 million pesos (about US$19,000 at 1,552 pesos per US dollar on 17 November, from the RT market-data service), split into 30 million ordinary shares of 1 peso each.

A long-exposure night view of an oil refinery in Plaza Huincul, Neuquén province. File photo. photo. The YPF refinery at Plaza Huincul, Neuquén province, Argentina, undated. Photo: Juan Mariano, CC0, Wikimedia Commons.

The company is set to run for 99 years from its registration, and its financial year ends on 31 December. Gustavo Mariani is president of Pampa AI, Martín Miliavsky is vice-president and María Carolina Sigwald is a director, according to the notice.

María Agustina Montes is the alternate director, and all board seats run for three financial years. Either the president or the vice-president can act for the company alone.

A supervisory committee, a body that audits the board, has three members plus alternates. Its stated purpose is broad, starting with designing, building, leasing and operating data centres and high-performance computing for AI and cloud services.

Pampa AI may also make, import and sell GPUs (graphics chips used to train AI), servers, racks, cooling and fibre. It may sell computing capacity as a service, including GPU-as-a-Service, which means renting out chip capacity, and AI model training and inference, which means running trained models.

On energy, the company may buy and use natural gas and fuels, and generate, store and trade electricity from any source. It may also act as a market agent in the wholesale electricity market (MEM), subject to the required authorisations.

It may also make financial investments, but not regulated banking. The notice does not say whether registration with the IGJ (Inspección General de Justicia, the Buenos Aires city company registry) is complete, or when it will be.

Live Company Intelligence Pampa Energia SA ADR — the full investor dossier Company overview and the latest Rio Times coverage.

Why Gas and Power Are the Draw

AI data centres run thousands of chips around the clock, so they need firm and affordable power. Chips can be bought, but they are useless without reliable power.

Pampa AI’s statute covers gas purchases, electricity generation and market trading, which fits that logic. The record does not say whether the site would run on gas or the grid.

What It Means for You

Pampa Energía’s shares trade in Buenos Aires and as American depositary receipts (ADRs, US-listed certificates for foreign shares) in New York under the ticker PAM. Its shareholders now own a group with a new AI arm.

The US$19,000 starting capital is a first step, not a budget for a data-centre build. Treat it as a signal of intent until customers, costs and approvals appear.

For US readers, the wider point is the global hunt for power to run AI. Argentina’s gas is one place such companies could look, and the Argentina hub tracks how that story develops.

What to Watch

Watch for the IGJ registry entry, which the notice does not date. Watch also for any named customer, partner or chip supplier.

Watch for a disclosed project cost and start date, and for the authorisations the statute mentions for electricity trading. A capital increase well above 30 million pesos (about US$19,000) would signal a step beyond paperwork.

What Is Not Known

The notice does not say whether any customer, partner or chip supplier is signed. It gives no project cost, no start date and no regulatory approvals.

The 30 million pesos (about US$19,000) is a starting amount, not a funding plan. The notice also says nothing about how much power a data centre would need.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Pampa AI?

Pampa AI S.A.U. is a new subsidiary of Pampa Energía, created on 26 October 2026 with the powers to build and operate AI data centres. Its sole shareholder is Pampa Energía S.A.

How much capital does Pampa AI have?

Pampa AI has 30 million pesos (about US$19,000), in 30 million ordinary shares of 1 peso. Pampa Energía subscribed and paid all of it.

Is the data-centre project funded or approved?

The notice does not say. It names no customer, project cost, start date or regulatory approval, and it does not say whether registration with the IGJ is complete.

Why build AI data centres in Vaca Muerta?

Pampa has said it can offer almost 800 MW of capacity from next year, and says it has land for a project in Vaca Muerta. Vaca Muerta also offers gas that could fuel generation.

Sources: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina, second section, 17 November 2026, notice 85689/26.

World.title: Chile’s Ripley Profit Jumps 53% on Its Bank
World.content:
CHILE · MARKETS

Chile’s Ripley Corp, a group of department stores, a consumer bank and shopping malls in Chile and Peru, grew third-quarter profit 53.2% to 5.787 billion pesos (about US$5.8 million). Ripley said in its results statement on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, that its bank did the heavy lifting.

The department stores in Chile did not. Their revenue fell 7.0% as the company cited higher unemployment, inflation and fuel prices.

Ripley’s bank and its Peruvian arm lifted profit in a tougher quarter for Chilean shoppers. The stores shrank, and the bank’s rising provisions are the number to follow.

Big Picture

Ripley is a Chilean retail and financial group. It runs department stores, a bank and shopping malls in Chile and Peru, and its shares trade in Santiago.

Ripley reported earlier that it closed 2025 with a record profit of about 119.2 billion pesos (about US$120 million). It also reported earlier that second-quarter 2026 profit rose about 60%.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 62.9 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Ripley Reported

Net profit was 5.787 billion pesos (about US$5.8 million), up 53.2% from about 3.8 billion pesos (about US$3.8 million) a year earlier. Revenue rose 3.7% to 512.644 billion pesos (about US$517 million).

EBITDA, which is operating earnings before interest, tax and depreciation, rose 5.6% to 35.743 billion pesos (about US$36 million). The EBITDA margin, which is EBITDA as a share of revenue, was 7.0% against 6.8% a year earlier.

A shopping arcade in central Santiago. File photo.
