World.title: Estonian parties take different views on restoring border control with Latvia
World.content:
According to EKRE Chairman Martin Helme, the party has repeatedly called for Estonia's eastern border to be closed. Helme suspects the government decided to close the border in the hope of boosting its approval ratings.

"It is particularly embarrassing to watch this farce over the eastern border when EKRE has repeatedly demanded since the summer that not only the eastern border but also the border with Latvia be brought under control. That is where those saboteurs and provocateurs came from who, according to the Internal Security Service, were carrying a GRU identification card and an operational plan. Not across the eastern border, but across the southern border. Just as hundreds of illegal immigrants have crossed from there unchecked whom the police are trying to apprehend every day. Yet the government is unwilling even to discuss closing the southern border, let alone bringing it under control," Helme wrote on social media.

"To the jokers in the government: Now that you've finally found your backbone and common sense, do us all a favor and bring the entire border under control. If that doesn't happen, all this huffing and puffing about closing the eastern border can only be seen as a pre-election circus. An exercise in futility. There is certainly no security dimension to it, nor can there be as long as the southern border remains open," he added.

SDE head: Closing the Estonia-Latvia border very resource-intensive

Social Democratic Party Chairman and former Interior Minister Lauri Läänemets said closing the Estonian-Latvian border would require substantial resources and that he does not consider it the most sensible solution.

"Since we don't have a border fence there either, it would mean deploying significantly more personnel. In fact, it would have the same effect on the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) as during the COVID-19 pandemic when many officers who were investigating various cases or dealing with migration issues, including foreign labor, had to take turns guarding the border. This means the PPA's other activities would have to be scaled back or put on hold," Läänemets said.

"Partial border controls could be reinstated, but they have significant gaps, especially along land borders, and mainly involve spot checks or increased inspections at border crossing points. Yes, this could be done and it has been implemented before," Läänemets said.

The SDE leader believes that instead of increasing border controls, Estonia should invest more in the counterintelligence capabilities of the Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/KAPO) and the response capabilities of the Police and Border Guard Board.

"That would be cheaper and more effective because it would be more precisely targeted. And ultimately, we wouldn't be stretching our police resources too thin," Läänemets said.

He predicted that closing the eastern border could prompt Russia to create migration pressure along Estonia's border as well.

"If we completely close the Estonian-Russian border — which is a very sensible move in this case — we may find ourselves facing increased migration pressure on that border at some point. One possible reason why Russia has not previously generated migration pressure in this way is that the border crossing points have remained open," Läänemets said.

"So we need to consider all possible future scenarios and target our measures more precisely. I think closing the Latvian border would not achieve the desired effect but would instead waste our resources unnecessarily," Läänemets added.

Center: Temporarily restoring checks on southern border worth considering

Center Party Chairman Mihhail Kõlvart said that, as with the eastern border, border controls along Estonia's southern border should not be a matter of political debate, particularly since genuine threats to Estonia have already come through Latvia.

"In my view, this is not even a political question but a matter of basic logic. If we close the eastern border because there is a threat that could cross it, then in the case of the Latvian border, we know that this threat — not a theoretical threat, but actual attacks — has already materialized. Not to mention that illegal migrants are also entering through Latvia. This is not yet a crisis, but it is always better to prevent a crisis than to deal with its consequences afterward. So I think this is an entirely objective issue: We need to discuss it with our Latvian counterparts, but also consider temporarily reinstating border controls," Kõlvart said.

"If we are currently taking preventive measures along one border, it makes sense to do the same along the other," Kõlvart added.

"As for resources, closing the eastern border would free up some of them. How border controls should be reinstated is, again, not something for politicians to decide. Whether that means restoring full border controls, conducting spot checks, increasing the number of patrols and so on — these are matters for experts in the relevant field to discuss. But when it comes to security, threats and potential crises, strengthening border controls is an entirely logical step at this point," Kõlvart said.

According to Kõlvart, closing the eastern border is not a political question either.

"If we identify an escalation in the situation and threats that could come across the border have also been identified — based on assessments by the relevant authorities, primarily the Estonian Internal Security Service — then we are dealing with an objective situation. And if this measure is necessary to ensure our security, then it must be implemented," Kõlvart said.

Isamaa leader: Border control suitable measure as migration pressure persists

Isamaa Chairman Urmas Reinsalu also said closing the eastern border would free up resources to strengthen the southern border, primarily to curb illegal migration pressure from Latvia.

"If we assume that the pressure will continue — primarily from Belarus, but also through Russia, with people being brought illegally into Latvian territory — and that this border cannot be secured, then introducing additional border control procedures within the Schengen Area would clearly be an entirely legitimate, appropriate and proportionate measure. A number of European countries, including Germany and Austria, have done this. It does not mean that such controls would be applied across the board, but rather according to the threat assessment. Isamaa is open to this option if less restrictive measures fail to stop illegal migration," Reinsalu said.

"However, we do not have a specific proposal. I think it is important for the government to prepare its own assessment of why such a large number of people have entered Estonian territory illegally, why these spot checks have failed to stem the flow of people and what the outlook is for the future," Reinsalu added.

"If this migration flow has continued since the summer, then clearly more needs to be done. One option is to introduce border controls, while another is to implement other control and surveillance measures," Reinsalu said.

Addressing reports that some Latvian citizens had entered Estonia to carry out acts of sabotage, Reinsalu said that because they are European Union citizens, they must be apprehended through means other than border controls.

Reform: Solution in cooperation with Latvia, not border checks

Mati Raidma of the Reform Party, a member of the Riigikogu National Defense Committee, said he does not see reinstating border controls between Estonia and Latvia as an option.

"Cooperation between the Estonian and Latvian security services is very effective, as can be seen in the resolution of all these cases. In reality, the key to addressing today's challenges lies in good cooperation and mutual assistance, not in closing the border," Raidma said.

"Close cooperation between the Estonian and Latvian security services is what allows us to keep the situation under control and thwart all kinds of plans at the earliest possible stage. These activities are not being orchestrated by the Latvian state, but by Russia and its intelligence services. That is where the real enemy lies," Raidma added.

Eesti 200 whip: Border control seems excessive

Toomas Uibo, chairman of the Eesti 200 parliamentary group, said that although the group has not discussed the issue, he personally believes there is currently no need for border controls.

"At the moment, it does seem like a somewhat excessive measure. Of course, we need to keep an eye on developments. If it becomes justified at some point, then naturally it should be done. Experts are better placed to make that assessment than politicians," Uibo said.

Interior minister: Government far from weighing border control

Interior Minister and Eesti 200 member Igor Taro said he does not believe any of the conditions that would warrant seriously considering the reinstatement of border controls between Estonia and Latvia have been met.

"We are nowhere near a crisis situation or anything that would require the introduction of full-scale border controls along the Latvian border," Taro told ERR.

"To actually restore border controls between Estonia and Latvia as they once existed, we would have to build infrastructure along the entire border. We would have to reinstate checkpoints on roads, but we obviously couldn't leave fields and forests unguarded. Restoring such border controls would cost around €300 million in investment alone, based on current construction costs, such as those incurred in building the Estonian-Russian border infrastructure," Taro said.

According to Taro, this would not be a practical use of resources at present.

"We have successfully dealt with illegal immigration, apprehended everyone who has attempted to travel through Estonia or enter the country illegally and, most recently, successfully thwarted an attempted act of sabotage involving individuals recruited in Latvia. This was possible thanks to very good cooperation with Latvia's security services and law enforcement agencies. Through this cooperation, we are able to keep the situation along the Latvian border well under control and mitigate risks without having to seriously consider building new border infrastructure between Estonia and Latvia," Taro said.

Addressing suggestions of introducing spot checks or more limited border controls, Taro said that compensatory measures under the Schengen framework are already in place.

"We have 50 patrols operating across Estonia, monitoring everything, including traffic coming from Latvia. There is no need for a vehicle to be stopped at a former border crossing point. We can apprehend illegal migrants attempting to pass through without obstructing the movement of ordinary law-abiding people or having to maintain a visible presence directly on the road at the Estonian-Latvian border," Taro added.

The debate follows the detention of eight Latvian citizens after an attempted arson at Estonian drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which Estonia's domestic intelligence service has attributed to Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU. Estonia is weighing closing its eastern border in response.

World.title: Estonia's youth jobs paradox: Firms struggle to find workers
World.content:
Estonian employers report staff shortages despite high youth unemployment, pointing to a mismatch between the skills young people have and those companies need.

Youth unemployment reached 23.7 percent in the third quarter, as employers struggled to fill technical, healthcare and education jobs.

Estonia's overall unemployment rate rose to 7.9 percent in the third quarter as employment fell. Young people were among the hardest hit, with youth employment down 5,400 year on year.

Employers say they see the same paradox from the other side. Hando Sutter, CEO of the Estonian Employers' Confederation, said that while employment in Estonia is "quite high", so too is youth unemployment, which is among the highest rates in Europe. At the same time, companies have been complaining of staff shortages.

"There is certainly more than one reason for this," Sutter said. He noted that young people are being trained in fields and occupations where there are fewer opportunities in the labor market. These tend to be less technical fields, he said. Demand is high in manufacturing, however, where employers are looking for people in engineering, mechanics and energy.

Hando Sutter. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Sutter, a former board chair of state-owned generator Eesti Energia, added there is also strong demand for workers in healthcare, while teachers are needed too. He said work can almost always be found in these areas. "We have a slight mismatch between supply and demand," he said.

"We have also discussed the quality of young people's training, which may be lacking in at least some fields," Sutter said. He added that employers also need to do more to support young people. An increasing number of companies in Estonia are taking on interns to help young people take their first step from education into employment and make the transition smoother.

Sutter noted that work processes are becoming increasingly complex as more technology is introduced. "I don't just mean artificial intelligence, but automation in general," he explained. With work becoming more complex, fewer simple entry-level jobs are available across the board. "For this reason, we need workers to have better skills and knowledge when entering the labor market," he said.

Social skills are also important, Sutter noted, as employees increasingly need to work in teams and interact with people across different teams. "Young people are still acquiring all of these skills," he said.

Estonia's unemployment rate has fluctuated in recent quarters amid weak economic conditions and declining employment. Young people have been particularly affected, with youth unemployment reaching 23.7 percent in the third quarter, while employment among those aged 25–64 remained relatively stable. Economists have pointed to factors including AI, remote working and employers' preference for experienced staff as contributing to weaker job prospects for younger workers.

World.title: President: Closing Estonian-Russian border cannot be an emotional decision
World.content:
Decisions on whether to close the Estonian-Russian border must be made based on an analysis of the economic, humanitarian, diplomatic and security implications, President Ülle Madise said.

While all tourism and cross-border shopping for cheap goods must come to an end, Madise believes diplomatic and humanitarian travel must remain possible and Estonia must avoid taking steps that may be emotionally satisfying but ultimately harmful to the country.

Commenting on the government's discussions about closing road border crossings on Estonia's eastern border, Madise said public outrage over the enemy's actions is understandable, but responsible statesmanship requires sober consideration.

"I hope an analysis of the economic, humanitarian, diplomatic and security consequences of this decision will be completed, that I will also have an opportunity to read it and that the decision will be made on the basis of that analysis," Madise said.

"The emotion behind issuing such a message is entirely understandable. Who among us wouldn't want to take action when they've caused some kind of trouble yet again? By 'they,' I naturally mean our enemies. But is this the right response? Is it proportionate? Does it serve Estonia's interests internationally as well? Sometimes, in an emotional moment, those questions go unasked. But they need to be asked and answered with a clear head," Madise said.

The president said that even when public pressure is aimed at provoking decision-makers into making mistakes, the difficulty of being a decision-maker and the burden of statesmanship lie precisely in making decisions that benefit Estonia while resisting those that may be emotionally satisfying but ultimately harmful.

President Ülle Madise. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Attacks would have happened despite closed borders

Asked why Estonia had not closed its border earlier, as Finland had done, Madise explained that the circumstances were different and that keeping the border open had benefited Estonia.

Madise also said closing the border would not have prevented recent attacks targeting Estonian companies.

"Finland's situation when it made its decisions was entirely different. Keeping the border open has been very beneficial to Estonia," the president said.

"It is always worth considering whether any of the incidents that have occurred here — I mean, for example, the attack on Milrem or the recent attempted attacks on Threod — would have been prevented if the border had been closed. The answer is a definite no. There may be other considerations, but as I said, I believe an analysis of all conceivable consequences and impacts is being prepared. I hope the government will examine that analysis thoroughly," the president said.

Madise noted that the government must also consider information that is not fully known to the public, including the recruitment of individuals during border crossings and the ability of security agencies to address potential threats.

"It is entirely natural to consider such incidents, as well as matters that may not be fully known to the public. For example, how many people are recruited to engage in activities against Estonia while crossing the border or because crossing the border is relatively easy? The details of that may not be publicly known," Madise said.

"The government needs to bring all this information together and weigh the public's emotional expectations against the actual consequences, as well as the Estonian Internal Security Service's actual ability to deal with potential negative effects. I would also very much like to commend the Police and Border Guard Board, the Internal Security Service, the Prosecutor's Office and our Latvian partners because the incidents we have experienced here have been brought under control very quickly, in the sense that the perpetrators have been identified. I also want to thank all the companies that have implemented the necessary security measures," Madise said.

Madise added that while the situation required preparedness, she sees no reason to interfere in other countries' border policies or reinstate border controls along Estonia's southern border. Asked whether Madise had questioned the Latvian president about why Latvia had not closed its eastern border, the president replied: "Of course not."

President Ülle Madise. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Madise pointed out that Poland also keeps its border crossings open and that Estonia must take into account essential travel by diplomats and ordinary people alike.

"Poland also keeps these border crossings open and please don't forget that diplomats need to travel. People also need to travel for humanitarian reasons — people who have very elderly parents on the other side of the border and cannot bring them here or go there themselves or who have children there. There are also jobs to consider. Yes, this creates additional work for the Internal Security Service, but that work needs to be done. We all have to do our jobs," the president said.

At the same time, Madise stressed that ordinary tourism and shopping trips across the eastern border were unjustified and that the government could tighten restrictions based on its analysis.

President Ülle Madise. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"My message is also clear: All tourism and trips simply to buy cheap goods should have ended long ago and must be stopped. I wouldn't rule out the possibility that, after reviewing all the analyses, the government will decide to impose further restrictions on border crossings, specifically on travel that is not necessary for humanitarian or diplomatic reasons. But let's wait and see. Everyone has their own job to do and this decision is the government's responsibility. I strongly recommend approaching it with a clear head and setting emotions aside," Madise said.

Addressing concerns about Narva's future and economic situation, Madise urged calm and highlighted the international presence in the border city. According to Madise, Frontex Deputy Executive Director Uku Sarekanno has confirmed that 60 employees of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, along with their families, are currently staying in Narva and Narva-Jõesuu to assess developments at the border.

"I wouldn't want to get carried away with overly gloomy thoughts," Madise said when discussing Narva's prospects.

"Let's remain calm. What is very important is that the message is clear: Estonia is worth investing in, it is worth building factories here and it is worth coming here to work. Those who already live here should feel that it is worth staying if they wish to do so. We must under no circumstances send a message that there are now extremely serious threats or that the situation is so difficult that people should avoid investing here at all costs. I think Narva is a really great city. It has tremendous potential. Right now, it simply takes a lot of courage to establish a home and a business there," Madise said.

Vikerraadio Editor-in-Chief Janek Luts welcomes President Ülle Madise. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

World.title: Estonia backs EU deportation center in Rwanda but won't join
World.content:
Five European Union member states are planning to establish a deportation center in Rwanda where people without a legal basis to remain in Europe could be sent in the future. Estonia supports the concept behind the pilot project but is not currently participating in it.

Under the proposed plan, a deportation center would be established in Rwanda, located in central Africa. It would accommodate individuals who have exhausted all legal avenues to challenge their removal from Europe.

According to the initial plan, about 100 people could be transferred to the center as early as the beginning of next year. The project is being spearheaded by Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark and the Netherlands, whose representatives met Monday in Vienna.

Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the agreement with Rwanda opens new opportunities.

"In the European Union, asylum seekers whose applications have been definitively rejected will in future be directed to these return centers. We want to deprive migrant smugglers of their inhumane business model and thereby prevent deaths in the Mediterranean and on other dangerous migration routes. Third, we want to reduce the burden on our reception systems, which have been under enormous pressure from migration flows in recent years," Stocker said.

Migrants housed at the deportation center would then be able to decide whether to return to their home country, remain in Rwanda or move to a country where they have a legal right to reside. The idea of establishing such centers has been supported by more than half of EU member states, including Estonia, said Janek Mägi, head of the Border Guard and Migration Department at the Ministry of the Interior.

Janek Mägi, Siseministeeriumi piirivalve - ja rändepoliitika osakonna juhataja Autor/allikas: Arp Müller / ERR

"The interior minister and foreign minister have repeatedly signed joint appeals asking the European Union to amend legislation and adopt measures that would make it possible to establish return centers. As a result, the new return regulation includes provisions allowing such centers to be created outside the EU. We cannot say there is extensive case law behind this yet, but it was done deliberately and the legal framework was adjusted accordingly," Mägi said.

Mägi added that Estonia has participated in the project's working group from the beginning. However, Estonia is not taking part in the Rwanda pilot at this stage because its deportation system is relatively successful compared with those of other European countries. In addition, most people deported from Estonia currently travel eastward.

"The number of people we deport each year remains below 100. Of those, we can say that we successfully deport almost all of them, with only a few problematic cases. Compared with the rest of Europe, our success rate is more than three times higher. But of course we see potential in this approach because the nationalities of those subject to deportation and the complexity of these cases are only increasing over time. This is one way to reduce pressure on Estonia and carry out deportations more successfully," Mägi explained.

Estonia could therefore join the pilot project at any time. For now, the five participating countries are funding it. The eventual cost of the project remains unclear.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen expressed hope that the creation of such a center would also send a deterrent message.

"The message we are sending is that people can no longer enter the European Union illegally and assume they can simply stay. I believe this message will discourage many people and cause thousands to think carefully before beginning the journey to Europe," Frederiksen said.

According to Mägi, the long-term goal is to make it possible to finance such centers through EU funds.

The initiative has been criticized by human rights organizations and some politicians.

The United Kingdom abandoned its own plan to send asylum seekers to Rwanda after the country's Supreme Court ruled it unlawful in 2023.

World.title: Hipodroomi intersection to open to traffic in both directions over winter
World.content:
The Hipodroomi intersection in Tallinn's Kristiine is set to reopen both lanes on Paldiski maantee over winter, and construction work will resume next spring.

The outbound lanes of Paldiski maantee will be completed by the end of November, allowing traffic to reopen in both directions along the entire construction section for the winter period, including at the Merimetsa tee intersection.

Construction work will continue next spring on the inbound lanes, when traffic in both directions will be diverted onto the completed outbound roadway.

Public transport stops will also be fully restored by the end of November. The city also wants to restore sidewalk access over the winter.

Deputy Mayor for Transport Joel Jesse said the work is on schedule.

"For the winter period, we will be able to ease restrictions and ensure full traffic flow in both directions in the area. However, it must be remembered that the reconstruction of the intersection is not yet complete, and work will resume in the spring, bringing further traffic changes," he said.

Reconstruction of the inbound lanes of Paldiski maantee will begin by March 1, 2027, and is expected to finish in July.

The Hipodroomi intersection is being reconstructed to better connect the new residential and commercial district with the rest of the city, and to improve traffic safety. Construction work is scheduled to be completed by the end of August 2027.

World.title: Tallinn bar security guards sentenced to 13 years for robberies
World.content:
Harju District Court on Tuesday found 30-year-old Ruslan Hrapko and 26-year-old Vladislav Kirillov guilty of assaulting and robbing intoxicated people while working as security guards at bars in Tallinn's Old Town. The court sentenced both men to 13 years in prison.

According to the prosecution, the men used their positions as security guards at several Old Town bars in 2024 to rob intoxicated patrons.

Prosecutors said the men targeted heavily intoxicated people in bars and on the streets of the Old Town who were unable to resist and from whom it was easy to steal phones, wallets and other valuables. When necessary, they used violence, including pepper spray and handcuffs.

The defendants were also accused of unlawfully depriving people of their liberty on several occasions, making threats and committing computer fraud.

Senior Prosecutor Kelly Kruusimägi. Source: ERR

According to Senior Prosecutor Kelly Kruusimägi, these were not random altercations associated with Tallinn's nightlife but repeated and deliberate crimes in which the authority and appearance of a security guard were used for criminal purposes.

Hisko Vares, head of the investigative department of the Lääne-Harju Police Station, said that the crimes were particularly cynical because the victims were targeted by people they should have been able to trust for protection and assistance.

The prosecution sought 13-year prison sentences for both defendants, and the court agreed. The court also ordered the confiscation of a Mercedes-Benz Vito belonging to Kirillov, which, according to the evidence, was used in the commission of the crimes. The convicted men must also pay compensation to the victims.

Five other people were charged in the same criminal case for participating in individual incidents or assisting in the crimes. In February, Harju District Court sentenced them under plea agreements to suspended prison terms ranging from eight months to three years and six months.

The ruling has not yet entered into force and may be appealed.

A bar in Tallinn. Photo is illustrative. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

World.title: Nvidia doubles revenue in third quarter, exceeding expectations
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO, United States: American chip giant Nvidia doubled revenue in its third quarter to more than $115 billion, the company reported Tuesday amid a scandal that forced out its charismatic CEO Jensen Huang.

The results exceeded analysts’ expectations but questions loom over the company after Huang resigned last week over allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy who might have funneled restricted chips to China.

For the first time in nearly 28 years, since the Santa Clara, California-based company’s IPO, Huang was not at the helm for the quarterly earnings call.

Instead, investors heard from Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, appointed interim CEO following Huang’s resignation on Thursday.

It’s “business as usual” at Nvidia, Kress said on the call, seeking to reassure investors and customers that the company is stable after the leadership shakeup.

The champion of semiconductors for artificial intelligence once again exceeded expectations, both in terms of revenue and net income, which reached $65.3 billion.

Nvidia also increased its forecast for next year’s revenue, which Kress said they expected to grow by 75 percent, up from 70 percent.

“Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital,” Kress said on the call.

Its revenue will also get a boost from major AI labs, such ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and Claude-maker Anthropic.

“We expect the major frontier labs to contribute approximately 15 percent of our data center revenue this year,” Kress said.

Earnings per share, the benchmark metric on Wall Street, came in at $2.77, compared to the $2.48 anticipated by analysts. The market reacted positively, and in after-hours trading, the stock rose by just over 2 percent.

Board won’t reinstate Huang

However, the surge should be viewed in perspective as the company has lost more than a quarter of its market capitalization since the initial revelations concerning Huang in late October.

“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating, our supply is growing, our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We’ve got this,” Kress said at the end of Tuesday’s call.

Huang, 63, was caught up in three adultery cases, two of which involved subordinates.

The third involved a Chinese businesswoman accused of shipping Nvidia chips to China despite a US embargo. US intelligence also suspected this entrepreneur, Alice Huang, of spying for China.

On Tuesday, a few hours before the results were released, Huang said he was ready to return to the helm of the group he co-founded if the board of directors offered him the position.

But Chairman Harvey Jones said the company does not plan to bring Huang back.

“The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said on the earnings call. He refused to address the circumstances of Huang’s resignation but said he would communicate further when appropriate.

Jones said the board wants to install a new CEO as quickly as possible, “but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.”

Huang has agreed to meet with US lawmakers on December 1 to answer about chips and national security concerns.

World.title: US push for $50 billion for aviation modernization faces Republican opposition
World.content:
WASHINGTON: A number of Republican senators said on Tuesday they would not support the Trump administration’s request for $50 billion for air traffic control reforms and airport improvements but were willing to support a more limited safety-focused request.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had asked on Friday for $30 billion — including $18 billion for airports — but raised that to $50 billion after a nationwide ground stop blamed on a single router resulted in the cancelation of more ‌than 18,000 flights.

“I’ll take ‌what I can get, and I will ​work ‌with ⁠the Congress to ​make ⁠sure that we do the highest priorities first,” Duffy said at a press conference on Tuesday following a weekly policy luncheon with Republican senators. “I’m going to build with whatever they give me.”

Congress last year approved $12.5 billion and only about 30 percent has been spent, senators said.

Duffy faced some hostile questions from Republican senators during the lunch who questioned the price tag, Senate aides said.

Democrats say they ⁠want more answers about what went wrong on Friday before ‌they approve more funds.

Some Republicans also said ‌airlines or other users of the system should ​pay part of the upgrade ‌costs. “I’m not going to vote to provide them money to help local ‌airports,” Republican Senator John Kennedy said, saying it was a “huge mistake” to go from $30 billion to $50 billion.

Senator Rand Paul said he did not understand how the price tag jumped to $50 billion. “The bottom line: we shouldn’t just throw money at a problem,” Paul said.

Republican ‌Senator Rick Scott said he thinks another $10 billion is needed to fix air traffic control systems. “Congress has a role ⁠to play, but ⁠the airlines need to put up money and have skin in this game too. And yes, they can do it without raising ticket prices,” Scott said.

Republican Senator Jon Husted said aviation system users could pay for the improvements. He suggested a small fee “so taxpayers who are not flying don’t have to foot the bill.”

Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Republicans asked questions about the $50 billion figure and noted the earlier $30 billion ask. “We will see what the traffic will bear, what’s achievable,” Thune said.

Senate Commerce Committee Chair Ted Cruz said he expected more money for safety-related improvements would be funded ​but said the message from Congress ​last year was “demonstrate that you can actually modernize and come back to Congress when you need additional funds.”

World.title: Iraq resumes oil exports through Turkish pipeline after 12-year break
World.content:
LONDON: After a 12-year hiatus, Iraq has resumed pumping oil through a Turkish pipeline at an initial capacity of 120,000 barrels per day, as the conflict between the US and Iran continues to disrupt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said on Tuesday that it planned gradually to increase export capacity to 500,000 barrels a day.

Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said the reopening of the 960-kilometer Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline followed maintenance and rehabilitation work, and technical and operational testing. It was forced offline by Daesh attacks in 2014.

“This achievement represents an important strategic step towards strengthening Iraq’s export capacity and diversifying crude oil export outlets, in addition to generating additional financial revenues for the national economy,” Khudair said.

He added that exports through this northern route allowed Iraq to sell crude oil at market prices without discounts, the Iraqi News Agency reported.

Iraq’s southern oil terminals have been affected by the Iran war, which began in late February, as Tehran has effectively blocked tankers from using the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq is the second-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, after Saudi Arabia. About 0.5 percent of the global oil supply passed through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline before it was closed down in 2014 due to repeated attacks by Daesh.

World.title: Kuwait under hostile drone attacks, says army
World.content:
RIYADH: Kuwait’s air defenses are countering hostile drone attacks, the army said on Wednesday.

In a statement posted on X, the General Staff of the Army said “any explosions heard are the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks” and requested that everyone comply with “security and safety instructions.”

The Gulf nation has been under attack from Iranian missiles and drones during the war launched by the US and Israel on Tehran.

Targets have included Kuwait International Airport, oil refineries and the Shuaiba power and desalination plant.

Last week, GCC defense ministers approved the launch of an advanced command for the Unified Military Command in Kuwait and allocated appropriate forces to it.

World.title: Crown prince chairs Saudi Cabinet session
World.content:
RIYADH: The Cabinet discussed the content of talks held in recent days between Saudi Arabia and friendly nations to broaden the prospects for bilateral and multilateral cooperation across various fields.

The talks aimed to support all efforts that help consolidate the foundations of security and peace in the region, the stability of energy markets, and the safety of maritime corridors and freedom of navigation, thereby preserving the smooth flow of global trade and supply chains.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman chaired the meeting in Riyadh.

In a statement to the Saudi Press Agency following the session, Minister of Media Salman Al-Dossary said the Cabinet reviewed the state’s overall work and the progress and successes achieved on various fronts despite the successive circumstances and shifts the world is witnessing, particularly in the regional environment.

The Kingdom is moving ahead to strengthen its capabilities and address emerging developments and challenges to safeguard its development gains and national achievements, along with its standing among nations and its active role regionally and internationally.

The Cabinet reviewed the latest developments in the national economy and the resilience it has shown in adapting to varying circumstances, underpinned by progress in diversifying sources of growth within the framework of Saudi Vision 2030 and by reforms that have sustained the continued expansion of non-oil activities.

It also noted the continued containment of inflation at low levels, support for investment, the expansion of private sector opportunities, the capacity of public finances to respond to change, and sustained spending on essential services and development projects.

The Cabinet commended the Kingdom’s continued achievements across various international indicators and the advanced global positions it has attained in a number of pillars and criteria related to artificial intelligence under the World Digital and AI Ranking issued by the International Institute for Management Development.

These results reflect the national data ecosystem’s efforts to build capabilities, stimulate investment, and develop regulatory frameworks.

The Cabinet deemed the Kingdom’s election to membership of the Council of the International Telecommunication Union an extension of its role in developing the communications, space, and technology sector and in helping to lead digital transformation globally, opening broad horizons in the service of people, the drivers of development, and the fields of innovation and artificial intelligence.

The Cabinet addressed other items on its agenda and issued several decisions, including the following:

First:

Authorizing the minister of energy, or a deputy, to discuss and sign a draft memorandum of understanding for cooperation in renewable energy with the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA).

Second:

Approving a memorandum of understanding between the Saudi Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources Canada for cooperation in the field of energy.

Third:

Authorizing the chairman of the board of directors of the King Abdulaziz Foundation (Darah), or a deputy, to discuss and sign a draft memorandum of understanding for scientific cooperation with the Institute of Manuscripts of the Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences.

Fourth:

Authorizing the minister of Islamic affairs, dawah and guidance, or a deputy, to discuss and sign a draft memorandum of understanding in Islamic affairs with the Ministry of Justice of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Fifth:

Authorizing the minister of environment, water and agriculture and chairman of the board of directors of the Saudi Water Authority, or a deputy, to discuss and sign a draft memorandum of understanding on integrated water resources management with PUB, Singapore’s National Water Agency.

Sixth:

Approving a memorandum of understanding between the Saudi Oversight and Anti-Corruption Authority and the Financial Crimes Commission of the Republic of Mauritius for cooperation in preventing and combating corruption and related crimes.

Seventh:

Approving two memoranda of understanding for cooperation in radio and television broadcasting between the Saudi Broadcasting Authority and the General Authority for Radio and Television of the Syrian Arab Republic and the National Television and Radio Broadcasting Corporation of the Kyrgyz Republic.

Eighth:

Amending the Code of Law Practice to allow foreign law firms to establish a professional company in the Kingdom, subject to a set of regulations.

Ninth:

Implementing two resolutions of the Supreme Council of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), adopted at its 41st session held in AlUla Governorate, approving the Gulf general framework for the public health plan for emergency preparedness and response and the early health warning system guide.

World.title: At hearing, US Navy chief blasted over Iran war and its toll on sailors
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Democratic lawmakers tore into President Donald Trump’s acting head of the Navy on Tuesday, accusing him of being a Trump “yes man” on the Iran ​war and downplaying its toll on sailors’ mental health after eight suicide attempts on an aircraft carrier.

The contentious hearing during the waning days of the Republican-led Senate could be a preview of what’s to come when Democrats take control in January after victories in midterm elections earlier this month.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, who is seeking to win Senate confirmation to keep the job, did not directly respond to some of the toughest questions before the Senate Armed Services Committee about the Iran war. Those included the cost of the US naval blockade on Iran and the damage to the Navy’s headquarters in the Middle East after attacks by Iran.

But it was his defense of Navy conditions on board the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group and ‌his praise for ‌the Navy’s mental health crisis response that drew the fiercest criticism from Democratic senators.

Senator ​Kirsten ‌Gillibrand, ⁠a Democrat ​from ⁠New York, asked him about a sailor who went overboard.

“Senator, that sailor was not trying to kill himself and he admitted that,” Cao told her, saying he used a life preserver.

Gillibrand responded: “What was he trying to do? Swim to Guam?“

“I think you are minimizing what mental health strain is on these service members,” Gillibrand replied, adding she thought Cao’s response was “inhumane” and “inadequate.”

Republican Representative Rob Wittman from Virginia extolled Cao as he introduced him as “a remarkable American story,” a refugee from Vietnam who served in the Navy for 25 years, including in Iraq, Afghanistan and Somalia, retiring at the rank of captain.

Cao, whose son is in the Marine Corps, told the committee ⁠he wanted the job to ensure sailors “don’t go to war the way we did” in ‌Iraq, without armored vehicles or enough body armor.

Senator Angus King, an independent ‌from Maine who caucuses with the Democrats, said he was moved by Cao’s ​personal story but said it was also ironic as Trump’s ‌administration cuts refugee admissions.

“Today, your family wouldn’t be let in the country,” King said.

QUANTITY FOR QUALITY?

Republican Senator Tom Cotton of ‌Arkansas dismissed talk of poor conditions on Navy ships. “If the picture painted by the Democrats were so bleak, would the Navy have reached its recruiting goals three months early?” he asked.

Cao responded, “Senator, we would not be there.”

Senator Jack Reed, a Democrat from Rhode Island, pointed to data he said showed most new Navy recruits required waivers from standard qualification requirements — including on issues like mental health.

“Are you sort of sacrificing ‌quality for quantity?” Reed asked, to a denial from Cao.

Cao will himself require a waiver to be confirmed to the job, since he only retired from the Navy in ⁠2021 — putting him below the required ⁠seven-year cooling-off period to become its civilian leader.

Voter anger over the Iran war, which has settled into an effective stalemate focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz, helped Democrats win control of Congress. A Reuters/Ipsos poll published last week found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress to act to end the war with Iran once and for all.

The Navy has played a critical role in the war, imposing a punishing naval blockade on Iran and helping deliver strikes on Iranian territory. This week, a third aircraft carrier entered Middle East waters, though officials say it is expected to replace one of the two carriers present.

While the US military points to the heavy toll imposed on Iran’s conventional military, and its ability to help escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz past Iranian shores, the Pentagon has not yet explained how it sees the conflict ending.

Senator Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois, asked whether Cao ever stood up to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ​over the war.

“Senator, it’s not within my purview to do ​that,” Cao said.

Duckworth responded sharply: “It is within your purview!“

“This is a failure of leadership by President Trump and the unqualified yes-men he’s installed, and it sounds like you want to be one of those,” she said.

World.title: Trump seeks diplomatic gains on Asia tour as Putin arrives in China
World.content:
MANILA/SHENZHEN: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday arrived in China ahead of a summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, who is on an Asian tour in search of diplomatic gains after a bruising election defeat back home.

Trump was in the Philippines on Tuesday for a meeting with the leaders of the so-called Quad countries and said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and North Korea’s Kim Jong Un at his next stop, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China’s Shenzhen.

“If it’s available, I would do that,” Trump told reporters as he stood for photos with fellow Quad leaders Narendra Modi of India, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australia’s Anthony Albanese.

He added that North Korea’s Kim “would like” to meet in China, hours after Beijing said it had no information about an encounter between the two.

Trump’s Quad meeting at the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit was the security alliance’s first since his January 2025 return to power.

While the Quad — broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence — has quietly progressed in deepening coordination, the short time allotted for Tuesday’s meeting meant it was unlikely to extend beyond pleasantries, according to analysts.

While Trump was greeted in Manila by a marching band and honor guard on the airport tarmac, elsewhere some 2,000 demonstrators faced off with police, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica” — a reference to a US supply chain initiative that has divided opinion in the Philippines.

Tariffs, chips and rare earths

While ASEAN leaders have spent three days grappling with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with the bloc.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market.

On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch China in rare earths production “within 10 months.”

“We are making rare earths at a level that we’ve never made before. We’re going to catch them within 10 months, they say,” he said.

Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle ASEAN members.

Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special license, as the countries were said to represent a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate “trusted access” for firms based in the city-state.

Pax Silica

Trump will meet Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen.

Hayley Channer, economic security director at the Sydney-based United States Studies Center, said the Manila visit was “likely because the US is trying to further its Pax Silica initiative, to build a complete mine-to-chip supply chain.”

Aimed at countering China’s dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines, as its flagship 1,620-hectare (about 4,000-acre) AI manufacturing hub north of Manila threatens to displace Indigenous families.

“We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people,” Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday’s protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words “Pax Silica Sashay Away!“

US Ambassador Lee Lipton said last week that a long-rumored deal signing for the site would not take place during the president’s visit.

As the ASEAN summit came to a close on Tuesday, President Marcos touted the bloc’s signing of a Digital Economy Framework Agreement — aimed at streamlining digital trade and cross-border payments — as its signature achievement.

But he also acknowledged the failure to deliver a “Code of Conduct” on the South China Sea between ASEAN and China during the Philippines’ year as bloc chair.

Marcos told reporters that “85-90 percent of it has actually been done,” leaving the ball in Singapore’s court when it takes the ASEAN reins next year.

World.title: 15,000 arrests in French school and cost-of-living protests: minister
World.content:
PARIS: French police arrested or detained about 15,000 people during cost-of-living and high school protests in recent weeks, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin told parliament on Tuesday.

Darmanin said 7,184 people had been detained during protests over inflation and salaries since October 17, some of which turned into major riots. Another 8,000 were held during protests by high school students over conditions in schools.

The minister said 3,053 cases from the cost-of-living arrests had resulted in charges and prison terms had already been ordered in 666 cases, with 195 sent straight to prison and others given suspended terms.

He said 4,523 of those arrested were adults and 2,661 were minors, with five minors still in custody.

He said that protests on October 17 when serious riots erupted in several cities accounted for about two thirds of the arrests and detentions.

Darmanin said that of the approximately 8,000 arrests in the separate student protests since September, only three people had been kept in detention and all were adults accused of assaulting police or teachers.

World.title: Iraq’s Kataib Hezbollah refuses to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iran-backed militant group Kataib Hezbollah has publicly refused an Iraqi government order to withdraw from its stronghold in Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, in Iraq’s central province of Babil.

According to reports, Iraqi and Iranian officials reached a mediation deal on Tuesday to defuse the crisis.

Kataib Hezbollah accused the government of fabricating allegations to weaken the group and blamed US special envoy Tom Barrack for the escalation.

On Monday, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered security forces to prepare to enter the area, located about 60 kilometers southwest of Baghdad. Kataib Hezbollah was given a deadline until November 20 to vacate the area.

The confrontation escalated after an Iraqi judicial committee reported uncovering evidence of major oil smuggling operations in Jurf al-Sakhar.

Kataib Hezbollah fighters blocked the judicial committee from accessing parts of the site to complete its investigation. An anonymous Kataib Hezbollah official told the Associated Press (AP) that two local facilities refine oil strictly to provide fuel for the group’s vehicles and generators.

Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani arrived in Baghdad on Monday evening on an urgent mission to defuse tension between the Iraqi government and the armed faction.

World.title: Quds Force commander meets Iraqi officials, leaders of armed factions in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani arrived in Baghdad on Monday evening on an urgent mission to defuse tension between the Iraqi government and the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Reports mentioned that Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dispatched Qaani directly to prevent the dispute from turning into an armed confrontation.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi issued a deadline requiring Kataib Hezbollah to vacate the strategic Jurf al-Sakhar district in Iraq’s central province of Babil by the weekend or face a military assault by Iraqi Counter-Terrorism forces.

The government’s attempts to organize weapons under state control and deal with suspected faction-linked smuggling in the region—which Kataib Hezbollah disputes—are the root causes of the issue. According to reports, both sides have increased their military presence in the district.

Qaani met with members of the Kataib Hezbollah Shura Council and leaders of the Coordination Framework to advocate for political involvement in opposition to a military solution and to call for de-escalation.

There has not been any immediate progress in the initial discussions. According to reports, al-Zaidi turned down a meeting with Qaani, insisting that the government’s attempt to reclaim Jurf al-Sakhar is unavoidable, despite ongoing backchannel attempts.

World.title: Iraq resumes oil flows via rehabilitated Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq officially resumed on Tuesday crude oil exports through the rehabilitated Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey.

Pumping restarted at an initial rate of 120,000 barrels per day following a 12-year hiatus.

Operations began at 120,000 barrels per day from the IT1A station through a 46-inch pipeline to the MS metering station.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed that flows will gradually scale up to 500,000 barrels per day, though a specific timeline for reaching full target capacity has not been announced.

Technical teams from the state-run North Oil Company completed extensive maintenance, hydrostatic testing, and operational checks to restore the federal line.

The 960-kilometer pipeline had been inactive since March 2014 due to severe damage caused by repeated attacks carried out by the terrorist group of ISIS.

The restart operates under a one-year interim agreement signed between Baghdad and Ankara in August 2026. That deal sets a minimum transportation capacity of 750,000 bpd through the Turkish system to the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

Baghdad has prioritized northern and overland export corridors since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East in late February 2026, which severely disrupted maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Mövenpick to open lakeside resort near Erbil in 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Accor, a global hospitality business, has collaborated with Erbil-based KRD Holding to develop the Mövenpick Erbil Gomaspan Resort, a 150-room luxury resort overlooking Gomaspan Dam about 35 kilometers northeast of Erbil.

The project, set to open in 2030, will be Mövenpick’s first hotel in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region and second in the nation, after the Mövenpick Hotel Al Zaytoon in Baghdad.

The resort will have hotel rooms and suites, restaurants, bars, a spa, swimming pools, a fitness center, and over 1,300 square meters of meeting and event space.

The plans also include a lakeside corniche with restaurants and cafés, a dining island encircled by the dam’s waters, and an adventure sports area featuring safari trails, quad riding, mountain motorcycling, and skydiving.

On September 29, Accor and KRD Holding inked a development agreement with the goal of luring both local and international visitors to the hilly terrain around Erbil.

Gomaspan Dam, which opened in October 2024, is the largest dam in Erbil Governorate and was built largely to support irrigation and fish farming, with the aim of boosting tourism in the surrounding region.

World.title: Chinese refiners ramp up Iraqi crude purchases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chinese independent refineries have ramped up purchases of Iraqi crude oil via international trading houses at narrower premiums, capitalizing on stabilized Gulf export flows, ample regional supply, and softer global benchmark prices, according to market traders cited by Reuters.

The surge in buying activity centers on China’s independent “teapot” refiners—primarily clustered in the eastern province of Shandong—seeking to utilize their remaining year-end crude import quotas while replacing sanctioned Iranian barrels choked off by the ongoing U.S. naval blockade.

Traders reported that spot premiums for Iraqi grades have dropped back into single-digit territory as trading firms lowered offers amid steady Gulf shipments. In recent deals, ADNOC Trading sold cargoes of both Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy to an independent refinery in Shandong for late-December delivery at a premium of roughly $6 per barrel above March ICE Brent futures.

Similarly, TotalEnergies’ trading arm, TOTSA, sold 2 million barrels of Basrah Heavy to a Chinese independent refiner for January delivery at a premium ranging between $7 and $8 per barrel over ICE Brent.

Parallel transactions across other regional Gulf grades reflected a similar pricing trend. Mercuria sold 2 million barrels of the UAE’s Upper Zakum crude to an independent Chinese refiner for second-half January delivery at roughly $8 per barrel over March Brent, while Vitol sold 1 million barrels of Qatar’s Al-Shaheen crude to another Shandong processor for February delivery at around $9 per barrel over February Brent.

Several converging commercial factors accelerated Chinese demand for Iraqi barrels. A sharp pullback in ICE Brent crude futures following the U.S. midterm elections—combined with declining tanker freight rates—improved refining margins for private Chinese processors.

Furthermore, data intelligence analysts note that Iraqi crude currently ranks among the most competitively priced grades of comparable quality on a delivered-China basis, offering prompt cargo availability at a time when Russian ESPO barrels remain prohibitively expensive due to competition from Chinese state-owned majors. With year-end deadlines approaching, independent refiners are moving quickly to exhaust their remaining 2026 import quotas before expiration.

World.title: US dollar holds above 171,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar recorded a renewed upward tick across major domestic parallel markets on Tuesday morning, November 17, 2026, holding firmly above the 171,000 IQD threshold across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

According to morning trading figures across key commercial hubs, physical banknote rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 171,050 IQD against buying offers of 170,250 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted selling rates at 171,250 IQD alongside buying bids of 170,500 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices matched Erbil’s selling ceiling at 171,250 IQD, with purchasing offers settling firmer at 170,750 IQD per $100.

This sustained parallel-market elevation maintains a spread of more than 19,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar)—a peg established following the government’s October 7, 2026 currency adjustment.

The persistent premium reflects heightened domestic political and security uncertainty alongside continued physical cash demand to settle unrecorded cross-border imports outside formal electronic banking channels.

World.title: Sirens activated after drone flew over Iraq’s Khor Mor gas field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Warning sirens were activated at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan on Monday after an unidentified drone flew over the facility.

Two security sources confirmed the alert to Reuters, noting there were no immediate reports of a strike, casualties, or new damage.

Security officials have not identified who launched the drone. Kurdish authorities have previously attributed similar threats against the site to Iran-backed armed factions.

The overflight comes just one week after a drone attack targeted the gas field on September 8, forcing joint field operator Dana Gas to halt production entirely.

The strike hit a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tank, causing a large fire that was later extinguished.

The facility is the main source of energy for the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the largest gas field there.

Between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of power output had been cut off due to the stoppage of gas operations, reducing 70 to 80 percent of the energy grid’s overall capacity.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s major cities, including Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal, were no longer receiving direct electricity supply.

The facility was temporarily closed in July due to security concerns resulting from escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Iraqi security identifies two illegal oil refineries in Jurf al-Nasr
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi authorities uncovered two illegal oil refineries, storage facilities, and evidence of pipeline tampering in the Jurf al-Nasr, also known as Jurf al-Sakhar, area in Iraq’s central province of Babil.

The discoveries were confirmed following a high-level government investigation launched by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and a parliamentary inquiry.

Six places were investigated by government detectives, who found two refineries operating illegally, oil tanks, and a tanker truck, as well as hidden changes in state oil pipelines.

A parliamentary committee examined drone footage, thermal images, and documents indicating around 25 tanker trucks, each with the capacity to carry 36,000 liters, were used within the smugglers’ network.

According to reports, the illicit operations had been ongoing since 2021, developing from exposed oil pits to covered loading points and underground storage to avoid being detected.

Following an emergency security meeting on Saturday, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil-sector officials. He also ordered all individuals implicated in the smuggling operations to be referred to the judiciary for prosecution.

On Monday, government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi announced that al-Zaidi ordered Iraqi troops into Jurf al-Nasr to restore state control and dismantle the networks.

Authorities also gave the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah, which controls Jurf al-Nasr, until the weekend as a deadline to withdraw.

World.title: Indian missing in tanker attack in Hormuz
World.content:
Panama-flagged LPG tanker came under a missile attack

21 of 24 Indians aboard tanker hit in Hormuz safe: MEA

NEW DELHI: One Indian seafarer went missing and two others were injured after Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT TARA GAS with 24 Indians on board was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. India on Tuesday strongly condemned the attack, expressing concern over repeated attacks on commercial vessels. With this, four Indian crew members have gone missing since the war in West Asia broke out in Feb.In a post on X, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said, "In a distressing development, the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS was subjected to a subsequent attack, forcing the entire crew to abandon the vessel."MEA said 21 of the 24 Indian nationals aboard the vessel had been safely brought ashore at Khasab in Oman, while the two injured crew members had been admitted to hospital. Sonowal said that govt is coordinating with the ship management company and regional rescue authorities to locate the missing seafarer and ensure the immediate safety and welfare of the rescued crew members.MEA said the Indian Embassy in Oman is coordinating with Omani authorities and closely monitoring the search-and-rescue operations and appreciated the timely assistance and support extended by the govt of Oman."The continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region are deeply worrisome and pose a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers," it added."The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," the ministry said. As per govt data, there have been 102 incidents in West Asia since the conflict broke out, with 11 Indian lives having been lost and another person presumed dead.

World.title: East Asia Summit: PM Modi announces international initiative to secure seafarers
World.content:
PM Narendra Modi addressed the East Asia Summit (EAS) in Manila where he announced a Seafarers' Safety Initiative and, highlighting the threat from terrorism, proposed an EAS Cyber Crime conference at the National Forensic Science University to address new-age threats from cross-border crimes.

EAS is an annual Asean-led dialogue forum of 19 Indo-Pacific countries, including US and China. "Our seas are the lifelines of our shared prosperity. Ensuring their security and freedom of navigation is the responsibility of us all... We are launching a Seafarers' Safety Initiative, under which we will enhance cooperation in joint training and emergency response," Modi said.

PM on regional peace

Modi said conflicts were putting increasing pressure on food, fuel and fertiliser supplies and ships and seafarers were also being targeted on international waterways.



"Alongside the serious threat of terrorism, new forms of cross-border crime, such as cyber fraud and online scams, are also on the rise," he said, adding that what the world needed most today was peace, stability and predictability.

Whether it was Ukraine or West Asia, Modi said, India would continue to support every effort towards peace and that the spirit of dialogue, mutual respect and cooperation was the cornerstone of India's foreign policy.





"Our shared future will be shaped not by conflict, but by mutual respect and cooperation. With this vision, India will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Asean, remaining committed to regional peace, stability and shared prosperity," he said.

Quad sends China message hours before Trump meet with Xi & Putin

Amid doubts not about Quad's survival but the level at which it will function, the leaders of member countries Australia, India, Japan and the US - PM Anthony Albanese, PM Narendra Modi, PM Sanae Takaichi and President Donald Trump - met in Manila on Tuesday for the first summit of the grouping in two years.They looked to turn up the heat on China as they expressed grave concern over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export curbs, and committed to working together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.Trump described Quad as very important and special - and Modi as a friend and a great leader - in his opening remarks, as he announced Quad will conduct its first military exercise featuring maritime patrol aircraft in March 2027, working to protect "peace through strength".Calling the meeting an important milestone, Modi said for India, Quad is a trusted partnership. "From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific," he said.The short joint press release - unlike the expansive 2024 Wilmington Declaration - cut Beijing some slack though by not explicitly mentioning South or East China Sea.With India unable to host the Quad summit for the past two years, Modi pitched a meeting in early 2027. There was no acknowledgement of the next summit in the joint release.The joint release, however, strongly opposed any "destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability". The meeting took place hours before Trump's departure for China, where he is set to attend a potentially landmark trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. Trump said Quad nations had reached several new critical mineral deals to secure their supply chains and ensure that none of them remained vulnerable to coercion by any single foreign supplier.The joint statement said that P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, "making our seas safer". The exercise will take place in Guam next year under the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, an initiative launched in May this year to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.The joint statement unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening the Quad's ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism.The statement also said that Quad is working to secure critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future, including investments and deployment of trusted AI, and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance.AI was a major area of focus, with the leaders backing AI Accelerator, which was announced by the foreign ministers on the margins of the G20 meeting in Atlanta and is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific.Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said the Quad leaders agreed to launch a business forum, bringing together businesses, academics and industries to foster greater business ties across private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.The statement recalled that this year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the 10th anniversary of the vision of a free and open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Japanese PM Shinzo Abe in 2016. "Together, we have shown the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability and prosperity," it said.

World.title: SC upholds stay on Azam Khan's conviction; offers son, wife relief
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta

in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate and granted the same relief to Khan's son and wife, who were denied this benefit by the high court.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said all three were on the same footing and questioned the HC for discriminating among them. It said there was "apparent legal dichotomy in the judgement". It said, "We find that the HC failed to articulate any coherent legal reason why similar relief, as granted to Mohammad Azam Khan, was denied, even though all three were convicted under the self-same charge of conspiracy.

"

"Where several convicts standing on the same footing seek stay/suspension of conviction, it is legitimate for them to expect similar treatment... Parity being a facet of Article 14 of Constitution, equals ought to be treated equally unless, of course, an intelligible differentia having a rational nexus with the object of the order distinguishes one from the others," the bench said.

SC said though differential treatment was not forbidden, "an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained". It said, "If the court grants a stay/suspension of conviction to one... while similar relief to other similarly situated convicts is denied, the distinguishing feature on the record must be identified and expressly stated as the reason for the departure from parity. An order silent on that point is, by itself, arbitrary.

World.title: 'Goldy Dhillon a petty thief': Lawrence gang on gangster who threatened Amitabh Bachchan
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Gangster Goldy Dhillon had a narrow escape in Germany during an attack by the Lawrence Bishnoi gang's Canada handler, Manna Brampton, and his Madrid counterpart, Mandeep Spain, in Jan this year, the duo said in a statement on social media Tuesday.

A day after Dhillon's post threatening actor Amitabh Bachchan, the duo hit out at Dhillon for killing an LGBTQ+ influencer, Mad Sandhu, in Amritsar and called him "publicity hungry" for targeting Bachchan.

Claiming Dhillon used to wash utensils at a restaurant in Germany for a living, they said he lacked the wherewithal to target Bachchan or even his domestic staff.

Calling Dhillon's claims of seeking revenge for the 1984 anti-Sikh riots a desperate bid for attention, Brampton and Spain said he was no-thing more than a petty thief and a "chitta" (heroin) peddler from Punjab with FIRs against him for drug-dealing and stealing cable wires.



On the attack, the gang said despite constantly boasting about weapons, Dhillon had nothing but a knife to defend himself. He managed to escape and subsequently fled the country, they claimed.

Furthermore, the former associates said they were the ones who had helped Dhillon gain a footing in the underworld by carrying out for free three murders and 20-25 firings in Canada to establish his name.

In a damning blow to his credibility in the underworld, Brampton and Spain also labelled Dhillon a police informer.

World.title: After govt push, curbs on sexual post recommendations on Instagram
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Meta has tightened

's recommendations in India, disclosing the changes a month after the govt asked it to review how Instagram and Facebook suggest posts. Meta said Instagram now recommends fewer sexually suggestive posts and depictions of violence.

The changes apply to suggested posts from accounts users do not follow, including in Reels, and the main feed. Posts complying with Instagram's rules can remain on the platform even if they are excluded from recommendations.

Meta said it had strengthened its default safeguards over the past year based on user feedback. Instagram uses AI models to assess posts before recommending them and has fine-tuned its systems for India to identify more sensitive material.



"We've seen people report recommended content about half as often as they were a year ago," Meta said in a blog post. The company did not disclose the underlying figures.

In its Oct 10 advisory, the IT ministry asked Meta to review how it ranks and recommends posts, citing concerns that its systems could give undue prominence to misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material. It also sought stronger checks on posts that could incite violence or disrupt public order.

World.title: Must remain politically neutral but learn from extraordinary leaders: Cabinet secy to babus
World.content:
Cabinet secretary TV Somnathan (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Civil servants have a constitutional duty to remain politically neutral, but they should learn administrative skills of extraordinary leaders, cabinet secretary T V Somanathan said on Wednesday, drawing on his experience of working with PM Narendra Modi and former Tamil Nadu CM M Karunanidhi.Addressing a leadership workshop for civil servants, Somanathan said elected heads of govt combine political and administrative leadership, and while bureaucrats must stay away from politics, they should learn from the latter aspect of their leadership.âWhile staying away from the political aspect, we can and should learn from the administrative skills of extraordinary leaders and that is the purpose of this workshop,â he said.Somanathan, who served as secretary to CM under Karunanidhi for around four years and worked in PMO for two-and-a-half years as joint secretary and additional secretary, said the longevity of the two leaders as heads of govt reflected extraordinary leadership skills.
