Karunanidhi held office for over 19 years, while Modi has completed 25 years as head of govt.Sharing lessons on leadership and governance, he said the questions senior officers raise during review meetings shape the priorities of officials down the administrative chain.If reviews focus only on expenditure, districts will concentrate on spending, but asking how many beneficiaries have actually received the intended benefits would shift attention towards outcomes.The Cabinet Secretary also emphasised the importance of listening directly to citizens rather than relying entirely on information filtered through several layers of administration. âEvery senior officer needs a few sources of information that have not been summarised by anyone,â he said, citing field visits, reading individual grievances and meeting visitors as ways to understand problems that may not figure in official reports.On decision-making, Somanathan said files should not be viewed as obstacles, as recording reasons, facts and options considered gives decisions legitimacy and helps them withstand scrutiny. âA sense of mission in the civil service must therefore work hand in hand with a sense of propriety and due process,â he said. Officers should not avoid taking decisions when file notings and advice differ, but must record cogent reasons before proceeding, even if it means overruling objections.Somanathan also urged senior officials to delegate authority and stand by juniors who take decisions in good faith. âOfficers will use the authority they already have only when they are confident that their seniors will not leave them to face the consequences alone when something goes wrong,â he said.On the need for course correction, he said well-reasoned changes in implementation should be seen as evidence of a programme learning from experience, rather than a deviation. The cabinet secretary also said leadership should also be judged by whether work continues effectively after an officer is transferred, stressing the importance of proper handover notes and institutional continuity.Somanathan urged officers to take decisions in public interest, record their reasons clearly and ensure that successors and reviewing authorities understand the rationale behind them.

World.title: Morning Digest: Jensen Huang open to return as Nvidia CEO; World needs peace and predictability, says PM Modi in Manila, and more
World.content:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has signalled his interest in returning to lead the AI computer chip company in his first public statement since he abruptly left the company last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said in a social media post.

World needs peace, stability, predictability: Modi in Manila

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) called for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world as he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit, and the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila, Philippines. He made a number of proposals aimed at maritime security, protecting critical minerals supply chains, and enhancing trade. The Quad Summit, which was being held for the first time in a non-member country, was hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump and was also attended by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, apart from Mr. Modi. The leaders issued a joint statement opposing economic and maritime “coercion” in the Indo-Pacific, and Mr. Modi announced that India would host the first Quad Business Forum in Mumbai in 2027.

Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change

Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time. “India is a nation of extraordinary innovation and ambition, facing immense environmental pressures, yet moving ahead with determination. Not because the challenge is simple, not because the path is easy. But because millions of people have decided that progress simply cannot wait,” said Prince William.

Congress-SP talks on U.P. seat-sharing deferred after Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh meet

A meeting that had been scheduled for Tuesday (November 17, 2026) for the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) to discuss seat-sharing in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections has been deferred following talks between the top leadership of the two parties. No fresh date has been set for the meeting, with sources saying that it is expected to take place “in a few days”. Sources indicated that the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and SP president Akhilesh Yadav had a word on the sidelines of the launch event of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, held in Delhi on Monday (November 16).

Nearly 75 lakh names added to draft SSR voter lists in 13 States and UTs

Months after final voter lists were published following the contentious special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, nearly 75 lakh more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process (SSR). The combined size of the electorate in these States before the SIR was 49.61 crore, which shrunk to 45.22 crore after the SIR and has now increased to 45.96 crore in the draft SSR list. This means there has been a cumulative increase of 1.64 %.

Thirupparankundram row: T.N. government pushes for stay of High Court order to avoid breach of peace

The Tamil Nadu government urged the Supreme Court on Tuesday to stay a Madras High Court decision of January 2026 which confirmed its earlier order to the Arulmigu Subramaniswamy Temple devasthanam or management body to light the Karthigai Deepam on a stone pillar located atop the Thirupparankundram Hill. The Division Bench of the High Court in January had upheld the earlier Single Judge order, while brushing aside fears expressed by the State that such an action would be a sure recipe for “disturbance of public tranquility and peace”, given the fact that the stone pillar was proximate to a dargah. The High Court had dismissed the fears as an “imaginary ghost”.

Opposition, OBC group voice concerns on 287 ‘other’ religions in the Census

Opposition leaders and the All India Other Backward Classes Students’ Association on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) raised questions about the way in which the 2027 Census is being conducted, reacting to The Hindu’s report on the self-enumeration portal listing as many as 287 options in a drop-down box for “Other” religions, including ‘ISKCON’, ‘Ramkrishna Paramhansa’, Shia, Sunni, and ‘Pentacostal’. This list vanished from the portal within hours of The Hindu’s queries about it, posed to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.

India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home. “Neither India nor any other country can dictate terms on this,” Mr. Zahed said during a media briefing when asked for comments on a media report saying New Delhi had hinted at two conditions for handing over Hasina.

U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.

A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry

A Russian military transport plane crashed in western Siberia on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), killing all 19 people on board, the Defence Ministry said. Preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure. The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow. Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash. The An-12 typically has a crew of six.

Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid

Bangladesh’s first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in the country’s northwest Pabna district began supplying electricity to the national grid on a trial basis on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to officials. The 2,400 MW Russian-assisted facility is expected to meet more than 10% of Bangladesh's electricity demand once fully operational, helping the country diversify its energy sources.

Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate

Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.

World.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses
World.content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has signalled his interest in returning to lead the AI computer chip company in his first public statement since he abruptly left the company last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said in a social media post.

He acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life but said that he’s received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return.

The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Mr. Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk. President Donald Trump also endorsed the bid.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Mr. Huang’s statement.

Also on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), key House lawmakers said that Mr. Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the chipmaker faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips.

Mr. Huang will appear before the committees on December 1, followed by the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, on Dec. 2.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” said a statement from the chairmen of three House committees with oversight of China and intelligence issues.

“The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” the lawmakers said, referring to the People’s Republic of China.

Meanwhile, Nvidia said it’s creating a new board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance following revelations that Mr. Huang had an extramarital affair with an alleged spy for China.

Nvidia said the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be responsible for oversight of national security policies and compliance with export controls.

Nvidia’s advanced chips are in high demand because they’re essential for cloud computing and data centres that underpin the artificial intelligence boom, but they face restrictions on their sale to China.

The committee will meet at least once every quarter and have three members from Nvidia’s board of directors. It will work with independent third-party experts as it oversees efforts to enhance the company’s existing national security and global trade compliance team.

“We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation,” Chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement.

President Donald Trump said it was “good” that Nvidia had created a national security and export control oversight committee shortly after arriving in the Philippines on Tuesday evening (November 17, 2026).

“Yes, that’s a good idea. It’s a great company,” Trump said during a photo opportunity in Manila with the leaders of Australia, India and Japan. “It’s a great idea.”

Mr. Huang was forced to resign as Nvidia’s CEO last week following scrutiny of his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who used to lead Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls.

World.title: Delhi Assembly Winter session from December 18 to 23
World.content:
The Winter Session of the Delhi Assembly will be held from December 18 to 23, the Chief Minister’s Office said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

This decision was taken during a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta at the Delhi Secretariat on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The Chief Minister said that serious and meaningful discussions regarding important issues related to Delhi’s development and public welfare schemes would take place during this session. “The government is committed to making necessary decisions, prioritising the public interest above all else, and implementing them effectively,” she said.

World.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry
World.content:
A Russian military transport plane crashed in western Siberia on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), killing all 19 people on board, the Defence Ministry said. Preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure.

The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow. Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash. The An-12 typically has a crew of six.

Kemerovo Gov. Ilya Serdyuk said the plane crashed near the village of Yagunovo, which is close to Kemerovo airport. “Emergency responders put out a fire on the site of the crash,” he said.

The Investigative Committee, the country’s top criminal investigation agency, launched an inquiry into possible violations of flight safety rules, a standard practice following crashes.

The An-12 is a Soviet-built four-engine turboprop transport plane that has been in service since the late 1950s. Over 1,000 were built and some still remain in operation in Russia and other nations.

World.title: Jharkhand SIR: Final BLO meetings at poll stations on November 18
World.content:
Jharkhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) K. Ravi Kumar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) appealed to all eligible Indian citizens in the State to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll being published under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Speaking to the media in Ranchi, Mr. Ravi asserted that an “Ek Aur Avsar” (One More Opportunity) camp will be held on November 18 at all polling stations in the State, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., where meetings of BLOs (Booth Level Officers) and BLAs-2 (Booth Level Agents-2) will take place in the form of a “Chunav Pathshala” (Electoral Awareness Session).

He pointed out that the objective of this special initiative is to provide one additional opportunity for any eligible Indian citizen who, for various reasons, has not yet had their name added to the electoral roll.

Mr. Ravi explained that the camps will focus primarily on three key areas. First, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is republishing the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) list at all polling stations. If any eligible Indian citizen has been included in this list, they may follow the prescribed procedure to submit Form-6 or an enumeration form.

Second, lists of voters in categories such as “No Mapping” or those with “Logical Discrepancies”—who have failed to provide the necessary documentation despite receiving two notices from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and undergoing a door-to-door verification process—will be made available at the respective polling stations.

Third, efforts are being made to identify eligible Indian citizens who will have turned 18 by October 1, 2026, but who have not yet registered their names in the electoral roll for their respective polling stations. Eligible Indian citizens will be able to have their names included in the electoral roll by submitting Form 6.

The CEO said that this is the sixth and final BLO-BLA-2 meeting being held under the ongoing SIR process in Jharkhand. He urged all eligible citizens in the state to take advantage of this opportunity and get their names added to the electoral roll, ensuring that no eligible Indian citizen remains excluded.

The ECI has already extended the deadline for final publication of electoral rolls in Jharkhand under the SIR to November 30. The final publication was initially scheduled for October 7 and was later extended to October 19 before being revised.

World.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
World.content:
A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

It also follows recent security scares at two British air force bases hosting the U.S. military, with officials accusing Iran of involvement in plots to target them.

A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

Held in British police custody since his November 10 arrest near Gloucester, southwest England, he was handed to the US military “over suspected national security and espionage allegations”, U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing said.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the decision to “pass the investigation to them to progress” followed an extensive probe by his counter-terror unit and subsequent discussions between British prosecutors and “American partners”.

FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that the unnamed Army officer was in U.S. custody after “an espionage investigation”.

He noted it had involved “close cooperation” between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and various other US and UK law enforcement and intelligence agencies.

“Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action,” Mr. Patel added.

Arrest, allegations

A senior NATO military official last week confirmed that the arrested soldier had been assigned to its Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), the alliance’s 20-nation, high-readiness force led by the British Army.

Based at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester, it can deploy at short notice anywhere in Europe or globally under the direct operational command of NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe.

Imjin is also just a few miles from the U.K.’s highly sensitive GCHQ intelligence, security and cyber agency headquarters.

Police had arrested the soldier under two sections of the U.K.’s national security laws, one relating to obtaining or disclosing protected information and the other to assisting a foreign intelligence service.

Officials revealed at the time that “the country to which the allegations relate is Russia”.

The Kremlin has denied Russia has any links to the soldier.

Officers carried out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire following the arrest, according to police.

U.S. Brigadier General Sean Stinchon said in a statement on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) the case “should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution”.

World.title: Construction activities on Kaziranga wildlife corridors flagged
World.content:
An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months.

In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order.

“We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including the Tiger Reserve, are restrained. No new construction shall be permitted on private lands which form part of the nine identified animal corridors,” the apex court’s order read.

“Despite this clear and categorical prohibition, the Government of Assam has displayed a disturbing disregard for the mandate of the Supreme Court by permitting and facilitating unlawful construction activities within these ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

He reminded the CEC of photographic evidence of a building under construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor attached to his May 11 letter. “The construction activity was allowed to proceed unabated and has now reached an advanced stage of completion,” he wrote, attaching recent photographs of the construction site.

Mr. Choudhury said the CEC’s inability to take up the matter six months ago “effectively afforded the concerned authorities sufficient time to continue and substantially complete the illegal construction”.

He said such delays in addressing matters of grave environmental significance seriously undermine the purpose and efficacy of the CEC’s mandate.

The activist further said the Assam Government did not inform the Supreme Court of any instance of violation of its April 12, 2019, order for necessary action.

“This persistent failure of enforcement has emboldened continued violations and weakened the protection envisaged by the Supreme Court,” he said, urging the CEC to recommend contempt proceedings against the officials responsible for permitting, facilitating or failing to prevent these blatant violations of the court’s binding directions.

“The matter concerns not merely a breach of judicial orders but the continued degradation of one of India’s most treasured ecological landscapes and a globally recognised natural heritage site. Immediate intervention is therefore both necessary and imperative,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

World.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
World.content:
Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.

According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.

Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.

The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

“The sharp rise in vehicle numbers reflects the growing pressure on pilgrimage infrastructure, road networks, traffic management, road safety and healthcare services. These trends underline the urgent need for strengthened safety measures, improved traffic management and a more coordinated, data-driven approach to ensuring a safe and sustainable Char Dham Yatra,” said Mr. Nautiyal.

He stressed that Uttarakhand must move beyond the pursuit of record-breaking pilgrim numbers and focus on carrying capacity, pilgrim health, sustainability and the long-term future of the Char Dham Yatra.

World.title: In hard-hitting speech, Bilawal says system was ‘made to collapse’
World.content:
Key takeaways:

Amid debate on a “system reset” in the country, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Tuesday that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

Over the past few months, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

During his speech at the Karachi Press Club, Bilawal recalled Naqvi’s remarks and said, “Nobody objects that the system has collapsed, but there is no discussion and debate on why it collapsed.”

He noted that the proposed solution “was not an actual remedy to the illness due to which we suffered a system collapse”.

“If we want to focus on resolving the issues of the public, if we want to fight poverty, unemployment, inflation, then we absolutely need to decide why the system collapsed,” the Bhutto scion said.

’Reset must be political’

Bilawal asserted a reset was “definitely needed”; however, he also stressed that it should be political.

“Why political? Because politicians are the representatives of the people, and if politicians do not play their role, then these fundamental issues won’t be resolved,” Bilawal said.

“I believe the system has not collapsed, but it has been made to collapse,” he stated, while acknowledging his own role in the matter.

“Everyone makes mistakes, but there comes a time when you must fix those mistakes. How do we fix that?” Bilawal asked rhetorically.

He contended that state institutions had “lost their legitimacy”, calling for it to be restored.

During his speech at the ‘Meet the Press’ event and responding to queries later, Bilawal firmly declared that the PPP would oppose any “unconstitutional” moves regarding new provinces.

He also voiced his strong opposition to a referendum on creating new provinces, questioning the “intent” behind it, and said his party lawmakers were facing “pressure” but would not succumb to it.

The PPP chairman’s remarks went beyond his oft-repeated calls for electoral reforms and political consensus, as he called for the opposition PTI to be given reserved seats as a “confidence-building measure”.

He also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, which he had strongly advocated for at the time of its passage just a year ago.

‘Injustices’ to PTI of reserved seats, symbol

The PPP chairman further observed that “some such injustices” had been done that, if corrected, could quickly restore the opposition’s trust.

In an indirect reference to the PTI, Bilawal recalled the revocation of the PPP’s party symbol in 1988 and said, “Revoking the symbol from a party is akin to you joking with the public, and the public denounced this tradition and action and responded to you in those elections.”

Then, in a stance deviating from the ruling coalition’s, Bilawal said that “what happened with the reserved seats was a joke”. He said the opposition was not only deprived of those seats, but “those in the treasury benches also put them in their pockets”.

The PTI — deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections — was declared eligible for the seats by the Supreme Court. However, a constitutional bench formed later via the 26th Amendment overturned that ruling while hearing review pleas of the coalition parties.

“And from those same reserved seats, which are not yours, you brought constitutional amendments not once but twice, and are now thinking to bring a third one,” Bilawal said.

He called for resolving reservations regarding rigging and returning the party symbol “so they have their own identity”.

“It is a confidence-building measure that we, without any preconditions, return the reserved seats to the opposition, which is their right,” said Bilawal, whose PPP was also among the beneficiaries of the reserved seats case.

‘Imran Khan a political prisoner’

Reiterating his call for electoral reforms, Bilawal also stressed the need to restore the PTI’s and the opposition’s trust in the Parliament.

“If we want the system to be reset and the Parliament to start functioning, vengeful actions will need to be stopped. How much revenge will you take after all?” he said.

The PPP chairman said not only should vengeful actions be halted, but the “tradition of revenge inserted in Pakistan’s politics” should be ended forever.

He even recalled a speech by PTI founder Imran Khan, who questioned if “we were ants”.

Bilawal called for efforts to ensure that there is no political prisoner in Pakistan, terming it necessary for the “system to function”.

“What a weird country this is; since 1947, whoever becomes the prime minister goes to jail, whoever gets out of jail goes to sit in the Prime Minister House,” he remarked.

“You broke [our] back, then ask ‘why did you fall’,” he quipped, emphasising that political prisoners would need to be released.

When asked whether he considered Imran a political prisoner, Bilawal responded in the affirmative.

“A person becomes the prime minister and is later imprisoned. So I can either accept that every prime minister in the country’s history has been a thief, or I can accept that all prime ministers in our history have been victims of political revenge,” he added.

Noting that the PTI had made mistakes as well, Bilawal said, “One day, I hope no prime minister should have to go to jail, and for that, we need to develop consensus.”

‘Federal govt must decide on reset’

Bilawal, in response to a question, also called on the federal government to present its stance on the governance reset.

Presenting his own approach, he said, “The political reset that I spoke of, I will try to develop that consensus, and I would like to create a consensus for it in my own party so that we can engage other political parties”.

As for the federal government, Bilawal said, “I don’t know what they are thinking.”

In an apparent reference to the interior minister’s remarks about being on the “same page” as Bilawal, the PPP chairman said, “I had heard we were on the same page, and if this is the page we are on, then nothing could be better.”

Bilawal said there had been a debate that had been “forced” in the country for the past few months.

“Even the cabinet had not discussed the matter, let alone the parliament [..] So, how could it be that federal ministers are talking about it of their own accord,” he asked.

At this, the PPP chairman said he would like to believe that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has “enough authority over his own ministers”.

“You are sabotaging your own prime minister, and then you complain that the system has collapsed [..] I believe that is unfair.”

In recent days, PML-N’s Khawaja Asif, who serves as the defence minister, has been advocating for new administrative units, suggesting the formation of up to 12 provinces.

Bilawal maintained that his party would welcome any debate and consensus on the matter; however, he hinted that deliberation and consensus “may not be on the agenda”.

Bilawal said that “suggestions” were coming from outside of the Parliament, which he described as showing “clear indication [..] that the opinion of Parliament, public, and cabinet did not hold any weight and you just want to use a backdoor channel”.

“Up until today, neither the prime minister nor a single member of the provinces has brought up the issue with the president of Pakistan or me,” he added.

On a possible rollback of the 18th Amendment, Bilawal pointed out that the Sindh government was giving the Centre Rs585 billion surplus in financial support.

“Donations worth Rs 260bn were given in security and national interest,” he said.

“I am not even counting the rightful share of the province — of petroleum levy and gas levy — it is about Rs1.7 trillion from the petroleum levy.”

He remarked, “So, you will pickpocket the province, loot our resources and then come and ask us, ‘why the roads are broken and why no schools or hospitals have been built’.”

Bilawal assailed the Centre, asking if a province was paying a Rs585bn surplus, Rs260bn for national security and Rs1.7tr on the petroleum levy, then “the federal government should be held responsible for the lack of public spending, not the provincial government”.

He claimed that the “easiest way to do corruption in Pakistan was to be on the state’s right side”.

‘Referendum has never been democratic’

On the interior minister’s recommendation of holding a referendum to decide on the creation of administrative units, the PPP chairman pointed to the “intention” behind the proposed action.

“In our history, a referendum has always been carried out for an undemocratic act and never a democratic one,” the Bhutto scion remarked.

He argued that if the Constitution had relevant provisions on the creation of administrative units, then the mere suggestion of holding a referendum “meant that you were looking for an unconstitutional method”.

The PPP chairman vowed that his party would stand firmly against any such “unconstitutional” action.

Bilawal also spoke against “any forced division” in Sindh, warning that while PPP remained in favour of creating provinces, it was against a “forced separation”.

He cautioned, “We talk about the garbage on Karachi’s streets, but if Sindh is divided, we will see blood flow through its streets.”

On being asked whether a compromise could be reached on the creation of new provinces, Bilawal recalled that several resolutions had been passed by the Sindh Assembly against the province’s division.

“Any more discussion on this issue is a slap to the people of Sindh,” he declared.

“I do not understand what Mohsin bhai is trying to do,” Bilawal said.

Replying to a question about new provinces and a “reset”, Bilawal said the PML-N-led government had not discussed the matter with the PPP, adding that this raised the question of why this was “being made to discuss by the media”.

Bilawal said he has invited PM Shehbaz to hold talks with the Sindh government on public issues, and also suggested that he convene his cabinet meetings in each province.

‘Pressure on PPP lawmakers’

Reiterating the PPP’s stance on new provinces, Bilawal stressed that as a generational politician, he would want to take steps as per the public’s wishes.

“Those from whom these suggestions are coming, they have not won even a single election in their lives. And neither do they have chances in the next election … they would become a minister, prime minister or chief minister whether they get a single vote or not in the next elections,” he said, adding that each side was taking a stance as per their situation.

Replying to another query, Bilawal said, “On the one hand, there are no discussions ongoing; on the other hand, there definitely is pressure on the party’s MNAs and MPAs, but PPP’s representatives do not function on someone else’s pressure, but the public’s.”

He further remarked, “If tomorrow, my software is updated and I direct my party to vote for Sindh’s division, there will be a revolt against me. They will not cast a majority vote even on my directives.”

He quipped that “some people were dreaming of becoming the chief minister of their area, but they would not even be able to remain their house’s chief minister”.

The Bhutto scion further affirmed that his PPP would not “back any conspiracy against Punjab”, adding that he would support only those decisions endorsed by the Punjab Assembly.

He pointed out that there was a lack of discussion on declaring Gilgit-Baltistan a province even though there was a consensus in the region on this demand.

‘27th Amendment passed with brute majority’

Speaking on the judiciary, Bilawal noted that “our internal wish of a constitutional court” as per the Charter of Democracy had been fulfilled, but questioned whether the court had the public’s confidence.

“If the lawyers and judges themselves do not have confidence in the courts, then the system did not collapse, but was made to collapse.”

The PPP chairman said he was not calling for the revocation of such moves, but for greater consensus. He asserted that the 26th Amendment was passed with “bilateral agreement, if not complete consensus”, as the opposition’s input was taken through Fazl.

Bilawal said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor bilateral agreement; it was passed with brute majority”.

He called for engaging with the opposition on judicial reforms and termed it a requirement for the “political, public and democratic reset”, adding that without such a reset, the public’s key issues of inflation and unemployment cannot be addressed.

Bilawal also noted that rigging allegations often surfaced during elections.

“I have been in politics for the past 20 years, and usually, I have seen that it is the opposition that accuses the other side of rigging and the government denies it. For the first time, I am seeing that people from within the government are claiming that rigging has been done.”

‘Fazl has right to criticise govt’

Bilawal also came to Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s defence as tensions between the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief and the government have flared in recent weeks.

The past month has witnessed exchanges of harsh remarks between Fazl and federal ministers, after the JUI-F chief accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

These developments came after Fazl joined the opposition in criticising the Centre’s imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in the PTI-ruled KP. He also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

In his address, Bilawal stressed that it was the opposition’s role in the Parliament to criticise the government.

“It is the opposition’s right to criticise you, and however he (Fazl) does it, it is their right,” he said.

Bilawal remarked that the opposition had the “most patriotic” role in the Parliament.

“For any government to question the patriotism of an opposition member [..] it is not only an injustice to that parliament or to the system, but the biggest injustice to the country,” he added.

The PPP chairman termed a difference of opinion within the Parliament the “beauty and strength of democracy”.

Bilawal reiterated, “If we want to reset the system, a political reset has to happen; it should begin from the parliament”.

He noted that the opposition had lost trust in the system.

“They genuinely have reasons to have lost confidence in the working of the Parliament, and we all have to regain this trust,” he said.

“The government cannot expect the opposition to clap along with every one of the government’s decisions,” he remarked.

He claimed that the “easiest way to do corruption in Pakistan was to be on the state’s right side”.

Bilawal said: “When someone from the opposition makes a speech [..] then all of a sudden, you set the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) on them, arrest their sons; there was no such realisation before.

“Now, all of a sudden, there is encroachment (around their house),” he said, in an apparent reference to the Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) recent notice on “unauthorised construction” at the JUI-F chief’s residence.

“This is why the system has collapsed […] you are making it collapse,” he said, calling on the Centre to engage with Fazl.

On governor’s rule in KP, Bilawal noted that PPP had the governor in the province, but stressed his stance that it could not remain forever.

“If you are yourself saying that the majority of them (PTI) were ready but one or two people sabotaged the talks, then what is stopping the government from approaching the opposition again?” he said, recalling remarks by “minister for everything”.

“If the PTI is ready to fight against terrorism together with you, then the governor’s rule can also be ended,” Bilawal said, terming it another way to regain the opposition’s trust.

World.title: Tarar says referendum 'legal and constitutional' method of gauging public opinion on new provinces
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that a referendum was a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces, adding that no political party should have reservations regarding it.

He made the comments in televised remarks following a hard-hitting speech by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The minister said that there was an ongoing debate in the country regarding “good governance”.

“The public wants a good government that is accountable … You and all of us have been part of this system for decades. Today, we cannot separate ourselves from the weaknesses of the system,” he said.

He said that to “enjoy the perks” being in power and also do opposition amounted to having a “double standard”. He said that the reason behind the PPP chairman’s remarks was the ongoing debate regarding provinces.

“And this debate is raging among the masses. Will you silence the people? Will you stop them from talking about improving governance? This debate will happen in Parliament and outside it,” he said.

The minister added that the people could not be stopped from talking about something that was for their benefit.

“Democratic and political processes demand that this debate be done by the people … What is the problem with going to the public? You and I are not going to decide what the people want. They are the ones who will decide,” he said.

“No political party should have reservations in going to the public. When public opinion comes forward … referendum is part of the Constitution. It is a legal and constitutional process. The people are the final decision-makers and good governance is the charter of every political party,” he said.

The minister said that the people appointed public representatives, not the other way round.

“The people are the ultimate decision-makers. If the people of Pakistan and Sindh was more provinces, then make them; otherwise, don’t,” he said. Tarar added that instead of making the issue of smaller administrative units smaller, they should be viewed through the lens of development.

“Will you deprive the people of their rights just because referendums were previously used in a non-democratic manner?” he asked.

“Look, we are part of the same government. Come and sit down [with us] so we can make decision for the betterment of the people and the country. [Let] this decision be based on public opinion. And a referendum is an excellent way of gauging public opinion, so what’s the harm?”

JUI-F backs Bilawal’s stance on referendum

On the other hand, the Jamiat-Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) voiced its support for Bilawal’s opposition to a referendum, warning that it could be misused.

The statement by party spokesperson Aslam Ghauri, posted on social media, termed Bilawal’s statements “realistic” and viewed them in high regard.

In his remarks, the PPP chairman had also expressed support for JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman amid the ongoing tensions between him and the government.

“By exposing the government’s mandate, Bilawal Bhutto has supported the JUI-F’s position,” Ghauri said. Stating that the PPP had made its position on the division of provinces clear, he expressed the JUI-F’s alignment with this position.

“The experience of holding referendums has always been tainted,” Ghauri added. “If the Constitution provides a procedure for resolving an issue, there is no need for a referendum.”

He claimed that referendums, “like emergencies and governor’s rule”, would also be “misused” by invoking the Constitution.

PTI highlights PPP’s shared responsibility

The PTI also expressed agreement with the PPP scion, but questioned why it had taken him so long to recognise the hardships faced by ordinary Pakistanis.

In a statement, the party’s Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said Bilawal had finally realised the difficulties confronting the public, but questioned the sincerity of his remarks. He argued that the PPP was itself part of the ruling arrangement and could not escape responsibility for the country’s deteriorating political and economic situation.

He maintained that the PPP could not enjoy the benefits of being part of the government while simultaneously criticising the very system it helped sustain.

Akram said the PML-N and the PPP shared responsibility for the country’s devastating economic conditions, adding that the latter could not absolve itself of accountability through political statements alone.

He also questioned Bilawal’s role in the passage of the 26th Constitutional Amendment, adding that the PPP chairman had played a leading part in securing its approval. He added that the amendment dealt a serious blow to judicial independence and constitutional supremacy, making the PPP equally accountable for the consequences.

The information secretary further said that retaining the PTI’s reserved parliamentary seats violated democratic principles and showed disregard for the public mandate. He challenged Bilawal to demonstrate his commitment to democracy by ensuring the return of those seats to the PTI, saying that advocating democracy while disregarding the people’s electoral mandate amounted to political hypocrisy.

He warned that political victimisation, coercion and undemocratic practices were deepening the country’s instability instead of addressing its mounting political and economic challenges.

Over the past few months, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Last week, Naqvi also floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and other senior party leaders have repeatedly declared that the division of Sindh was neither legally nor politically acceptable to the party.

In September, the Sindh Assembly adopted a resolution rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units.

President Asif Ali Zardari also met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif over the weekend. Official sources said the two agreed to “strictly adhere to constitutional provisions” governing the creation of new provinces or administrative units, with any proposed referendum on the contentious issue also requiring parliamentary approval.

However, Bilawal on Tuesday termed the referendum an “unconstitutional move”, vowing that his party would stand against any such measure.

World.title: Pakistan fall to India in SAFF final after late heartbreak
World.content:
Pakistan’s hopes of lifting their maiden SAFF Championship title ended in heartbreak on Tuesday as defending champions India came from behind to secure a 2-1 victory in the final at the National Stadium, extending their record to 10 titles and completing an unprecedented hat-trick of consecutive triumphs.

The Shaheens produced an impressive first-half display and looked on course for a historic victory after taking the lead through Alamgir Ghazi in stoppage time.

However, the dismissal of defender Junaid Shah early in the second half proved a turning point, allowing India to seize control and score twice to retain their crown.

Pakistan, appearing in their first-ever SAFF Championship final, began confidently and enjoyed the better of the opening exchanges, putting India’s reshuffled side under sustained pressure.

The Green Shirts threatened repeatedly down the flanks, with the combination of Abdul Samad Arshad and Haris Zeb causing problems for the Indian defence.

India, meanwhile, struggled to establish attacking rhythm, although they came close to scoring around the 35th minute when Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf Butt produced an important save to deny a dangerous effort.

Just when the first half appeared destined to end goalless, Pakistan broke the deadlock in spectacular fashion.

Junaid Shah delivered a cross from the left during first-half stoppage time which took a deflection off an Indian defender before falling to Alamgir inside the penalty area.

The midfielder made no mistake, curling a superb right-footed effort into the far corner to send Pakistan into the interval with a deserved 1-0 advantage.

India returned after the break with greater urgency and immediately began pushing forward in search of an equaliser. Yousuf was called into action in the 51st minute, denying PV Vishnu after the Indian midfielder made his way through the Pakistan defence.

The contest, however, took a dramatic turn in the 60th minute when a Video Assistant Referee (VAR) review resulted in Junaid being shown a straight red card for a reckless challenge on Brison Fernandes.

Reduced to 10 men, Pakistan struggled to contain the defending champions, who wasted little time capitalising on their numerical advantage.

India restored parity almost immediately when a free-kick delivery from Lhungdim Khaiminthang caused problems inside the penalty area. Macarton Nickson got a slight touch before Suhail Ahmad Bhat side-footed the ball into the net to make it 1-1.

The equaliser shifted the momentum firmly in India’s favour as Pakistan were forced to retreat and defend deep. Butt kept his side in contention with another important intervention in the 67th minute, turning away an effort from Vishnu.

Pakistan coach Nolberto Solano responded with substitutions, withdrawing Alamgir as he attempted to reorganise his depleted side. However, India continued to dominate possession and press for a decisive goal.

Their persistence finally paid off in the 88th minute when a corner created confusion inside the Pakistan penalty area. Sandip Mandi found himself unmarked and headed past Yousuf to put India ahead for the first time in the match.

Pakistan threw players forward during the closing stages in a desperate attempt to force an equaliser, but India held firm through five minutes of added time to secure victory.

The defeat was particularly painful for Pakistan, who had reached the final after defeating hosts Bangladesh 1-0 in the semi-final, courtesy of Abdul Samad Arshad’s late winner.

Despite falling short of the title, the Shaheens’ run to their first-ever final marked a significant milestone for the national side.

For India, meanwhile, the victory reinforced their regional dominance, taking their SAFF Championship tally to 10 titles and making them the first team to win three successive editions of the tournament.

World.title: Former KP ministers Jhagra, Bangash among 3 PTI leaders held under MPO despite bail from PHC
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa ministers Taimoor Saleem Jhagra and Kamran Bangash were among three PTI leaders taken into “preventative” custody by police shortly after they were granted interim bail by the high court.

Jhagra, Bangash and PTI’s Peshawar president Irfan Saleem had been granted bail until Nov 17 (today) by an anti-terrorism court (ATC) in the 2023 case pertaining to vandalism and arson at the Radio Pakistan building during the May 9 riots.

Earlier in the day, an ATC denied the three leaders bail that had been extended twice previously, following which they evaded arrest to reach the Peshawar High Court (PHC).

Chief Justice SM Attique Shah, heading the single-member bench, pronounced an order granting the three leaders bail till Nov 23, on the condition of furnishing two sureties of Rs1 million each or depositing cash equivalent to it.

The judge directed them to join the investigation and appear before the investigating officer as and when required.

Following the order, an hours-long standoff unfolded between a huge police force present around PHC and the three petitioners.

Led by Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Operations Farhan Khan, the police aimed to take the PTI leaders into custody, stating that the district administration had issued detention orders under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

The petitioners had taken refuge in the PHC’s barroom, where several members of Insaf Lawyers Forum (ILF) were also accompanying them.

During ensuing developments, the SSP visited them in the barroom to negotiate their surrender.

Finally, at around 6pm, the PTI leaders left the barroom and were taken into custody by the police at the high court’s entrance.

They were detained under the MPO ordinance, SSP Farhan told media persons at the high court.

PHC approached after ATC denies bail

Jhagra, Bangash and Saleem were among those named in the supplementary charge-sheet submitted to the ATC last month, though they had later been allowed pre-arrest bail. Sohail Afridi, the non-functional chief minister, had also been added as an accused in the case.

The court last week initiated proceedings to declare Afridi and activist Mohammad Amir Khan proclaimed offenders. While both of them have reportedly been in preventive custody, the police have claimed that they could not be traced in pursuance of their arrest warrants.

On Tuesday, an ATC presided over by Judge Wali Muhammad Khan decided not to confirm pre-arrest bails of Jhagra, Bangash and Saleem.

The three leaders appeared along with their counsel, while senior lawyer Shabbir Hussain Gigyani represented the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation (PBC).

The petitioners’ lawyers challenged the veracity of video footage on the basis of which they had been nominated in the case, stating that it had not yet been clarified from where those videos were obtained and who had prepared them.

They argued that the petitioners’ mere presence in the said videos was not proof of any crime, nor had they been seen vandalising property. Therefore, they argued that the allegations against them were baseless and pre-arrest bail be confirmed.

Advocate Gigyani opposed the PTI leaders’ bails, arguing that the current PBC’s station director Tufail Ahmed was posted as a programme manager at the time of the incident, while Nadra and Punjab Forensic Science Agency had confirmed the identification of the suspects in the videos, after which police nominated them in the supplementary challan.

He stated that videos of the suspects were still present on social media.

The ATC rejected the PTI leaders’ applications. The situation turned tense when police tried to arrest the three leaders after the order’s pronouncement.

While they briefly caught hold of Bangash and Saleem, ILF members managed to free them from police custody.

Later, police closed all entry and exit routes to the Judicial Complex, upon which lawyers forced their way to the adjoining PHC building, where the three PTI leaders also reached.

In the meantime, SSP Farhan and other senior police officials reached PHC. In view of the situation, additional police force was also deployed at the high court.

At the PHC, a panel of lawyers, including Muhammad Inam Yousafzai, Ali Gohar Durrani, Syed Sikander Hayat Shah and Naseeruddin Shah, appeared for the three PTI leaders.

The lawyers contended that the first information report was registered on May 10, 2023, wherein the suspect-petitioners were not initially nominated by name.

They argued that the petitioners were also not included in the charge sheet submitted by the prosecution, in the light of which around 85 people had been indicted and were now facing trial.

The lawyers said their clients were later implicated in the case by the prosecution on Jun 29, 2026, after a lapse of more than three years, alleging mala fide intent to humiliate and harass them on account of their association with the PTI.

Subsequently, the PTI leaders approached the ATC on Oct 29 seeking concession of interim pre-arrest bail, which was initially granted to them, the lawyers recalled.

They informed the PHC that their applications were rejected by the ATC today and they had been provided copies of the orders so far; therefore, they approached the high court.

World.title: Over 170 major websites hit by attack, including BBC, Ikea and Air France: report
World.content:
Nearly 200 major websites, including those of the BBC, HSBC UAE bank, Air France and Ikea were targeted by a malicious cyber attack seeking to steal financial information and infect Apple devices, specialist media reported on Tuesday.

Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript code into tools hosted by Optimizely, a digital platform used by major companies to customise users’ online experiences, Cyber News reported, with some 178 websites targeted.

“The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, HSBC (UAE), Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock,” security researcher Scott Helme, who first uncovered the hack, wrote on Monday on his blog.

“The attacker’s (crypto) wallets had received about $7,040, all within roughly nine hours on the 16th (of November).”

Most of the malicious code had been removed from affected sites, Helme said in his post.

Optimizely confirmed the incident and said it had identified “a security incident in which an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects”.

It said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the injected code from affected projects, taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorised code from being delivered.

“The vulnerable path is blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers have been contacted directly,” it added on X.

Bid to steal crypto, target iPhone users

The websites were compromised in an effort to steal cryptocurrency and infect iPhones, Helme said.

According to the researcher, the scripts attempted to replace cryptocurrency payment addresses with the attacker’s wallet.

The malicious script also sought to capture payment card details as users entered them, steal cookies and screenshots, and deploy exploit code targeting Apple’s iOS devices, Helme said.

Cybersecurity firm HudsonRock said it had also found evidence that the affected sites had served malicious code to visitors.

Reuters could not immediately determine whether the malicious code had been successfully used in each case or the extent of any resulting compromises.

Salesforce and Ikea said they were investigating the incident linked to Optimizely script changes. Salesforce said it had disabled scripts from the platform as a precaution.

Equifax said it had immediately investigated the issue and stopped using the platform. “We have not identified evidence of any compromise to our systems,” it said.

HSBC said unauthorised scripts were not active on its websites. Apple, Zoom and CNN did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The incident highlights growing risks facing organisations that rely on third-party software embedded in websites.

Cryptocurrency hacks have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis. Last month, a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3bn stolen from the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance.

World.title: Petrol price reduced by Rs3 per litre, diesel remains unchanged
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre, marking the eleventh consecutive decrease in the rate, but left the price of high-speed diesel unchanged.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs325 per litre, while HSD will remain at Rs358 on Nov 18 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: US proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United States Department of Labour has published sweeping proposed changes to the rules governing employment-based green cards, requiring companies to make greater efforts to recruit American workers before sponsoring foreign employees for permanent residency.

The proposed overhaul would extend recruitment periods, restrict sponsorship by companies that have recently laid off US workers and eliminate special exemptions currently available to certain healthcare professionals.

Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling said existing rules had allowed companies to sponsor foreign workers “without fully considering American applicants”, a practice the department seeks to address through “expanded recruitment and enforcement requirements”.

The proposals would affect employers seeking to sponsor foreign nationals through the EB-2 and EB-3 employment-based green card categories under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme.

Under the existing system, employers must demonstrate that qualified American workers are unavailable for a particular position and that hiring a foreign worker would not adversely affect domestic wages or working conditions.

The proposed rules would increase the minimum recruitment period from 30 to 90 calendar days. Employers that normally advertise comparable vacancies for longer periods would be required to follow their established recruitment schedules.

Companies would also have to expand their use of digital recruitment platforms, including online job boards, corporate websites and social media. Job s would be required to disclose offered wages or salary ranges, while employers would have to demonstrate that American applicants received fair consideration.

Employers would face stricter documentation requirements as well. They would have to submit recruitment reports, supporting records and the resumes of American applicants along with their labour certification applications. Under current regulations, much of this material is generally retained by employers and produced if an application is selected for a federal audit.

Another significant provision would restrict companies that have laid off American workers in the same or similar occupations within the same geographical area during the preceding two years from obtaining labour certification for those positions.

Existing regulations generally require employers to notify and consider potentially qualified American workers laid off within the previous six months. The proposed changes would extend the period during which such layoffs could affect sponsorship decisions.

The restrictions would also cover certain layoffs involving third-party staffing companies. Employers would have to report subsequent workforce reductions and continue considering qualified displaced American workers during the related immigration petition process.

Healthcare employers could face additional difficulties under the proposed overhaul.

The department plans to eliminate Schedule A, a provision that currently allows employers to sponsor professional nurses, physical therapists and certain individuals with exceptional abilities in the sciences or arts without completing the standard labour market recruitment process.

Removing the exemption would require hospitals and other healthcare facilities to advertise vacancies, consider qualified American applicants and obtain labour certification before proceeding with immigration petitions for foreign professionals.

The change could particularly affect healthcare institutions that rely on internationally recruited nurses and physical therapists.

The proposals would constitute the first comprehensive overhaul of PERM regulations in nearly two decades.

World.title: Jensen Huang says willing to return as Nvidia CEO, 'owns mistakes'
World.content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on Tuesday that he would be willing to return to the post due to an “outpouring of calls” for his reinstatement after he quit last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang said in a statement he posted on X.

It was Huang’s first public statement since he resigned on Thursday following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with an executive of a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

The turmoil has battered shares in Nvidia, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company.

Tech tycoon Elon Musk and other major AI investors have been calling for Huang’s reinstatement with an open letter that has garnered more than 190,000 signatures.

US President Donald Trump also signalled on Monday his support for the return of Huang, who has advised him on AI policy and is perhaps the tech industry’s most recognised promoter of artificial intelligence.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in the statement.

He sounded a note of contrition.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” he said.

“I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.”

US lawmakers said Tuesday that Huang will appear before three US House committees on Dec 1 for questioning over concerns that China was able to gain access to advanced US chips from Nvidia.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry.
